# Documentation index
Ownership splits in two: pages this repository writes, and pages synced verbatim from the family's public repositories.

Owned pages
- [Family](family.md): the agent family, and where this hub stands.
- [Engineering law](engineering-law.md): the discipline every public repository keeps.
- [Sync contract](sync.md): how sources arrive, on what schedule, with what provenance.
- [Site integration](site-integration.md): the specified handoff to vidoxlabs.dev.
- [Timeline guide](timeline/README.md): how to use the development timeline, read order, and continual integration workflow.
- [Roadmap](timeline/roadmap.md): milestones `M0` to `M9`, horizons, Bloom CLI phase mapping, and pending owner rulings.
- [Capability catalog](timeline/capabilities.json): machine-readable registry of `CAP-01` through `CAP-19`.
- [Capability ledger](timeline/ledger.md): status and claim table for all family capabilities.

- [Hub capabilities](capabilities/README.md): hub capability index ([index.json](capabilities/index.json)), [CAP-01](capabilities/CAP-01-development-timeline-ledger.md), and [CAP-02](capabilities/CAP-02-docs-freshness-check.md).

Synced sources

# Architecture Decision Records
This folder defines the Architecture Decision Record (ADR) convention for the `docs` hub and every peer repository in the Vidoxlabs family.

Naming and numbering
- Each repository keeps its own `docs/adr/` directory with its own `README.md` pointing to this hub convention.
- Files are named `NNNN-<slug>.md` using a four-digit zero-padded number starting at `0001` per repository (`0001-<slug>.md`, `0002-<slug>.md`, and so on).

Status lifecycle
Every ADR carries one of four statuses:

- `Proposed`: Drafted by an agent or contributor for review.
- `Accepted`: Ratified by an owner answer recorded under the [Owner questions](../timeline/agent-guide.md#owner-questions) process.
- `Superseded by NNNN`: Replaced by a newer accepted ADR in the same repository.
- `Deferred`: Parked by owner decision without adoption.

Governance rules
- **Agents propose ADRs**: Only an owner answer recorded under the [Owner questions](../timeline/agent-guide.md#owner-questions) process moves an ADR to `Accepted`, `Superseded`, or `Deferred`.
- **Dependencies require an ADR first**: Per [engineering-law.md](../engineering-law.md), repositories keep zero runtime dependencies (`bloom` pins only `seed`). Any proposal to introduce a dependency must open and win owner acceptance as an ADR before any dependency enters `package.json`.
- **Format**: Follow [template.md](template.md) with plain Markdown headings and zero YAML frontmatter.

# NNNN: Architecture decision title
Status: `Proposed`
Date: `YYYY-MM-DD`
Capability: `CAP-NN` (or `none`)

Context
State the technical problem, constraints, and family rules motivating a decision.

Decision
State the proposed architectural choice clearly and concisely.

Consequences
List positive outcomes, maintenance costs, compatibility effects, and migration requirements.

Alternatives
Summarize the other options considered and why they were not selected.

Links
Link related capability specs, contracts, proposals, or owner decision anchors (`D-YYYYMMDD-NN`).

Plans, verdicts, and the assembly gate # aestivation Plan proposal, deterministic validation, review verdicts, and the assembly gate. Aestivation is the admission and review member of the bloom agent family. Before work opens, it happens here: a plan is proposed, a deterministic rule pack validates it, reviewers record approve or revise verdicts, and a gate holds automatic assembly until the plan is both valid and approved. A revision verdict stops assembly; the reasons say what to change; the next plan is a new proposal.

Status
Version 0.5.0. The plan rule pack, verdict ledger, and assembly gate are `implemented` as a tested reference library. A durable ledger, live reviewers, and service interfaces remain `specified` or `planned`.

Install
```bash
npm install @vidoxlabs/aestivation
```

Requires Node >= 22.13. Zero runtime dependencies.

Modules
| Module | What it holds | Label |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `plan.mjs` | Plan proposals: objective plus ordered steps, the SHA-256 digest of each proposal's content, and the deterministic rule pack that validates stages, titles, and order. | `implemented` |
| `verdict.mjs` | Verdict records (approve or revise) that may name the plan digest they reviewed, the append-only ledger, and the soundness check over every record. | `implemented` |
| `intent.mjs` | Read-only intent assessments that name missing sources and ground personal recall in admitted memory references. Tool and memory-write lists stay under caller admission. | `implemented` |
| `correction.mjs` | Corrections within existing scope after an exact-digest revise verdict, with new frozen proposals, a two-replan limit per in-process lineage, and a check that refuses superseded results. The judge cannot apply the patch. | `implemented` |
| `gate.mjs` | The assembly gate: one function that checks the ledger, holds a review of a different plan version as stale, and composes validation and verdicts into permitted or held, with the reason. | `implemented` |

The name
Aestivation is the arrangement of petals in a bud before it opens. That is the entire doctrine: the work of arranging before the opening. Nothing assembles until the arrangement has been validated and reviewed. When it opens, it opens because the gate said so for stated reasons.

The rule pack
The baseline deterministic rules a plan must pass:

1. A plan has at least one step.
2. Every step names a known stage: `research`, `work`, `review`, `assemble`, or `verify`.
3. Every step has a non-empty title.
4. When review and assemble are both present, review precedes the first assemble.
5. When verify is present, it is the final step.

The same plan validates the same way every time, and no review can wave it through. The split runs both ways: no rule pack approves a plan on a reviewer's behalf. Judgment and rules are separate lanes; the gate composes them.

The family
The family follows one design law: ordinary botanical words for public products.

| Name | Province |
| :--- | :--- |
| [`seed`](https://github.com/Vidoxlabs/seed) | Harness foundation: runs, tools, providers |
| [`capillary`](https://github.com/Vidoxlabs/capillary) | Context retrieval and relations, provenance-first |
| [`myosotis`](https://github.com/Vidoxlabs/myosotis) | Memory with consent and structural forget |
| `aestivation` (this repo) | Plans, verdicts, and the gate before assembly |
| [`drosera`](https://github.com/Vidoxlabs/drosera) | Tool faces, skills, hooks, cookbooks |
| [`trellis`](https://github.com/Vidoxlabs/trellis) | Multi-point testing with dated evidence |
| [`bloom`](https://github.com/Vidoxlabs/bloom) | The team workspace harness |
| [`docs`](https://github.com/Vidoxlabs/docs) | Family documentation, synced from every public repository |

Documentation
- `AGENTS.md`: start here before editing. Stay in this repository's province.
- `docs/charter.md`: mission, principles, non-goals.
- `docs/architecture.md`: the bud and its four whorls.
- `docs/contracts/`: the plan, verdict, and gate contracts.
- `docs/interop.md`: how bloom runs the loop, and how seed carries its effects.

Development
```bash
npm test
```

Tests use the Node built-in runner. Adding a rule means adding the test that holds it.

# Architecture Decision Records
Architecture Decision Records (ADRs) for `aestivation` live in this directory, numbered sequentially from `0001` (`NNNN-<slug>.md`).

- Format, lifecycle (`Proposed`, `Accepted`, `Superseded by NNNN`, `Deferred`), and review rules follow the hub ADR convention in [Vidoxlabs/docs](https://github.com/Vidoxlabs/docs/blob/main/docs/adr/README.md).
- Agents write `Proposed` ADRs; only an explicit owner decision moves an ADR to `Accepted`.
- Any runtime dependency proposal requires an ADR before adding a package.
- Record every added or updated ADR in `docs/capabilities/index.json` in the same pull request.

# Aestivation architecture
Four whorls, one gate.

```
            ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────┐
            │                  the bud                     │
            │                                              │
 proposal ──►│  rule pack ──► verdict ledger ──► the gate  │──► assembly permitted
   {objective,                                 held?        (or held, with reason)
    steps[]}    deterministic   judgment,        reason:
                yes/no          with reasons     plan-invalid
                                                 ledger-unsound
                                                 awaiting-verdict
                                                 review-stale
                                                 revisions-requested
            └─────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

The proposal
A plan is an objective plus ordered steps. Each step names a stage from a closed set — `research`, `work`, `review`, `assemble`, `verify` — and carries a title. The proposal is the unit of review: reviewers read it whole, and a revised plan is a new proposal, not an edit of the old one in place. Each proposal carries the SHA-256 digest of its content, so a verdict can name exactly which version it reviewed.

The verdict ledger
Review is recorded, not remembered. Each verdict names its plan, carries a decision from `{approve, revise}`, names the judge, and — when the decision is revise — carries at least one reason. The ledger is append-only: soundness means every verdict references a known plan and every record is well-formed. The latest verdict for a plan is the one that counts; history stays underneath it.

The gate
One composition, one answer. Given a validation result and a ledger, the gate answers: is automatic assembly of this plan permitted? Held reasons, in order:

1. `plan-invalid` — the rule pack rejected it. Deterministic outranks judgment; an approval cannot rescue an invalid plan.
2. `ledger-unsound` — the ledger holds a malformed record, or, when known plans are given, a reference to an unknown plan. Judgment counts only from a ledger the gate can trust.
3. `awaiting-verdict` — no verdict exists for the plan. Unreviewed plans do not self-assemble.
4. `review-stale` — given the plan's digest, the latest verdict reviewed a different version or named none. The proposal reviewed is the proposal assembled.
5. `revisions-requested` — the latest verdict is revise. The reasons say what to change; the plan comes back as a new proposal.

Permitted means one thing: valid plan, approved by the latest verdict. Not good, not owner-ratified, not deployed — permitted to assemble, with the ledger showing exactly why.

What this edition is
`src/` implements the four parts as pure functions over plain data: the rule pack, verdict construction and ledger soundness, and the gate. No I/O, no persistence, no concurrency. A durable ledger behind this state machine is `specified` in the contracts; the mapping onto any particular store is deliberately out of scope here.

# CAP-07: Plan review and approval loop
- ID: `CAP-07`
- Title: Plan review and approval loop
- Lead: `aestivation`
- Touches: `seed`, `bloom`
- Horizon: `next`
- Milestone: `M3`
- CLI phase: `P3`
- Status: `proposed`
- Claim: `planned`
- Depends on: `CAP-06.1`

Why
Multi-step workspace runs need an explicit, deterministic plan-review and owner-approval loop so plans carry role-bound steps, hold when a clarifying question is open, enforce a strict step status machine, bound revisions per run, and never mistake a reviewer verdict or model belief for owner ratification.

What it does
- **Plan payload extensions (`CAP-07.1`)**: a plan proposal carries `request` (the task request), `seats` (role IDs only from the closed set `chair`, `framing`, `risk`, `coherence`, `sequencing`), `knownFacts` (explicit grounded facts), `steps` (each carrying a seat role ID from that closed set, a stage, a title, and an `action`), `summary`, and an optional `clarifyingQuestion`. When `clarifyingQuestion` is present, the plan is held until the owner answers; no execution step advances while held.
- **Step status machine (`CAP-07.1`)**: every plan step holds a status in the closed set `{ planned, awaiting-review, approved, rejected, running, done, failed, cancelled }`. Transitions follow the full deterministic table below; every transition absent from the table (including skipping review, reversing direction, or leaving terminal statuses `rejected`, `done`, `failed`, `cancelled`) is illegal and refused.

| From status | Allowed next statuses | Meaning |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `planned` | `awaiting-review`, `cancelled` | Submitted for review or cancelled before review |
| `awaiting-review` | `approved`, `rejected`, `cancelled` | Review outcome recorded or cancelled while awaiting review |
| `approved` | `running`, `cancelled` | Execution begins after assembly gate and owner approval, or cancelled |
| `rejected` | (none, terminal) | Rejected step ends; revision opens a new proposal version |
| `running` | `done`, `failed`, `cancelled` | Step finishes, fails, or is

Contract touchpoints
- `aestivation/docs/contracts/plan.md`: plan payload fields (`request`, `seats`, `knownFacts`, `steps` with seat role ID and `action`, `summary`, optional `clarifyingQuestion`), step status machine, and per-run revision cap (`CAP-07.1`, `CAP-07.2`).
- `aestivation/docs/contracts/verdict.md`: `approve` and `revise` verdict records with mandatory reasons on `revise` and append-only ledger soundness checks.
- `aestivation/docs/contracts/gate.md`: `assemblyGate` precedence (`plan-invalid`, `ledger-unsound`, `awaiting-verdict`, `review-stale`, `revisions-requested`) and non-ratification guarantee.
- `seed/docs/contracts/run-model.md`: `seed` owner-gate decision record binding to `planDigest` (`CAP-06.1` at `M3`).
- `bloom/docs/architecture.md`: loop wiring and emission of `plan.*` events (`CAP-07.4`).

Tool IDs and events
### Tool IDs

No new tool IDs are introduced by `CAP-07`.

| Tool ID | Effect class | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |

### Events

| Event | Emitted by | Payload summary |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `plan.proposed` | `bloom` | `planId`, `planDigest`, `request`, `seats` (role IDs), `steps`, `summary`, optional `clarifyingQuestion` |
| `plan.verdict` | `bloom` | `planId`, `planDigest`, `decision` (`approve` or `revise`), `judge` role ID, `reasons` |
| `plan.gate` | `bloom` | `planId`, `planDigest`, `permitted`, `held` reason (if held), ledger soundness status |
| `plan.decision` | `bloom` | `seed` owner-gate decision (`approve`, `edit`, `reject`, `respond`) bound to `planDigest` |

Acceptance tests
- `step-status-legal-transitions`: every legal transition in the eight-status table succeeds and returns a frozen step record.
- `step-status-illegal-moves-refused`: every illegal move not listed in the transition table (across all 8 x 8 pairs plus unknown statuses, including `planned` to `running`, `planned` to `approved`, and any exit from terminal states `rejected`, `done`, `failed`, `cancelled`) is explicitly tested and refused.
- `clarifying-question-holds-plan`: a plan containing `clarifyingQuestion` holds execution until the owner answers.
- `unsound-ledger-closes-assembly-gate`: a malformed verdict or unknown plan reference causes `assemblyGate` to hold with `ledger-unsound` and `verdict: null`.
- `review-verdict-and-memory-never-ratify`: a reviewer `approve` verdict, model belief, or memory entry never counts as owner approval; execution remains blocked until a `seed` owner-gate record (`CAP-06.1`) bound to `planDigest` records owner acceptance or edit.
- `owner-edit-updates-plan-digest`: an owner edit yields a new `planDigest`, invalidating any earlier verdict or decision for the superseded digest.
- `revision-cap-holds-with-stated-reason`: reaching the per-run revision cap refuses further revision attempts and holds the plan with a stated reason.

Slices
- `CAP-07.1` (`aestivation`, `M3`, `proposed`): Plan payload extensions, clarifying question hold, and step status machine.
- `CAP-07.2` (`aestivation`, `M3`, `proposed`): Revision cap and separation of review verdict from owner approval.
- `CAP-07.4` (`bloom`, `M3`, `proposed`): Plan review loop wiring and plan events (`plan.proposed`, `plan.verdict`, `plan.gate`, `plan.decision`).

Non-goals
- Executing or scheduling plan steps inside `aestivation` (execution belongs to `bloom` and `seed`).
- Letting `aestivation`, a model reviewer, or memory ratify a plan on the owner's behalf.
- Defining seat instruction files or character personas (seats use closed role IDs only).
- Adding persistence or I/O inside `aestivation` (durable storage belongs to `CAP-13`).

Family rules and conflicts
- Role IDs only: `seats` and step assignments use only `chair`, `framing`, `risk`, `coherence`, and `sequencing`, never persona names.
- Deterministic checks outrank reviewer judgment: `assemblyGate` rejects invalid plans and unsound ledgers regardless of any `approve` verdict.
- `aestivation` remains a zero-dependency pure reference library with no I/O, no model calls, and no peer imports.

Open owner decisions
- **D14 (pending owner decision)**: Under the review sequencing convention, `CAP-06.1` (`seed` owner-gate record binding to `planDigest`) lands at `M3` with `CAP-07.3` folded into `CAP-06.1` (`CAP-07.4` preserved without renumbering), and `CAP-07` depends on `CAP-06.1` at `M3` ahead of `CAP-06.2` through `CAP-06.4` at `M4`.
- Per-run revision cap default and owner plan-gate threshold (pending owner decision, not yet numbered): confirm the default per-run revision cap and whether owner plan approval gates every multi-step plan or only plans exceeding declared effect thresholds.

Evidence
- Status `planned`: Phase 0 specification created. Baseline plan validation, verdict ledger soundness, `assemblyGate`, read-only intent assessment, and bounded two-replan corrections are implemented and verified by `npm test` in `aestivation` (`0.5.0`); `CAP-07.1` and `CAP-07.2` extensions remain to be implemented.

Changes
- `2026-11-23`: Initial Phase 0 specification (`CAP-01`).
- `2026-11-23`: Folded `CAP-07.3` into `CAP-06.1` and updated dependency to `CAP-06.1` (`D14`).
- `2026-11-23`: Removed `D12` attribution from the unnumbered revision-cap and owner plan-gate threshold open question and formatted capability IDs in Changes (`CAP-01.5`).

# Changelog

Unreleased
### Added

- Capability ledger scaffold (`docs/capabilities/index.json`), capability guide, `CAP-07` plan review and approval loop specification, ADR index (`docs/adr/README.md`), and changelog convention (CAP-01, aestivation#1).
# Aestivation charter

Mission
Build the loop that decides, before work opens, whether the work may open. Aestivation holds the contracts for planning: propose, validate deterministically, review with reasons, and hold assembly at a gate. The loop's judgments are recorded, its rules are plain, and nothing automatic assembles until the plan has passed both lanes.

The name is the doctrine. Aestivation is the arrangement of petals in the bud before it opens. Petals that never arrange do not open well; work that never gets planned does not assemble well. Everything here happens before the opening — and the opening itself is a gated, stated event.

Principles
1. **Deterministic first, judgment second.** The rule pack runs on every plan, the same way every time. An invalid plan is held no matter who approved it. Rules and review are separate lanes; the gate composes them, and neither can substitute for the other.
2. **Verdicts carry their reasons.** A revise verdict always states what to change. An approve verdict may carry reasons too — an approval with no explanation is weaker than one with its basis on its face, but it is a valid verdict.
3. **The ledger is append-only.** A verdict is a record of a moment in review. It is never edited. Re-review after revision is a new verdict appended to the plan's history.
4. **Revise stops assembly.** When a plan's latest verdict is revise, the gate holds. Automatic assembly does not proceed on a maybe.
5. **The loop never ratifies for the owner.** A verdict records review; a gate opening permits assembly. Neither is the owner's assent. Effects that exceed the plan's scope — publishing, deploying, deleting, spending — are gated effects, and they route the owner's gate in the harness, not the reviewer's pen.
6. **Held states say why.** A gate that holds names the reason: plan-invalid, ledger-unsound, awaiting-verdict, review-stale, revisions-requested. "No" without a reason teaches nothing.

Non-goals
- **Not a scheduler.** Aestivation does not run the steps. The harness runs work; this loop decides whether the arrangement admits it.
- **Not a judge of quality.** The rule pack checks shape and order. Reviewers judge content. Neither claims to measure whether the work is good, and the gate certifies neither.
- **Not an approval substitute.** The loop's outputs are records and a gate state. Ratification — the owner's act of accepting the outcome — happens outside this loop, always.

# Contract: the assembly gate
Label: `specified` (rules), `implemented` (in `src/gate.mjs`).

Shape
```
assemblyGate({ validation, verdicts, planId, planDigest?, knownPlanIds? }) → { permitted, held, validation, ledger, verdict }
```

The gate's one question
Is automatic assembly of this plan permitted? The answer is composed from the validation and the verdict ledger, in a fixed order:

| Order | Condition | Held reason |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 1 | `validation.ok === false` | `plan-invalid` |
| 2 | the verdict ledger is unsound | `ledger-unsound` |
| 3 | no verdict exists for the plan | `awaiting-verdict` |
| 4 | a `planDigest` was given and the latest verdict names a different one, or none | `review-stale` |
| 5 | latest verdict is `revise` | `revisions-requested` |
| — | none of the above: valid plan, sound ledger, latest verdict `approve` (of this exact version, when a digest was given) | (permitted) |

The held reasons are closed and exported in this order as `HELD_REASONS`.

Why the order is the order
1. **Deterministic outranks judgment.** An invalid plan is held even when a reviewer approved. The rule pack's rejection cannot be overruled by a pen, and this ordering is what makes that principle structural rather than aspirational.
2. **Judgment counts only from a ledger the gate can trust.** The gate checks the whole ledger with the verdict contract's soundness rules before it reads any verdict. One malformed record anywhere, such as an approval with no judge or a revise with no reason, makes the ledger unsound and holds the gate. When `knownPlanIds` is given, a verdict naming an unknown plan, or a gated `planId` that is not itself known, is also unsound. Without `knownPlanIds` the gate checks record well-formedness only.
3. **Unreviewed never self-assembles.** A valid plan with no verdict waits. Silence is not approval and absence is not consent.
4. **A review covers the version it read.** Given the plan's `planDigest`, the gate holds as `review-stale` when the latest verdict for the plan names a different digest or none. A step added, removed, or retitled after review changes the digest, so the old approval no longer opens the gate. The latest verdict still counts: a later review of another version leaves this version stale rather than reaching back to an older approval. Without `planDigest` the gate does not check versions and answers as before.
5. **Revise is a stop, not a pause of opinion.** The latest revise verdict holds assembly until a

Output semantics
- `permitted: true` means the two lanes passed over a sound ledger: valid, approved. Nothing more.
- `permitted: false` always carries a `held` reason from the table above. There is no naked refusal.
- The gate returns the validation, the ledger soundness result (`{ ok, errors }`), and the latest verdict alongside its answer, so a caller never re-derives what the gate already judged.
- When the ledger is unsound, `verdict` is `null`: a verdict from an untrusted ledger is never surfaced as the answer.

Prohibitions
- The gate never ratifies. Permission to assemble is not owner assent; effects exceeding the plan's scope route the owner's gate in the harness.
- The gate never judges content. If the rule pack and the reviewers both passed it, the gate opens whether or not a third party would have preferred different work.
- The gate never mutates its inputs. It composes; it does not rewrite the ledger or re-validate with different rules.

Changes
- `0.2.0` — the gate checks ledger soundness, adding held reason `ledger-unsound` (order 2), the optional `knownPlanIds` input, the `ledger` output, and `HELD_REASONS`. Before `0.2.0` the verdict contract said an unsound ledger is refused by the gate, but the gate read verdicts unchecked, so a hand-built approval with no judge could permit assembly. Gate answers over ledgers built with `verdictRecord` are unchanged. A caller that matches on `held` values should handle the new reason.
- `0.3.0` — the optional `planDigest` input and held reason `review-stale` (order 4). A malformed `planDigest` is refused with an error. Without `planDigest`, answers are unchanged. A caller that matches on `held` values should handle the new reason.

# Contract: plan
Label: `specified` (shape), `implemented` (rule pack in `src/plan.mjs`).

The closed set of stages
| Stage | Meaning |
| :--- | :--- |
| `research` | Gathering evidence and reading context. |
| `work` | Making changes, producing artifacts. |
| `review` | Judgment on the proposal's outputs, recorded as verdicts. |
| `assemble` | Automatic assembly of the plan's outputs. |
| `verify` | Deterministic verification of the assembled result. |

Baseline rule pack
1. **Non-empty.** A plan with zero steps is not a plan.
2. **Known stages.** A step naming an unknown stage is rejected, not guessed.
3. **Titled.** A step without a title is rejected.
4. **Review precedes assemble.** When both are present, the first `review` step comes before the first `assemble` step. Assembly without review before it is the failure mode this loop exists to prevent.
5. **Verify is final.** When a `verify` step is present, it is the last step. Deterministic verification comes after assembly, before anything opens.

All five are shape and order rules. None of them judges content.

Validation output
```
{ ok: boolean, errors: string[] }   — errors carries every violated rule, not the first
```

A validation result is data. The gate consumes it; a caller may not string-match a validation's prose, because prose changes and rules stay.

The plan digest
`implemented` in `src/plan.mjs`. `planDigest(proposal)` is the SHA-256, in 64 lowercase hex, of the proposal's content as canonical JSON: `{ id, objective, steps }`, every step with all of its fields, object keys sorted, undefined members dropped, no whitespace. `planProposal` stores it as `digest`. Key order does not change the digest; any change to the id, the objective, a step's fields, or the step list does. A verdict names this digest to say which version of the plan it reviewed (see the verdict contract), and that is how "the proposal reviewed is the proposal assembled" is checked.

Intent assessment
`implemented` in `src/intent.mjs`. An intent assessment is advice about a request:
`{ label, needs, confidence, authority: 'advisory', evidencePolicy }`, frozen. `needs` lists evidence
needs from `project-knowledge`, `live-state`, `durable-memory`, and `none`.

1. **It grants nothing.** An input carrying `tools`, `allowedTools`, `memoryWrites`,
   `grants`, `scopes`, or `actions` is refused.
2. **It is read-only.** `admitWithIntent(admission, assessment)` returns the admission's
   `allowedTools` and `memoryWrites`, copied and frozen, unchanged. The input is not
   mutated. A `durable-memory` need sets `memoryRecallAdvised`: advice to read, never a
   write.
3. **Only a real record composes.** A look-alike object, or a copy of a record, is
   refused, so a forged assessment cannot add a tool.
4. **Missing evidence is named.** `evidencePolicy.missingSource` is `state-unavailable`.
   The caller can supply `availableSources` with evidence types it verified. Composition
   returns a frozen `evidence` record with `missingSources` and a `statement` naming
   each gap. The statement is `null` when all required evidence is available.
5. **Personal recall uses admitted memory.** `evidencePolicy.personalRecall` is
   `admitted-memory-only`. A `durable-memory` need is met only by nonempty
   `admission.admittedMemory`, a list of references already admitted by the caller.
   The evidence record copies those references for a recall need. Conversation history,
   an asse

Corrections
`implemented` in `src/correction.mjs`. `correctPlan({ previous, verdict, author,
objective?, steps? })` answers a revise verdict:

1. The verdict must be a `revise` of `previous.id` at `previous.digest`. An approval is
   refused with `correction-not-needed`; a review of another version, or of no named
   version, with `review-mismatch`.
2. The previous proposal is not edited. The correction is a new frozen proposal with the
   same id and a new digest, and a record `{ planId, previousDigest, digest, reviewedBy,
   author, reasons }`. A correction that leaves the digest unchanged is refused with
   `correction-unchanged`.
3. The judge who asked for the revision cannot apply it: an `author` equal to the
   verdict's judge, or no author, is refused with `reviewer-cannot-apply`.
4. An approval of the previous digest does not open the gate for the correction. The
   gate holds it as `review-stale` until the new digest is reviewed.
5. Each parent proposal can spend two successful replans in its in-process lineage.
   `correctPlan` retires the old digest when it returns the next proposal. A correction
   from a retired proposal or back to a retired digest is refused with `order-superseded`.
   The third replan is refused with `replan-exhausted`. Refusals spend no replan.
6. Before consuming a result, call `assertCurrentPlanResult(proposal, { planId,
   planDigest })` with the proposal instance held by the run. The check refuses retired
   digests with `order-superseded`

Prohibitions
- No silent step injection. The proposal reviewed is the proposal assembled; steps appearing after review are a new proposal.
- No stage migration inside a plan object. A plan is frozen on creation.
- No rule pack may approve on a reviewer's behalf, and no reviewer verdict may waive a rule.

Changes
- `0.5.0` — `correctPlan` accepts optional scope fields and refuses requested
  expansion. `ScopeExpansionError` extends `CorrectionError`. Calls within the
  existing scope keep the original correction contract.

- `0.4.0` — intent assessments and corrections are new. Additive: no existing export
  changed.

- `0.3.0` — `planDigest` and the proposal's `digest` field are new. Additive: validation and proposal construction are otherwise unchanged.

# Contract: verdict
Label: `specified` (rules), `implemented` (ledger in `src/verdict.mjs`).

Shape
```
verdict { planId, planDigest, decision, judge, reasons[] }
decision  one of: approve, revise
```

Rules
1. **A verdict names its plan.** `planId` is required and must reference a known proposal. The ledger's soundness check rejects dangling references.
2. **A verdict may name the version it reviewed.** `planDigest` is the 64-hex `planDigest` of the proposal the judge read, or `null` when not given. A malformed digest makes the record invalid. When the gate is given a plan digest, a verdict counts only for the version it names (see the gate contract).
3. **A verdict names its judge.** A review without a reviewer is not a review. `judge` is a non-empty string; who judges is the ledger's provenance.
4. **Revise carries reasons.** A `revise` decision without at least one reason is rejected. A reviewer who wants changes says what changes.
5. **Approve may carry reasons.** An approval is valid with an empty reasons list, though an approval that states its basis is the better record.
6. **The ledger is append-only.** Verdicts are frozen on creation. Correction happens by appending, never by editing history.
7. **The latest verdict counts.** A plan may be reviewed many times across revisions; the verdict in force is the last one recorded for it.

Ledger soundness
```
isSoundVerdictLedger(verdicts, knownPlanIds) → { ok, errors[] }
```

A ledger is sound when it is a list, every verdict is a well-formed record by rules 1 through 4 (the same checks `verdictRecord` applies), and every `planId` references a known plan. Errors carry the verdict's index. An unsound ledger is refused by the gate with held reason `ledger-unsound` — the gate does not grade verdicts it cannot trust.

`implemented` in `src/verdict.mjs` and `src/gate.mjs` as of `0.2.0`; before it, soundness checked only plan references and the gate did not check it at all.

Changes
- `0.3.0` — the optional `planDigest` field; every verdict record now carries it (`null` when not given). Additive: verdicts without it are well-formed as before.

Prohibitions
- No verdict speaks for the owner. A verdict records review; ratification is a separate act by a separate authority, always outside this loop.
- No backdating. The ledger records in order; the order is the record.
- No editing verdicts into approval. The path from revise to permitted is a new plan and a new verdict, on the record.

# Aestivation interop
How aestivation meets the family. Every behavior attributed to a peer below is sourced from that peer's published repository at the time of writing; where a peer has not shipped the behavior, it is not claimed.

bloom: the proved shape
Bloom describes the plan-and-review loop as the interplay of its planner, validators, and review specialists:

> The head proposes an ordered plan... A deterministic rule validates the response and the stage order. A reviewer records approve or revise. A revision verdict stops automatic assembly... A review verdict of "revise" pauses assembly... address the author with the requested changes and attach the review when continuing.

Mapping onto aestivation's contracts:

| Bloom behavior | Aestivation contract |
| :--- | :--- |
| The head proposes an ordered plan | `planProposal`: objective plus frozen, ordered steps. |
| A deterministic rule validates response and stage order | The rule pack: `validatePlan` with the baseline five rules. |
| A reviewer records approve or revise | `verdictRecord`: decision from `{approve, revise}`, judge, reasons. |
| A revision verdict stops automatic assembly | `assemblyGate` held reason `revisions-requested`. |
| Review "revise" pauses, author re-proposes with changes attached | Append-only ledger: the revise verdict stays; the revised plan is a new proposal; the latest verdict counts. |
| "Review approved" / "Changes requested" strings | `decision: 'approve'` / `decision: 'revise'` as data, not prose. |

The one deliberate difference: bloom's review specialists emit strings into a message stream; aestivation holds the same loop as typed records a harness can compose deterministically.

seed: carrying the effects
Aestivation has no tool domain of its own on seed's registry. It is not a connector; it is the loop code the harness runs. Three integrations, all in-process:

1. **Plan validation is a deterministic check.** In bloom the rule is stated as a validator the harness runs without model agency; on seed's run model the same rule runs as verification code the harness executes — the plan enters a `verify`-class checkpoint as data, and the rule pack's output is read as data.
2. **Verdict recording is work product.** A review specialist's judgment lands in the ledger through ordinary harness messages; the verdict record is constructed from the decision, the judge, and the reasons, and it is `data`, not an effect.
3. **Gated effects route the owner gate.** When assembly, publishing, or any scope-exceeding effect follows from a permitted gate, that effect is a gated effect on the harness, with the owner's assent required — permission to assemble is the loop's verdict, ratification is the owner's act, and the loop never confuses the two.

Nothing in this section requires myosotis: verdicts and plans are loop records, not memory. If a harness chooses to remember a review, that act crosses into myosotis under its own contracts.

capillary: evidence into review
Review reads evidence. When a reviewer's reasons cite material, the retrieval of that material is capillary's province — packets with provenance, budgets, and bounded reads. Aestivation consumes none of it directly; the harness hands the reviewer what capillary retrieved, and the verdict records what the reviewer said. The boundary stays clean: capillary proves where evidence came from, aestivation records what was judged and gates what follows.

Family
The family law and the full table live in the [capillary repository's family doc](https://github.com/Vidoxlabs/capillary/blob/main/docs/family.md). Short form: seed for the harness foundation, capillary for retrieval, myosotis for memory, aestivation for admission and review, bloom for the harness. Names are ordinary botanical words; provinces stay distinct.

- Status: Accepted

and review. Each peer ships without runtime dependencies.

commit SHAs and record pending upstream merges. Reconcile each pin to the merged
upstream commit on the next touch after merge.

# Architecture decision records
Architecture decision records for Bloom live in this directory and follow the [hub ADR convention](https://github.com/Vidoxlabs/docs/blob/main/docs/adr/README.md) and [ADR template](https://github.com/Vidoxlabs/docs/blob/main/docs/adr/template.md).

ADRs are named `NNNN-<slug>.md` and numbered sequentially starting from `0001`. Agents author ADRs with status `Proposed`; only an owner decision moves an ADR to `Accepted`.

The planned `docs/adr/0001-terminal-renderer.md` (covering terminal rendering without a third-party TUI library, open under decision `D12` in [CAP-10](../capabilities/CAP-10-trace-observability.md)) keeps number `0001`.

# How Bloom works
Bloom runs as one Node.js webserver with an embedded SQLite database, a directory of Markdown artifacts and a browser client. One head owns a team conversation. Every group post names its author. Durable sequence numbers let a disconnected browser replay activity. A model adapter supplies generations. The harness decides which files to read, which specialist owns the next step and when to stop.

Terminal shell
**Implemented.** The terminal shell shares the team loop, demo adapter, provider selection and SQLite event stream with the browser. Headless JSON ends with an unstored `run.result` record. Missing usage stays unreported. The terminal reads provider addresses from its private data directory configuration. A configured address is masked before events are stored or rendered. Session exports also mask the stored workspace path. File replay reads the exported events without opening a store or starting a runtime.

The shared computer
Grok Bot’s published design gives a user one persistent cloud computer. The bots share files and browser state, have individual screens, and can hand tasks to another bot in a group. Its primary bot can create specialists. Each responding bot consumes usage. These are product behaviors described by xAI. Its internal prompts and scheduling algorithms are proprietary. [How Grok Bot works](https://docs.x.ai/grok-bot/how-grok-bot-works) · [Shared computer](https://docs.x.ai/grok-bot/computer-and-apps) · [Group messaging](https://docs.x.ai/grok-bot/chat-and-collaboration)

Bloom implements the shared-computer idea locally. Every team can discover ordinary files from the same desktop. Each output gets an immutable ID, a readable filename, a hash and directed input edges. Specialists can change files they were given: a revision, rename or move into a folder writes a new immutable file in the same revision chain, linked to the version it replaces. The desktop lists the newest revision each team may see, and every earlier revision stays readable. A revision derived from team notes is private to that team, so other teams keep the last shareable revision, and Forget withdraws it. Folders are catalog metadata; files on disk stay flat. The shell and browser in the optional graphical desktop belong to the user. Agent-controlled mouse, keyboard, separate screens and browser-login handoff are future integrations. The OS account remains the trust boundary.

Agent and memory contracts
| Concept | Local implementation |
| --- | --- |
| VI (Virtual Intelligence) | The head holds a name and charter. The planner assigns work by name to saved personas or current team members. Bloom drops unknown names and stops when no assignment matches. Recruiting a persona copies its saved jurisdiction, voice, stage and optional model onto the team. The scripted demo supplies its own example profiles. |
| OAI (Open AI Instance) | A provider-backed generation fulfills a role. The same profile can run on another configured model, and a persona with a preferred model runs on it. Each dispatch owns its input and reports its usage independently. |
| LA (Logical Agent) | The head can assign the verify stage to a named deterministic worker. It re-reads the admitted files and verifies their hashes without spending a model call. |
| Memory recall | Memory keeps the recall distinctions apart. Owner-confirmed notes are either rules, which always apply, or facts, recalled only when they match the task. A note belongs to one team or is shared with every team on the installation. Agent suggestions stay unconfirmed and are never recalled until the owner keeps them. Correct supersedes a note; Correct and Forget both move the epoch of every team that could use the note, so derived files and pending suggestions are withdrawn. Recall ranks notes with a portable floatation reading (`synaptic.score.v1`): lexical relevance in place of vector similarity (0.45), provenanc

Teams talk to each other
A head agent sees the other teams on the installation by name and jurisdiction. It may ask one of them one question per task. Bloom opens a turn in the other team's conversation, so that team shows as busy, cannot start its own task meanwhile, and can stop the answer. The other team's head answers once from shareable material only: its jurisdiction, notes shared with every team, its unscoped group posts and its shareable desktop titles. Private notes never cross a team boundary. The asking head sees no notes, so its question cannot carry them either. The answering head sees no other teams, so a question cannot be passed along. The question and answer are recorded in both conversations' event histories. The answer reaches the asking team's specialists, labelled as coming from another team. The asking team's call and token limits cover the answer.

Model calls and evidence
The head receives the brief, roster and ordinary desktop file titles. Worker calls receive the jurisdiction, explicit assignment, the ranked notes admitted for that assignment, recent group handoffs (including answers from other teams) and attached evidence. The text budget for all file excerpts in a worker packet is 28,000 characters, with a per-file cap of 12,000 characters. Character caps protect packet size. The usage ledger uses provider-reported token counts. Stable system instructions precede the changing evidence, allowing supporting providers to reuse their prompt prefix.

A team provider implements `generate({system, prompt, model, signal, ...})` and returns `{text, complete, model, usage, costUSD}`. `text` is always a string; a reply with no text body is returned as an empty, incomplete record. `usage` holds token counts only, in five fields: `input`, `output`, `total`, `cacheRead` and `cacheWrite`. A reported monetary cost is `costUSD`, beside usage rather than inside it. Missing metrics use null. Since 0.7.0 Bloom imports seed and runs every team provider behind its provider seam (`src/provider.mjs`): seed's `validateProvider` checks the adapter when Bloom starts, and seed's `normalizeGeneration` checks every reply before the team loop reads it. A reply outside the record stops the turn with `PROVIDER_CONTRACT`. Seed's record has no money field, so Bloom carries a reported `costUSD` beside it. `test/generation-record.test.mjs` holds both

Workspace tools
`src/workspace-tools.mjs` binds Drosera's workspace tool pack to the canonical
session directory from `workspacePath`. Its file tools check relative paths
and resolved link targets before content I/O. A recursive text search
visits regular workspace files in path order. Directory output and search
matches use workspace-relative names.

Writes queue by canonical path in the Bloom process and replace the target
atomically. A targeted update needs one exact match, including the check for
overlapping matches. Command execution uses the canonical workspace as its
working directory and takes an executable and arguments without shell
expansion. Bloom forwards `PATH`, `LANG`, and `TERM`. Each command gets a fresh
temporary `HOME`, and `USERPROFILE` on Windows, outside the workspace and the
user's home. Bloom removes it after the run. The command deadline
stops output capture and terminates the launched process. On POSIX it targets
the process group. Commands run under the local OS account and the coding
adapter owns the approval and dispatch flow.
Commands are off by default. The executor runs `workspace.shell.execute` only
when it is created with the `workspaceCommandAccess` symbol, which
`src/workspace-tools.mjs` exports and only `src/coding-loop.mjs` passes (a
guard test checks this). There is no test-only command mode: tests use the
same allowlisted gate.

The executor returns `output`, `truncatedBytes`, and `outputSha256`. It keeps a
UTF-8 prefix ending at a comp

Coding loop
**Implemented.** `src/coding-loop.mjs` is a coding runtime on the harness seam
`run(input, hooks)`. `bloom chat --workspace PATH` and `bloom run --headless
--workspace PATH` use it when no `--team` is named, and the browser workspace
lists it as a runtime when an endpoint is configured. Every model call runs
behind `src/provider.mjs`, so seed's `normalizeGeneration` checks each record.

Each model reply holds a short note and exactly one fenced json block,
`{ "tool": "<tool id>", "args": { } }`. Parsing is strict. Bloom checks the tool
against the admitted tools and the arguments against the face `inputSchema`
with seed's `validateValue`, and checks a result against an `outputSchema` when
the face declares one. Argument and output checks share one repair turn; a
call that runs resets it. A second failure stops the turn as `malformed`, and
nothing malformed runs. A reply the model did not finish (`complete: false`)
counts as malformed. `run.answer.create` ends the turn with `turn.finished`.

Read tools run without a prompt. `workspace.file.write`, `workspace.file.update`
and `workspace.shell.execute` raise `permission.requested` first, showing the
full content, the edit, or the command with every argument verbatim. A
rejection never executes, and the model is told "denied by owner". "Allow this
exact call for the session" binds the tool ID plus a SHA-256 digest of the
arguments, and is never offered for `workspace.shell.execute`. A headless run
refuses every write

Cloud providers
A provider with `locality` set to `cloud` is refused in the terminal until
`--allow-cloud` is passed, and only inside a folder created by
`scripts/make-sandbox.mjs` for the coding loop. Team sessions never use a cloud
provider. While cloud is on, Bloom asks before the first message leaves the
machine and before every tool call, including reads, and does not offer
session-wide allow. Model rows say cloud. The web workspace stays local only.
Opt-in live tests run with `BLOOM_LIVE=1 npm run test:live` (and
`BLOOM_LIVE_ALLOW_CLOUD=1` when the provider is cloud) and never from offline
`npm test`.

In cloud mode these leave the machine and go to the provider named in your
config (for AI Studio, Google): each task you approve, Bloom's fixed tool
instructions, short summaries of earlier tasks and answers in the same session,
the model's own replies within the turn, and every tool result you approve,
including file contents and command output. Bloom asks before each task is sent
and before each tool call; the follow-up requests inside a turn carry only
results you already approved and are sent without a further prompt. Your key
travels only in the request's Authorization header. What the provider keeps,
and for how long, is set by its terms, not by Bloom: Google's Gemini API terms
say that on unpaid use, including AI Studio and free quota, Google uses
submitted content and responses to improve its products. Use a throwaway
sandbox and send nothing you would not publish

Model profiles
`bloom doctor --probe` asks the configured provider what it supports and saves
the answer as a seed model profile in `profiles.json` in Bloom's data
directory, keyed by the provider's config name and the model alias. The file
holds no address, and the printed checks name the provider only by its config
name and locality.

The probe sends two requests. The models list, with a 5 second limit, shows
whether the server answers, which model IDs it lists, and whether the
configured alias's backend model is among them. A failure is reported as
`refused`, `timeout`, `tls` or `http-<code>`. One fixed one-token streaming
request, with a 30 second limit, shows whether the server streams; it carries
the same short message every time and nothing from the user. Context length,
tool calling and constrained output are `reported` only when the models list
entry publishes them, and `unknown` otherwise. No probe request carries a tools
or schema field, and an unknown check is never a pass. `doctor --probe` exits 1
on any failed check.

The coding loop reads the saved profile for the provider and alias it runs
with. A reported or probed context length sets the prompt budget, and a probed
"no" for streaming makes it ask for whole replies. Anything unknown falls back
to the default budget and to streaming. The action format stays the fenced json
block whatever the profile says, so tool calling and constrained output are
recorded but do not change the requests yet.

Local note writes
The HTTP handler checks the local host and rejects a mismatched Origin before looking up the team. Add note, Correct, Keep and Forget require `confirmed: true` in the request body after that lookup. The browser sends it on the corresponding user action. An authenticated seat gate would require independently verified browser identity and a seat binding. Bloom's session IDs identify local conversations, and the OS account is the trust boundary.

ViDesign continuity
Bloom’s original UI uses ViDesign’s emitted Nocturne property names for surfaces, contrast, Geist typography, radii and spacing. The conversation uses solid reading surfaces and a single composer. The application self-hosts its OFL fonts and requires no remote art or font requests. Team identity uses names, charters and voices.

The project includes the numerical and typographic properties it consumes. A maintainer with a ViDesign checkout can verify the public snapshot against its generated CSS:

```sh
npm run design:sync -- ../videsign/dist/tokens.css --check
```

Omit `--check` to update the used properties. A fresh Bloom checkout runs from the included snapshot. The upstream design handbook, source layouts, character artwork and brand marks are separate works.

Verification
The portable suite exercises the budgets, group handoffs, review hold, restart, deletion fence, file-integrity checks, the chat-completions adapter, the provider seam, the coding-session harness against a scripted runtime, the command gate, the provider probe against a fake server, the coding loop against a scripted provider and a synthetic project with zero network calls, and the smoke eval over the same synthetic project. The hosted checks start a real Bloom listener on Windows, macOS and Linux. A Chromium journey opens a reviewed document and tests a narrow viewport. These checks use synthetic briefs and source files. A hosted, billed generation and a graphical desktop session have distinct verification requirements.

# Bloom agent runtime
> **Withdrawn in part.** This pass planned five fixed starter seats with set names. Vivarium ships no fixed roster: agents are created by each person in setup, from generic templates ([vivarium ADR-0002](https://github.com/Vidoxlabs/vivarium/blob/main/docs/adr/0002-internal-agents-use-the-public-setup.md)). The starter-seat steps below are kept as history with placeholder names and are not to be built.

1. What the user does
A normal message to the head gets one head reply and creates no specialists.

Try a sample task sets staff for the next Send. The head may then create and run specialists.

To or @Name talks to one existing seat.

The five starter seats are `Starter 1` to `Starter 5`. The user can edit a seat through the member update route. The form for that edit is not in this pass.

2. Create
Inside `Teams.create`, after `nameOf` and before `this.harness.store.transaction`, reject a colliding head name. If `name.toLowerCase()` matches a starter seat name, throw the existing `bad(...)` error (`TEAM_INPUT`, HTTP 400) with a message that names the starter seats. Do not open the transaction. No session row, no `teams` row, and no `members` rows are written.

When the name does not collide, keep the current session and `teams` insert. In that same transaction, after `TeamStore.create`, insert exactly five `members` rows, in this order, so `rowid` order matches:

1. `Starter 1`
2. `Starter 2`
3. `Starter 3`
4. `Starter 4`
5. `Starter 5`

Each row uses the columns that already exist. Every row stores the same profile text:

- `charter`: `Help the user shape the next agent.`
- `voice`: `Clear and specific.`
- `stage`: `work`
- `model`: `null`

Charter and voice are profile text in those columns. They are shown by the existing member row (charter paragraph, voice hint). They are not a second prompt, and `Teams.create` does not gain a prompt column. The five share the turn model because `model` is null and the existing work call already falls back to `selectedModel`. Do not write a model id on these rows. Do not add a persona-library row for these names. The head remains the `teams` row and the session title, not a sixth `members` row.

3. Staff
`POST /api/sessions/:id/turns` keeps the body `Harness.start` already accepts. Add a boolean `staff`.

`Teams.input` sets `staff` to true only when `request.staff === true`. Omission, `false`, and any other value are false. `Teams.input` does not read the prompt to decide, and it does not call the provider.

The model must not decide `staff`. No plan call, worker call, or other provider call sets it. The model writes the reply and does not set staff. The sample button is the only way this pass sets staff true.

The browser may set the field. In `public/team.js`, the `Try a sample task` button may set a page flag when it inserts this exact sentence:

`Create a researcher to extract claims from the attached sources, a reviewer to check them, and an assembler to write a guide. Flag any evidence gaps.`

`teamView.target()` includes `staff: true` only while that flag is set. The flag stays set if the user edits the sentence before Send. Typing that sentence, or any other sentence, without using the button does not set the flag. After a successful Send, clear the flag. Clear it on `teamView.reset` as well. Do not add a second button, a checkbox, or a prompt scan in this pass.

`src/harness.mjs` includes `request.staff === true` in the request fingerprint array, after the files entry, so a replay cannot apply a different staff value to the same request id.

In `Teams.run`:

- A direct member (`To` or `@Name:`) ignores `staff`. Keep today’s single assignment, with no planner

4. Edit
Add `PATCH /api/teams/:id/members` beside the existing `POST` recruit branch. Do not change recruit. The seat name is JSON, not the UUID the path captures.

Body: `{ name, charter, voice, stage, renameTo }`. `renameTo` is optional. Ignore `model`, `prompt`, and any other field.

`name` identifies the current row, compared case-insensitively. Validate it with `nameOf`. If no member row matches, throw `bad('This agent is not on the team.')`. This route does not insert a row.

`charter` uses `string(..., 600, 'a jurisdiction')`. `voice` uses `string(..., 300, 'a voice')`. `stage` must be one of `research`, `review`, `assemble`, `work`, `verify`. Otherwise throw `bad('Choose a stage: research, review, assemble, work or verify.')`. Do not accept `head`.

If `renameTo` is omitted or null, keep the name. If it is present, validate it with `nameOf`. If it matches the current name case-insensitively, keep the name. If it matches the head name case-insensitively, throw `bad('The head agent already uses this name.')`. If another member already has that name, throw `bad('This team already has an agent with this name.')`.

Add `TeamStore.updateMember`. Update the existing row in place so its `rowid` does not change. Set `name` (when renaming), `charter`, `voice`, and `stage`. Do not set `model`.

If `this.harness.active` has this team id, throw the same error recruit uses: `BloomError('TURN_ACTIVE', 'Wait for the current turn to finish before changing the team.', 409)`.

Return HT

5. Timeline
Keep one center log. After `turn.started` clears the previous activity lists, `#plan` is the timeline for the new turn. Append rows in arrival order. Keep the existing `team.call` append. Do not append a second `team.call` row. Keep the existing `#tools` and `#usage` renderers. Do not copy usage into `#plan`. Usage stays in Usage.

Row text, using events the loop already emits:

- `turn.started`: `Turn started`
- `tool.updated`: the title and status label `renderTool` already writes. No new title.
- `team.call`: the existing `${actor} · Planning` when `phase` is `plan`, otherwise `${actor} · Working`
- `team.usage`: no timeline row
- `team.recall`: the existing `${actor} · notes reused · ${count} notes` when `hit` is true, otherwise `${actor} · notes loaded · ${count} notes`
- `team.message`: the author. When `verdict` is present, also `Review approved` for `approve`, and `Changes requested` for any other verdict
- `turn.finished`: `labels[data.status]` from `public/app.js`, or `data.status` when the map has no entry

Do not invent a route event.

Route line, only on a `team.message` whose `assignments` array is present. Under the list `public/app.js` already renders (`name — assignment`), add one text line: the author, then `, `, then each `assignments[].name` in array order, separated by `, `. Example shape: `Lead, Planner, Reviewer`. No arrow. No word “to”. Do not read or write a recipient. Do not put the `persona` boolean on this line.

When a later `team.mess

6. Already present
These already exist. A code agent does not rebuild them.

- `POST /api/teams/:id/members` recruits through `Teams.recruit`.
- `PUT` on the persona path calls `harness.teams.updatePersona`.
- `members.model` is a column. The work call passes `model || selectedModel`. A stored member model replaces the turn model when it is set.
- Specialist rows have a `Save as persona` button.

7. Leave out
- A mailbox, a second chat, and a `to` field on `team.message`.
- A per-member model. The five inserts store `model` null. `updateMember` does not change `model`. Do not add a seat model control.
- A prompt column.
- A sixth seeded seat. The head is the `teams` row. Do not insert these five into the persona library.
- Any seeded stage other than `work`. Do not seed `review`, `assemble`, or `verify`. Do not add a stage id. Do not order assignments so a `revise` verdict skips the starter seats. The existing `reviewBlocked` rule stays as it is.
- The untrusted six-step excerpt as `Teams.run`. Do not run one seat twice. Do not add agents or stages for that excerpt.
- A prompt scan, on the server or in the browser, that decides `staff`.
- A loop that runs every stored member on a head turn whose `staff` is not true.
- An insert on `PATCH /api/teams/:id/members`.
- A visible member editor, a roster relabel, and any edit to `docs/ui/interface-contract.md` or any other file under `docs/ui/`.
- Any edit to `docs/backend/research/agent-runtime-patterns.md`.
- A new route event, a usage row inside `#plan`, and an arrow or recipient on the assignment-order line.
- Prompt text copied into charter, voice, docs, or tests.
- Setting omitted `staff` to true.

Files a code agent may change
- `src/teams.mjs`
- `src/team-store.mjs`
- `src/http.mjs`
- `src/harness.mjs`
- `public/team.js`
- `public/app.js`

- A sixth seeded seat. The head is the `teams` row. Do not insert these five into the persona library.
- Any seeded stage other than `work`. Do not seed `review`, `assemble`, or `verify`. Do not add a stage id. Do not order assignments so a `revise` verdict skips the starter seats. The existing `reviewBlocked` rule stays as it is.
- The untrusted six-step excerpt as `Teams.run`. Do not run one seat twice. Do not add agents or stages for that excerpt.
- A prompt scan, on the server or in the browser, that decides `staff`.
- A loop that runs every stored member on a head turn whose `staff` is not true.
- An insert on `PATCH /api/teams/:id/members`.
- A visible member editor, a roster relabel, and any edit to `docs/ui/interface-contract.md` or any other file under `docs/ui/`.
- Any edit to `docs/backend/research/agent-runtime-patterns.md`.
- A new route event, a usage row inside `#plan`, and an arrow or recipient on the assignment-order line.
- Prompt text copied into charter, voice, docs, or tests.
- Setting omitted `staff` to true.

# CAP-04: Workspace tool set and coding loop
- ID: `CAP-04`
- Title: Workspace tool set and coding loop
- Lead: `bloom`
- Touches: `drosera`
- Horizon: `now`
- Milestone: `M2`
- CLI phase: `P2`
- Status: `in-progress`
- Claim: `specified`
- Depends on: `CAP-03`

Why
Bloom's coding sessions (`src/harness.mjs`) currently run only the scripted demonstration adapter (`src/demo.mjs`) and ship no live coding runtime (`docs/architecture.md`). A local coding loop needs deterministic workspace tools bound to the session workspace root so an agent can inspect, search, edit, test, and finish cleanly without escaping the workspace or racing on concurrent writes.

What it does
- Defines seven neutral tools whose faces and recipe live in `drosera` (`CAP-04.1`) and whose execution runs inside `bloom` (`CAP-04.2`, `CAP-04.3`):
  - Read tools: `workspace.file.read`, `workspace.dir.list`, `workspace.text.search`, and `run.answer.create`.
  - Write tools: `workspace.file.write`, `workspace.file.update`, and `workspace.shell.execute`.
- Read takes `path` and optional one-based inclusive `startLine` and `endLine`. List and literal search use an optional `path` rooted at the workspace. Search requires `query`. Write takes `path` and `content`. Update takes `path`, `oldText`, and `newText`. Command takes `command` and optional string array `args`. Finish takes `text`.
- Contains file tool paths: file tool path parameters resolve relative to the session's canonical workspace root (`realpath` of `session.workspace` in `src/harness.mjs`). File tools check symlink targets and refuse outside paths before content I/O.
- Serializes writes per canonical file path: concurrent `workspace.file.write` and `workspace.file.update` calls targeting the same file wait on a per-path queue so updates never interleave or drop edits.
- Caps tool output deterministically: retain a UTF-8 prefix with no partial code point, report `truncatedBytes`, and include the SHA-256 hex digest of the full decoded output.
- Integrates the coding loop into Bloom's runtime: each model call passes through `src/provider.mjs` (`validateProvider` and `normalizeGeneration`), validates inp

Contract touchpoints
- `docs/architecture.md`: coding runtime seam (`run(input, hooks)`), provider seam (`src/provider.mjs`), and OS-account / workspace trust boundary.
- `drosera/docs/contracts/tools.md` and `drosera/docs/contracts/cookbook.md` (`CAP-04.1`): workspace and finish tool face pack and coding-loop recipe.
- `seed/docs/contracts/tool-id.md` and `seed/docs/contracts/run-model.md`: tool-ID grammar, reading classes, intent-first recording, and `allowedTools` admission.

Tool IDs and events
### Tool IDs

| Tool ID | Effect | Third-party egress | Owner gate | Summary |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `workspace.file.read` | `read` | `false` | `false` | Read file contents or bounded line ranges inside the workspace root |
| `workspace.dir.list` | `read` | `false` | `false` | List directory entries inside the workspace root |
| `workspace.text.search` | `read` | `false` | `false` | Search text patterns across files inside the workspace root |
| `workspace.file.write` | `write` | `false` | `false` | Create or overwrite a file inside the workspace root |
| `workspace.file.update` | `write` | `false` | `false` | Apply targeted edits to an existing file inside the workspace root |
| `workspace.shell.execute` | `write` | `false` | `false` | Run an allowlisted command with the workspace as the working directory, after per-call approval |
| `run.answer.create` | `read` | `false` | `false` | Emit the structured final response that ends the coding loop |

### Events

| Event | Producer | Payload fields | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `tool.updated` | `bloom` (`src/coding-loop.mjs`) | `id`, `toolId`, `effect`, `summary`, `status`, `durationMs`, `approval`, `bytes`, `truncatedBytes`, `outputSha256`, and for commands `exitCode`, `timedOut`, `output`, `homeCleanupFailed` | One trace row per call; the summary names paths and commands, never file contents |
| `model.call` | `bloom` (`src/coding-loop.mjs`) | `call`, `durationMs`, `model`, `complete`, `u

Acceptance tests
- `workspace-root-containment-refuses-escape`: traversal segments and symlinks escaping the workspace root fail closed before any read or write.
- `per-path-write-serialization`: concurrent `workspace.file.write` and `workspace.file.update` calls on one canonical path execute sequentially with no lost edits.
- `capped-output-reports-truncated-bytes-and-sha256`: oversized tool output truncates to budget and includes exact `truncatedBytes` plus SHA-256 of the untruncated output.
- `coding-loop-finishes-via-run-answer-create`: coding loop dispatches provider generations behind `src/provider.mjs`, runs admitted tools, and stops cleanly on `run.answer.create`.
- `unadmitted-tool-rejected-before-execution`: any tool outside the objective's `allowedTools` list is refused before execution.
- `coding-loop-fixes-fixture-offline`: the loop fixes the synthetic project's failing test through approved calls with zero network calls.
- `demo-session-fixture-is-lf`, `demo-session-export-is-byte-stable`: the recorded session stays LF and matches a fresh stable export on every platform.
- `reject-is-never-executed`, `allow-session-binds-args-digest`, `headless-never-writes`, `trace-row-per-call-without-file-contents`, `endpoint-marker-never-in-events-or-export`.
- `shell-refuses-unlisted-command`, `shell-refuses-absolute-and-parent-args`, `shell-refuses-symlinked-outside-arg`, `shell-refuses-eval-flags`, `shell-home-is-isolated`, `shell-home-cleanup-failure-flagged`, `command-a

Slices
- `CAP-04.1` (`drosera`, milestone `M2`, status `landed`): Workspace and finish tool faces pack and recipe.
- `CAP-04.2` (`bloom`, milestone `M2`, status `landed`): Workspace root path containment, write serialization, capped digest output.
- `CAP-04.3` (`bloom`, milestone `M2`, status `landed`): Coding loop integration with workspace tools and finish action. Before `workspace.shell.execute` runs outside tests, all of these hold: the exact command allowlist `node`, `npm` and `git`, resolved against a fixed search path; refusal of interpreter eval and redirect flags (`node -e`, `--eval`, `-p`, `--print`, `-r`, `--require`, `--import`, `--input-type`; `npm exec`, `npm x`, `npm --prefix`; `git -C`, `--git-dir`, `--work-tree`, `-c`, `--exec-path`; and `sh`, `bash`, `cmd` and `powershell` as commands); refusal of arguments that are absolute, contain `..`, or resolve outside the workspace, including through links and in `--flag=value`; an isolated per-run `HOME` (and `USERPROFILE` on Windows); per-call approval with no session-wide allow for commands; the owner's network answer, verbatim (2026-11-24): "I accept option A for bloom's coding shell: network not blocked; npm offline; git local-only; risk documented"; and tests for each in `test/shell-gate.test.mjs` and `test/coding-loop.test.mjs`.

Non-goals
- Importing `drosera` inside `bloom` at runtime before an explicit package adoption task.
- Virtual path remapping or default-off shell scope isolation across custom roots (`CAP-17`).
- The approval modal and resume (`CAP-06.4`) or trace HTML export (`CAP-10`).
- An operating-system sandbox or network block for commands.

Family rules and conflicts
- Tool faces and recipe definitions belong in `drosera` (`CAP-04.1`); execution and workspace I/O belong in `bloom` (`CAP-04.2`, `CAP-04.3`).
- Every tool ID conforms to `seed` grammar and every provider call runs behind `src/provider.mjs`.
- Zero new runtime dependencies.

Open owner decisions
- `D12` Decided 2026-11-24 in drosera#4: Approve the workspace update, shell, and finish tool IDs? Owner's answer, relayed from the Codex session (not yet confirmed in the owner's own typed words): "Continue with work and assume D12 is approved".

Owner's answer, relayed from the Codex session (not yet confirmed in the owner's own typed words): "Assume recommended and continue".
- `D17` Decided 2026-11-24 in bloom#5: Command allowlist: exactly `node`, `npm` and `git`? Owner's answer, relayed from the Codex session (not yet confirmed in the owner's own typed words): "Assume recommended and continue".
- `D18` Decided 2026-11-24 in bloom#5: Approvals: write tools always ask, "Allow for session" binds the tool ID plus an arguments digest, and is never offered for `workspace.shell.execute`? Owner's answer, relayed from the Codex session (not yet confirmed in the owner's own typed words): "Assume recommended and continue".
- `D19` Decided 2026-11-24 in bloom#5: Should shell commands be able to r

Evidence
- `CAP-04.3`: `test/shell-gate.test.mjs` checks Git metadata refusal and keeps ordinary directories writable. Its Git fixture reads back the repository settings and requires status, add, commit, and diff to succeed without running the configured programs.
- Cloud opt-in and Gemini (bloom#9): `src/sandbox-marker.mjs` and `scripts/make-sandbox.mjs` mark throwaway sandboxes; `--allow-cloud` gates cloud providers in the terminal; `src/provider-errors.mjs` maps Google rate-limit errors; `test/cloud-gemini.test.mjs` covers the offline gate and probe shape; `test/live/live-suite.live.mjs` is loaded only by `npm run test:live`.

- `CAP-04.1`: drosera#4 exports the workspace tool pack and coding recipe. Bloom pins its head pending upstream merge.
- `CAP-04.3`: `test/coding-loop.test.mjs` runs the loop over a synthetic project with a scripted provider and zero network calls, writes the byte-stable session `test/fixtures/demo-session.jsonl` through the export path, and covers the repair budget, admission, approvals, headless refusal, trace rows and endpoint masking. `test/shell-gate.test.mjs` covers the command gate, `test/mode

Changes
