# CAP-08: Seat orchestration
- ID: `CAP-08`
- Title: Seat orchestration
- Lead: `bloom`
- Touches: `seed`
- Horizon: `next`
- Milestone: `M3`
- CLI phase: `P3`
- Status: `proposed`
- Claim: `planned`
- Depends on: `CAP-07`

Why
Bloom's team loop (`src/teams.mjs`) coordinates a head planner and specialist stages sequentially, while `docs/backend/agent-runtime.md` tracks team seats in database `members` rows. Multi-seat runs need declarative seat definitions keyed by role IDs rather than hardcoded character names or per-agent instruction files, pre-run validation so broken team documents fail before any model call, and bounded parallel fan-out that merges results deterministically in plan order.

What it does
- Preserves deterministic coordinator and verifier roles: the head (`chair`) plans seat assignments, specialists execute in plan order, a `revise` verdict stops downstream assembly, and the deterministic verifier checks file integrity and invariants without calling any model.
- Stores seats strictly as structured data in `src/seats.mjs` alongside persisted `members` rows in `src/team-store.mjs`: stored rows, events, tool IDs, and model prompts carry closed role IDs only (`chair`, `framing`, `risk`, `coherence`, `sequencing`), never per-agent instruction files and never display names; display labels come from the design canon and are read **only by renderers** (pending owner ruling `D12`).
- Validates the declarative team document before a run starts (`CAP-08.1` in `seed`, wired in `CAP-08.2`): passes parsed `agents` and `tools` documents through `seed`'s `checkRegistryDocuments` plus tool-ID grammar checks (`parseToolId` / `checkRegistry`) and stops before any model call if any reference or ID is invalid.
- Adds bounded parallel fan-out (`CAP-08.3`): independent steps marked for parallel execution run under a strict concurrency cap, a per-step timeout, and a per-seat tool subset strictly contained within the objective's `allowedTools`, merging outputs deterministically in plan order.

Contract touchpoints
- `docs/architecture.md`: coordinator, specialist, and deterministic verifier roles, admission checks, and review hold behavior.
- `docs/backend/agent-runtime.md`: `members` table persistence, direct vs planned execution paths, and deterministic verifier step semantics.
- `seed/docs/contracts/tool-id.md` (`CAP-08.1`): `checkRegistryDocuments`, tool-ID grammar checks, and `allowedTools` constraints.
- `seed/docs/contracts/run-model.md`: objective `allowedTools` and deterministic ordering rules.

Tool IDs and events
### Tool IDs

| Tool ID | Effect | Third-party egress | Owner gate | Summary |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |

None. This capability introduces no tool IDs.

### Events

| Event | Producer | Payload fields | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `team.call` | `bloom` (`src/teams.mjs`) | `actor`, `roleId`, `calls`, `limit`, `phase`, `stepIndex` | Records seat role ID and step order for planned and fan-out calls |
| `team.message` | `bloom` (`src/teams.mjs`) | `author`, `roleId`, `text`, `epoch`, `assignments`, `verdict` | Carries ordered assignments, review verdicts, and deterministic verifier output |
| `team.usage` | `bloom` (`src/teams.mjs`) | `actor`, `roleId`, `calls`, `limit`, `model`, `usage`, `costUSD` | Records per-seat usage independently through `src/provider.mjs` |

Acceptance tests
- `invalid-team-document-stops-before-model-call`: malformed `agents` or `tools` document, unknown tool in `allowedTools`, or invalid tool ID stops via `checkRegistryDocuments` before invoking the provider.
- `revise-verdict-blocks-assembly`: a specialist review returning `revise` halts assembly and downstream assignments.
- `deterministic-verifier-makes-zero-model-calls`: verifier seat validates hashes and invariants deterministically with zero calls to `provider.generate`.
- `seats-data-uses-role-ids-only-no-instruction-files`: `src/seats.mjs`, `members` rows, emitted events, tool IDs, and model prompts carry only `chair`, `framing`, `risk`, `coherence`, and `sequencing` role IDs with no display names or instruction markdown files, while display labels come from the design canon and are read only by renderers (pending `D12`).
- `bounded-fanout-respects-concurrency-timeout-and-tool-subset`: parallel fan-out enforces max concurrency, cancels/times out slow steps at per-step limit, and rejects tools outside the seat's subset of objective `allowedTools`.
- `fanout-merges-results-in-plan-order`: regardless of completion arrival order, merged messages and artifacts match original plan step order.

Slices
- `CAP-08.1` (`seed`, milestone `M3`, status `proposed`): Declarative team document validation checks.
- `CAP-08.2` (`bloom`, milestone `M3`, status `proposed`): Declarative seats data, role IDs, and deterministic verifier handoff.
- `CAP-08.3` (`bloom`, milestone `M3`, status `proposed`): Bounded parallel fan-out with timeout, tool subset, and plan-order merge.

Non-goals
- Storing per-seat prompt or instruction markdown files in the repository (`AGENTS.md` prohibits agent instruction directories).
- Allowing any seat to expand `allowedTools` beyond the objective's admitted set.
- Defining the plan review state machine or owner plan-gate records (`CAP-07` in `aestivation`).

Family rules and conflicts
- Stored seat rows (`src/seats.mjs` and `members` rows), events, tool IDs, and model prompts carry only the five closed role IDs (`chair`, `framing`, `risk`, `coherence`, `sequencing`); display labels come from the design canon and are read **only by renderers** (pending `D12`).
- Pre-run validation delegates to `seed`'s `checkRegistryDocuments` and `parseToolId` rather than duplicating registry validation in Bloom.
- Sequencing note: `CAP-08` (`M3`) depends on `CAP-07` (`M3`), which depends on `CAP-06.1` (owner-gate decision record at `M3`, with `CAP-07.3` plan-digest binding folded into `CAP-06.1` under `D14`), keeping all of `CAP-08` inside `M3`.

Open owner decisions
- `D12` (pending owner ruling): seats ruling confirming that `src/seats.mjs` and `members` rows store closed role IDs (`chair`, `framing`, `risk`, `coherence`, `sequencing`) while display labels live in the design canon and are read only by renderers, how `src/seats.mjs` aligns with or supersedes starter `members` rows in `docs/backend/agent-runtime.md`, plus default concurrency cap and step timeout values.
- `D14` (pending owner confirmation unless overridden): `CAP-06.1` ships at `M3` with `CAP-07.3` folded in so `CAP-07` depends on `CAP-06.1` at `M3`.

Evidence
- None yet (`claim: planned`).

Changes
- `2026-11-23`: Clarified role-ID storage vs renderer-only design-canon display labels (`D12`), updated `CAP-07` sequencing note to `CAP-06.1` at `M3` (`D14`), and added `M3` slice milestones.
- `2026-11-23`: Initial capability specification created in Phase 0 timeline scaffold.

# CAP-10: Trace and observability
- ID: `CAP-10`
- Title: Trace and observability
- Lead: `bloom`
- Touches: `seed`
- Horizon: `next`
- Milestone: `M4`
- CLI phase: `P4`
- Status: `proposed`
- Claim: `planned`
- Depends on: `CAP-04`

Why
`Store` (`src/store.mjs`) and SSE streaming (`src/http.mjs`) already persist and stream numbered events, but team and coding turns emit different payloads without uniform correlation IDs, there is no `bloom trace` replay or static HTML export command, and private content plus endpoint privacy rules require explicit digest redaction across stored events and exports.

What it does
- Unifies team and coding runs onto one append-only typed event stream with monotonic sequence numbers (`seq`) and correlation IDs (`run`, `attempt`, `step`, `seat`) specified in `CAP-10.1` (`seed`) and emitted by `bloom` (`CAP-10.2`).
- Supports four read-only renderer views driven strictly from the persisted event stream (renderers never mutate run state or call providers):
  1. Full state post-step view
  2. Deltas-only view
  3. Debug view (correlation IDs, digests, counts, refusal codes)
  4. Token deltas view (streamed model text chunks)
- Implements `bloom trace <run>` (`CAP-10.3`) to replay a stored run step-by-step in the terminal or export a self-contained static HTML trace report with zero external network links or third-party assets.
- Enforces digest redaction and endpoint privacy: private content (private notes, redacted tool or memory payloads) is logged using SHA-256 digests and byte/character counts rather than raw private text, and configured provider endpoint addresses and credentials are never recorded in events or exports.
- Aggregates per-seat and per-step usage across `seed`'s five-field token record (`input`, `output`, `total`, `cacheRead`, `cacheWrite`) and optional reported `costUSD`, keeping unreported metrics `null`.

Contract touchpoints
- `docs/architecture.md`: durable event sequence numbers, SSE replay, provider usage ledger (`costUSD` beside usage), and private-note scoping.
- `seed/docs/contracts/run-model.md` (`CAP-10.1`): correlation IDs (`run`, `attempt`, `step`, `seat`) on run trace records.
- `seed/docs/contracts/provider.md`: normalized five-field `usage` record.

Tool IDs and events
### Tool IDs

| Tool ID | Effect | Third-party egress | Owner gate | Summary |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |

None. This capability introduces no tool IDs.

### Events

| Event | Producer | Payload fields | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `turn.started` | `bloom` (`src/store.mjs`) | `seq`, `run`, `attempt`, `model`, `title` | Starts correlated trace span for a run attempt |
| `assistant.delta` | `bloom` (`src/harness.mjs`) | `seq`, `run`, `attempt`, `step`, `seat`, `text` | Streamed text delta consumed by the token-delta view |
| `tool.updated` | `bloom` (`src/harness.mjs`) | `seq`, `run`, `attempt`, `step`, `seat`, `toolId`, `status`, `outputSha256`, `truncatedBytes` | Typed tool lifecycle record with digest metadata |
| `team.call` | `bloom` (`src/teams.mjs`) | `seq`, `run`, `attempt`, `step`, `seat`, `actor`, `phase` | Correlated model dispatch marker |
| `team.usage` | `bloom` (`src/teams.mjs`) | `seq`, `run`, `attempt`, `step`, `seat`, `model`, `usage`, `costUSD` | Per-seat and per-step token usage and reported cost |
| `team.recall` | `bloom` (`src/teams.mjs`) | `seq`, `run`, `attempt`, `step`, `seat`, `hit`, `count`, `digests` | Records memory participation using digests/counts under strict redaction |
| `turn.finished` | `bloom` (`src/store.mjs`) | `seq`, `run`, `attempt`, `status`, `reason` | Closes correlated trace span |

Acceptance tests
- `stream-preserves-monotonic-seq-and-correlation-ids`: every emitted event carries strictly increasing `seq` and valid `run`, `attempt`, `step`, and `seat` correlation IDs.
- `four-renderer-views-read-only-over-same-stream`: full-state, deltas-only, debug, and token-deltas views render deterministically from the persisted event stream without mutating state.
- `bloom-trace-replays-steps-and-exports-self-contained-html`: `bloom trace <run>` replays events step-by-step and emits a single self-contained HTML file with zero external requests.
- `private-content-stored-as-digests-and-endpoint-address-never-recorded`: private memory text and endpoint addresses/credentials never appear in stored events or exported HTML.
- `per-seat-and-per-step-usage-preserves-null-for-missing-metrics`: usage summaries break down token fields and `costUSD` by `seat` and `step` while keeping missing counts as `null`.

Slices
- `CAP-10.1` (`seed`, milestone `M4`, status `proposed`): Correlation IDs on run trace records.
- `CAP-10.2` (`bloom`, milestone `M4`, status `proposed`): Unified append-only typed event stream and four renderer views.
- `CAP-10.3` (`bloom`, milestone `M4`, status `proposed`): Trace replay command, HTML export, digest redaction, and per-seat usage.

Non-goals
- Adding a third-party terminal UI library (zero runtime dependencies remain law).
- Streaming traces to a remote observability backend or loading external scripts/styles in HTML exports.
- Estimating missing token counts or fabricating monetary cost savings.

Family rules and conflicts
- Zero new runtime dependencies: terminal renderer and HTML export use Node.js built-ins and Bloom's self-hosted Nocturne CSS snapshot.
- Renderers are strictly read-only consumers of the event stream.
- Endpoint URLs, credentials, and raw private notes must never reach stored traces or exports.

Open owner decisions
- `D12` (pending owner ruling): renderer ruling without a third-party TUI library, governing terminal view formatting and planned for `docs/adr/0001-terminal-renderer.md`.

Evidence
- None yet (`claim: planned`).

Changes
- `2026-11-23`: Added `M4` slice milestones across `CAP-10.1`..`CAP-10.3` and aligned `D12` ADR status reference.
- `2026-11-23`: Initial capability specification created in Phase 0 timeline scaffold.

# CAP-14: Eval harness
- ID: `CAP-14`
- Title: Eval harness
- Lead: `bloom`
- Touches: `seed`, `trellis`
- Horizon: `next` (`CAP-14.1`, `CAP-14.2` in `M5`; `CAP-14.3`, `CAP-14.4` in `later` `M8`)
- Milestone: `M5` (`CAP-14.1`, `CAP-14.2` at `M5`; `CAP-14.3`, `CAP-14.4` at `M8`)
- CLI phase: `P5`
- Status: `in-progress`
- Claim: `specified`
- Depends on: `CAP-10`

Why
Bloom needs repeatable, deterministic evaluation over coding and team workflows so changes to prompts, tool schemas, context packing, or orchestration can be measured locally against known cases and saved baselines without manual testing or opaque scores.

What it does
- Defines a structured dataset format of evaluation cases, each carrying `id`, `input` (prompt, workspace fixture, admitted tools), `expected` assertions, and `metadata` (tags, suite tier, baseline reference).
- Runs deterministic evaluators first on every case:
  - `exact`: exact normalized text equality.
  - `contains`: required substring or pattern presence.
  - `schema-valid`: output conformance via `CAP-03` schema validation.
  - `tool-trajectory`: invoked tool IDs checked in exact order or as an unordered set.
  - `files-changed`: expected modified file paths and content digests inside the isolated fixture workspace.
  - `tests-pass`: deterministic command exit check inside the fixture workspace.
- Supports an optional model-based evaluator only when explicitly enabled, always labeled `judge` in outputs and reports, and never allowed as the sole pass criterion (any deterministic evaluator failure fails the case).

# CAP-15: Research flow
- ID: `CAP-15`
- Title: Research flow
- Lead: `bloom`
- Touches: `capillary`, `aestivation`, `drosera`
- Horizon: `later`
- Milestone: `M8`
- CLI phase: `none`
- Status: `proposed`
- Claim: `planned`
- Depends on: `CAP-05`, `CAP-07`, `CAP-08`

Why
Today `src/sources.mjs` (`importURL`) only retrieves literal HTTPS URLs pasted into a brief by the user (`src/teams.mjs`). Complex investigations need coordinator routing between a direct answer and a structured research workflow, optional local context scanning, an owner-approved research plan before external egress, owner-gated source searches, and a reporter that ties every factual claim to recorded sources or labels gaps explicitly.

What it does
- **Coordinator routing (`CAP-15.4`)**: The coordinator (`chair`) evaluates whether the prompt can be answered directly from admitted local context or requires a multi-step research workflow.
- **Optional background scan**: When local context is needed first, a bounded workspace scan gathers project context via `capillary`'s context packer (`CAP-05`) before planning external research.
- **Owner-approved typed research plan (`CAP-15.2` in `aestivation`)**: Proposes a plan with typed steps (`research`, `analysis`, `processing`) routed through `CAP-07` (`aestivation` validation plus owner approval or edit) before any search or processing step executes.
- **Owner-gated search and read (`CAP-15.1` in `drosera`, `CAP-15.4` in `bloom`)**: External search runs through `research.source.search` (`effect: read`, `thirdPartyEgress: true`), passing through the `CAP-06` owner gate before leaving the owner's system. Retrieved public documents are stored as recorded `capillary` sources with SHA-256 digests (`CAP-15.3`).
- **Cited reporter (`CAP-15.3` in `capillary`, `CAP-15.4` in `bloom`)**: Final research output cites recorded `capillary` source IDs and digests for claims; any claim lacking a supporting recorded source is explicitly flagged as uncited rather than presented as verified.
- **Plan revision and step caps**: Research plans enforce strict per-run step limits and plan revision limits; reaching either limit stops further exploration and reports the limit reason cleanly

Contract touchpoints
- `docs/architecture.md`: public source retrieval rules (`src/sources.mjs`), coordinator planning, evidence packet bounds.
- `drosera/docs/contracts/tools.md` (`CAP-15.1`): `research.source.search` tool face with `thirdPartyEgress: true`.
- `aestivation/docs/contracts/plan.md` (`CAP-15.2`): typed research steps (`research`, `analysis`, `processing`) and step/revision caps.
- `capillary/docs/contracts/retrieval.md` (`CAP-15.3`): cited source attachment and uncited-claim flagging.

# Live test runbook
This runbook takes the coding loop from an offline rehearsal to a first live run against your own local model, in a throwaway sandbox. Every write and every command asks first. Run the commands from the folder that holds your checkouts. `<sandbox folder>` is a new or empty folder outside any git clone, and `<your-endpoint>` is your model server's chat-completions base URL.

The endpoint lives only in the private config file described below. Never put it on a command line, in an environment variable, in a chat message or in a shared log. Bloom prints the provider by its config name and locality, never by its address.

Offline rehearsal
These steps call no model and need no config file.

Run the test suite:

```bash
cd bloom && npm install && npm test
```

Step through the recorded coding session, pressing Enter to advance:

```bash
cd bloom && node bin/bloom.mjs replay test/fixtures/demo-session.jsonl --step
```

Run the scripted model against a fresh sandbox. It asks before each write and command and ends with the sandbox's git diff:

```bash
cd bloom && node scripts/scripted-run.mjs <sandbox folder>
```

The shell rows show the demo test failing (`pass 0 fail 1`) and then passing (`pass 1 fail 0`). The diff adds `NOTES.md` and changes `value < end` to `value <= end` in `src/range.mjs`.

Probe
Ask the server what it supports and save its model profile:

```bash
cd bloom && node bin/bloom.mjs doctor --probe
```

The probe sends two requests: the models list, and one fixed one-token streaming request that carries nothing of yours. Each row reads `pass`, `fail` or `unknown`. Reachability, Model IDs and Model should pass. Context length, Tool calling and Constrained output stay `unknown` unless the server publishes them, and that is fine. The command exits 1 if any row fails. The saved profile sets the coding loop's prompt budget and whether it streams. The offline version of the probe runs in `npm test` against a fake server.

Live run
Make a fresh sandbox, then start the coding loop in it:

```bash
cd bloom && node scripts/make-sandbox.mjs <sandbox folder>
```

```bash
cd bloom && node bin/bloom.mjs chat --workspace <sandbox folder>
```

At the prompt, type the same task the rehearsal uses:

```text
Create NOTES.md with one line describing this project. Run the tests, fix the failing test, run the tests again, and finish with a short summary.
```

Read each approval before you answer it. Approve writes and test commands in the sandbox, and reject anything else. When the loop finishes, look at what changed:

```bash
cd <sandbox folder> && env -u GEMINI_API_KEY git -c core.fsmonitor=false --no-pager status && env -u GEMINI_API_KEY git -c core.fsmonitor=false --no-pager diff --no-ext-diff
```

The run passes when all of these hold:

- Text streams as the model writes it, and a model row follows each call.
- Every tool call shows one trace row with its tool, summary, status and timing, and no file contents.
- Bloom asked before every write and every command, and nothing you rejected ran.
- The sandbox tests fail first, and pass after the fix.
- The loop ends with an answer, and the diff holds only the note and the fix.
- No output shows the endpoint.

Web view
The same run in the browser, against a second fresh sandbox:

```bash
cd bloom && node scripts/make-sandbox.mjs <sandbox folder>
```

```bash
cd bloom && npm start -- --workspace <sandbox folder>
```

Open the local page the command prints, choose a coding session with the sandbox folder, and send the task. The conversation streams the replies and ends with an Answer message. The activity panel shows a row for each model call and each tool call, with command output under shell rows, and an approval card with the exact change or command before each write and command. Answer approvals in the page. Stop the server with Ctrl-C, then check the diff as in the live run. To see the same view with no model at all, start Bloom with `npm run demo` and create a coding session: the scripted demo runtime drives it.

Troubleshooting
- **Reachability fails with `refused`:** the server is not running, or the address in the config is wrong. Fix the config file and probe again.
- **`timeout`:** the server answered too slowly. The models list gets 5 seconds and the streaming check 30.
- **`tls`:** the server's certificate is not trusted. Use a trusted certificate, or for a plain HTTP server on your own network set `"allowInsecureHttp": true`.
- **`http-401` or `http-403`:** the server wants a key. Set the key field described in the README and keep the key in your shell's environment.
- **`http-404`:** the base URL usually needs its API path, such as one ending in `/v1`.
- **Model fails:** the alias's backend model is not among the listed IDs. Copy the exact ID from the Model IDs row into `backendModel`.
- **The run stops as `malformed`:** the model did not reply with exactly one fenced json action, even after one repair turn. Try a model that follows instructions more closely.
- **A command is refused:** only `node`, `npm` and `git` run, with arguments inside the workspace. The refusal message names the rule.
- **Replies arrive all at once:** the probe saw that the server does not stream, so the loop asks for whole replies.

Google AI Studio
Use your provider's OpenAI-compatible base URL as `<cloud-endpoint>` (the provider's own documentation names it) with a cloud provider and the model id `gemini-4-hydrogen` (or the id your AI Studio list shows). Example provider entry:

```json
"aistudio": {
  "kind": "chat-completions",
  "baseURL": "<cloud-endpoint>",
  "locality": "cloud",
  "apiKeyEnv": "GEMINI_API_KEY"
}
```

Put the key only in the shell (type this yourself; do not paste the value into chat or a file): `read -rs GEMINI_API_KEY && export GEMINI_API_KEY`.

Probe and chat need `--allow-cloud`, and chat only inside a sandbox from `scripts/make-sandbox.mjs`:

```bash
cd bloom && node bin/bloom.mjs doctor --probe --allow-cloud
```

```bash
cd bloom && node scripts/make-sandbox.mjs <sandbox folder>
```

```bash
cd bloom && node bin/bloom.mjs chat --workspace <sandbox folder> --allow-cloud
```

While cloud is on, Bloom asks before the first message leaves the machine and before every tool call, including reads. Model rows say cloud. The web workspace stays local only.
Team sessions never use a cloud provider.
The sandbox marker guards against mistakes; it is not a security boundary.

Opt-in live tests
Offline `npm test` never loads these. Against your configured provider:

```bash
cd bloom && BLOOM_LIVE=1 npm run test:live
```

At most 20 model calls per run of the whole suite. The suite reads the provider only from bloom's data directory (or `BLOOM_LIVE_DATA_DIR`), never from an endpoint environment variable. When the configured provider is cloud, set `BLOOM_LIVE_ALLOW_CLOUD=1` as well; without that second flag the cloud live tests fail on an assert before any request. `live-loop-fixes-sandbox` is local-only and does not use the cloud flag. Local providers need only `BLOOM_LIVE=1`.

Residual risk
Approval of each call is the boundary. `npm test` runs whatever the sandbox's `package.json` scripts say, and the model may have written those scripts in a write you approved. Commands can reach the network: npm is set offline (flags that change registry, cache or online mode are refused) and git is limited to local subcommands with fsmonitor, hooks and `diff.external` forced off, but Bloom does not block network access from the process. The isolated `HOME` only changes an environment variable, so a command can still find your real home folder through the operating system. A detached grandchild process can outlive the call. Writes under `.git/` are refused. Use a throwaway sandbox, read every approval, and keep the sandbox away from folders you care about. [architecture.md](architecture.md) has the full command gate.

In cloud mode these leave the machine and go to the provider named in your config (for AI Studio, Google): each task you approve, Bloom's fixed tool instructions, short summaries of earlier tasks and answers in the same session, the model's own replies within the turn, and every tool result you approve, including file contents and command output. Bloom asks before each task is sent and before each tool call; the follow-up requests inside a turn carry only results you already approved and are sent without a further prompt. Your key travels only in the request's Authorization header. What the provider keeps, and for how long, is set by its terms, not

Saved notes are included as data on a specialist call. `Forget` removes that note, advances the team epoch, and stops an active turn. After the recall-line change, a hit reads `{actor} · notes reused · {count} notes` and a miss reads `{actor} · notes loaded · {count} notes`.

**Jurisdiction.** This is the head agent’s charter field, labeled `Jurisdiction`, with the hint `What this agent is responsible for.` and the placeholder `What should this head agent be responsible for?` The roster shows that text under the head agent. A specialist row shows that specialist’s charter under the name. There is no separate Jurisdiction screen.

**Stage words.** The roster summary shows the stage. Display `head` as `Head agent`, `research` as `Research`, `review` as `Review`, `assemble` as `Assemble`, `work` as `Work`, and `verify` as `Check`. Stored specialist stages stay the five ids `research`, `review`, `assemble`, `work`, and `verify`. `verify` still writes a hash report and does not call a model. A review post still shows `Review approved` or `Changes requested`.

**The head agent.** The head agent is the name in `Head agent name`, default `Lead`, and that name becomes the session title. `To` lists the head agent first, and it is the default recipient. A message to the head agent can plan one to five specialists. A message addressed with `To`, or with

6a. Desktop revisions and folders (added with agent desktop changes)
- Files sit under their folder name, shown as a muted heading in the `Shared desktop` list. Files without a folder come first, with no heading.
- A file with more than one revision shows ` · v{n}` after its title. Only the newest revision of each file is listed.
- The reader's detail line adds the folder and `Revision {n}` when the file has other revisions.
- Under the label `Other revisions`, the reader lists each other revision as `Revision {n} · {title} · {author}`. Choosing one opens it.
- A rename or move shows in `Activity` as `Rename {old title}` or `File {old title}`.
- The demo files research under `Research` and guides under `Guides`. When the guide is supplied again, the demo assembler revises it and posts `I revised the guide; the earlier version stays in its history.`

6b. Persona library (added on owner request, 2026-11-22)
A persona is a saved specialist: name, Jurisdiction, voice, stage, and an optional model. The library belongs to the installation, so every head agent can use it.

- The left sidebar shows a `Personas` section under the workspace list. It has a `+ New` button and the hint `Saved specialists any head agent can recruit by name.`
- Each row reads `{name} · {Stage word}`, using the stage words in section 6. It has two text buttons: `Edit`, and `Add to team`. `Add to team` appears only while a team is open.
- `+ New` opens the dialog `New persona`. `Edit` opens `Edit {name}`. The fields are `Name`, `Jurisdiction` (placeholder `What is this specialist responsible for?`), `Voice` (placeholder `Clear and specific.`), `Stage` (`Research`, `Review`, `Assemble`, `Work`, `Check`) and `Model` (placeholder `Team model`, hint `Leave blank to use the team's model.`). The buttons are `Cancel` and `Save`. An edit also has `Delete`, which first asks `Delete {name} from the library? Teams that already recruited it keep their copy.`
- In the roster, each specialist's row has `Save as persona`, which opens `New persona` filled in from that specialist. A row with its own model shows that model as a hint line.
- The head agent sees the library when it plans. When it uses a persona's exact name, the saved Jurisdiction, voice, stage and model are used; the head only writes the assignment. The demo head recruits a saved persona for a matching sta

6c. Team memory and team-to-team questions (added on owner request, 2026-11-22)
Memory follows the recall distinctions: confirmed notes are kept apart from agent suggestions, and a team's own notes are kept apart from notes shared with every team.

- **Adding a note.** The `Save a team note` dialog gains two checkboxes. `Always use` is checked by default, with the hint `Turn off to use this note only when it matches the task.` `Share with every team` is unchecked by default.
- **Note rows.** Each note shows its text and one hint line built from: `Always used` or `Used when relevant`, `Shared with every team`, `Suggested by {agent}`, `Corrected`, and `Used {n} time` / `Used {n} times`. Each row has `Correct` and `Forget`.
- **Correct.** Opens the dialog `Correct a note`, label `What should the team remember instead?`, filled with the old text. Saving replaces the note. Like `Forget`, it withdraws everything built from the old note.
- **Suggestions.** Specialists can suggest up to two facts per handoff. They are listed under the heading `Suggested by agents`, with the hint `Agents never use a suggestion until you keep it.` Each row shows the text, the suggesting agent, `Keep` and `Dismiss`. `Keep` turns it into a note used when relevant. Forget or Correct clears pending suggestions.
- **Notes used.** In `Activity`, each specialist shows `{actor} · {used} of {considered} notes used`. Expanding it lists each note it received, prefixed `Always · ` or `Relevant · `.
- **Recall.** `

7. Leave out
- The section 6 request to name the team expanded field `cache write`. The word on that line is `write`.
- The sentence `A model call did not report tokens, so the token limit stopped the run.`
- A coding-session promise of ACP `usage_update`, `used`, `size`, USD, `this session`, or a child-session total.
- A context ring.
- Replacing the coding-session usage line with the team details block.
- An Allow button, or any approval card, on a team turn.
- A second cache control for notes.
- A new approval dialog. `Always allow` is a button on the current card.
- A local file picker, a live computer, a terminal, or an app preview in the Shared desktop pane. Agent-operated screens remain future work (`docs/architecture.md`); this edition does not claim them.
- The on-disk folder name and any absolute workspace path.
- A memory-engine screen or an intent-engine screen. The persona library is the sidebar section in section 6b, not a separate screen.
- Planner-prompt edits, README edits, server fallback renames, and test edits.
- Any string this review does not list. In particular, the empty-state paragraph, the note dialog, the source URL placeholder, and the six-file error stay.

# Bloom browser surface
These docs specify the Bloom browser surface so a new person can start a team or a coding session without a separate guide.

Source of truth
[The interface contract](interface-contract.md) is the source of truth for the next UI pass. A code agent copies its strings and its three behavior changes.

Its section 0 records the owner's decisions of 2026-11-22. They override both research files. `Head agent`, `Jurisdiction` and `Shared desktop` stay as names and gain plain helper text instead of being renamed.

Evidence
Two research files are the evidence behind the contract:

- [Implementability review](research/implementability-review.md). The coordinator approved this review. Section 7 is the include list and the leave-out list.
- [Familiar harness patterns](research/familiar-harness-patterns.md). This report is evidence. It is not a second include list. Where the report and the review disagree, the review wins. It once carried a section reading an unrelated third-party repository; that section is removed, and the note at the top of the report explains why.

What a code agent may change, and what it must leave alone
May change:

- Visible strings the contract lists as copy, and only those strings.
- The second empty-state button, `Create a coding session`, on the existing form.
- `allow_always` on the current approval card, with resolved title `Allowed always`.
- Hiding and clearing the path line on a team.

Must leave alone:

- Element ids, option values, stored stage ids, event names, and handlers.
- The repository README, both research files, tests, planner prompt text, and server fallback names.
- Strings the contract does not list.
- A team approval card, a second cache control for notes, and any new screen for memory, intent, or personas.
- The leave-out list in the contract.

# Familiar harness patterns for Bloom
> **Correction, 2026-11-22 (owner decision).** One section of this report read an unrelated third-party repository that presents itself under a name similar to that of a product Bloom follows ([how that product works](https://docs.x.ai/grok-bot/how-grok-bot-works), [shared computer](https://docs.x.ai/grok-bot/computer-and-apps), [group messaging](https://docs.x.ai/grok-bot/chat-and-collaboration)). That repository is not the product, and the section has been removed. Conclusions drawn from it, including the `Files` and `Lead name` renames, are set aside. The owner kept `Head agent`, `Jurisdiction` and `Shared desktop`; see section 0 of [the interface contract](../interface-contract.md). The rest of this report is unchanged.

Read on 2026-11-22. This report is evidence for a later reviewer. It separates what the pages and this checkout show from what Bloom should change.

Bloom should feel familiar on first open. The familiar gesture is: pick a place to work, type a task, watch the reply, and allow or reject a risky step. People already know the words task, files, team, allow, model, and usage. They do not know Jurisdiction, Head agent, Token stop threshold, or Shared desktop as names for those gestures.

1. What a new user already knows
OBSERVED across the pages opened on 2026-11-22:

- First run is a short path. Install or open the app, sign in if the product requires it, choose a folder or repository, and type a task in ordinary language. Cursor’s quickstart says to pick a folder and open Agent. Claude Code’s terminal quickstart says to `cd` into a project and run `claude`. Claude’s desktop quickstart says to choose Local and Open folder. Codex CLI says to run `codex` in a project and describe a task. GitHub Copilot’s task page says to pick a repository, type a prompt, and press Enter. OpenCode’s TUI page says to run `opencode` in the project and press Enter.
- Chat is the place the user types. It sits in a side pane (Cursor Agent, Cmd+I), under a prompt box (Claude desktop, Codex CLI, Copilot), or as a scrolling transcript with a fixed composer (OpenCode TUI).
- Files are the project. People attach them with `@` (Cursor, Claude desktop, OpenCode) or they let the agent search. A separate computer screen, live desktop, or preview is a second surface, present in some products and absent in others.
- Extra agents are created by asking in the task, by a named control such as Create an agent, or by a file the product already knows how to load. The user is rarely asked to invent a legal-sounding charter before the first message.
- Approvals are a pause with a short choice: allow this once, allow it again, or reject it. The words differ. The gesture does not.
- The model is a pick

2. Product-by-product observations
Each block is OBSERVED from the listed URL on 2026-11-22. No live app was opened. Where a page returned chrome or an illustration as text, that is stated. Screens that were not in the fetched text are not described.

### OpenCode

URLs opened:

- https://opencode.ai/docs/

Chat: the TUI transcript is the session. `@` attaches a file. `!` runs a shell command in the session. `/` opens commands. While a turn is running, Enter steers it. Tabs and `/sessions` return to earlier work. `session.sidebar` can be `auto` or `hide`. The settings page does not say the sidebar is a file tree.

Files: the working directory is the project. ACP `cwd` must be an absolute path. Additional directories can be granted. There is a `/diff` view with a file tree. The TUI page does not show a separate computer or desktop.

Agents: `/agents` or Shift+Tab cycles primary agents. Built-in primary agents are Build and Plan. Built-in subagents are General and Explore. A subagent is a Markdown file or

3. Bloom surface as it exists in this checkout
OBSERVED from `README.md`, `package.json`, `public/index.html`, `src/teams.mjs`, and the rendering in `public/app.js`, `public/team.js`, `src/opencode.mjs`, `src/harness.mjs`, and `src/team-store.mjs`. The page title is **bloom**. The package is `@vidoxlabs/bloom` 0.2.0, “A local-first web workspace for agent teams and shared artifacts.” The README still titles the product ViBloom and tells the reader to create a session and enter a project path. The browser form is the surface a person sees at the loopback port in the README.

The page is three columns.

- Left, aria-label **Workspaces**. **+ New** opens a form. **Workspace type** is **Agent team** or **Direct coding session**. Agent team is the form’s initial value. The submit button reads **Create team** until the type changes, then **Create session**.
- Center, aria-label **Group conversation**. The visible heading starts as **Workspace**. The transcript is the chat. The composer has a message box, a **Model** field, **Stop**, and **Send**.
- Right, aria-label **Inspector**. For a team it shows **Team**, **Shared desktop**, and **Team memory**, then **Run activity** for every workspace. Activity includes a turn state, `#usage`, a region labeled **Pending approvals**, **Agent plan**, and **Tool calls**.

Agent team form:

- **Head agent name**, default value **Lead**.
- **Jurisdiction**, placeholder “What should this head own?”
- A disclosure, **Model and budget**, containing

4. Familiarity map
OBSERVED gesture, then the Bloom pane that already receives it.

| Familiar gesture | Where it was seen | Bloom pane now |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Pick a folder, then type a task | Cursor quickstart, Claude desktop, Codex CLI directory line, Copilot repository dropdown, OpenCode `cwd` | **Direct coding session** → **Workspace directory**, then the center composer. The path shows under the session title. |
| Start a team by describing the teammates in the task | Claude agent teams; Cursor “coordinator agent”; Codex “specialized agents”; Copilot agent dropdown | **Agent team**. The first Send to the lead creates the roster. **To** addresses one member later. **Use research brief** is a sample of that sentence. |
| Chat in the center, work on the side | Claude prompt with optional file, diff, and browser panes; Cursor side pane or Agents Window | Center **Group conversation**. Right **Inspector**. Left **Workspaces**. |
| Attach files with a mention or a picker | Cursor `@`, Claude `@filename`, OpenCode `@`, Copilot `@` and the + menu | Team: check up to six rows, or paste a URL in the brief. Direct: no file checklist. The agent uses the workspace path. |
| Open a file the agent wrote | Cursor diff and checkpoints; Claude `+12 -1` diff; Codex “inspect diffs”; Copilot session changes | Transcript button **Open** plus the title, and **Open** on a desktop row. The reader is Markdown text, not a diff. |
| Watch a live computer or app preview | Claude Browser pane; C

5. Label changes worth making
RECOMMENDED. Each row names the control, the current text, and the change. Behavior changes are limited to what a code agent can do in the existing panes.

| `#sample-brief` | Use research brief | Try a sample t

6. Usage and cache
OBSERVED in Bloom:

- Team usage is visible only after the first `team.usage` event. The line already uses ordinary measurement words: input, output, cache read, cache write, and USD.
- “cache read” and “cache write” are prompt-cache token counts from `src/models.mjs`.
- “memory cache hit” is a different cache. `src/team-store.mjs` keeps notes in memory for up to 60 seconds. The activity row uses the word cache for that hit. A new user can read it as the same cache as the usage line.
- If the provider omits a total, the run stops when a token limit is set, and the summary says `(partial)`. The create form does not explain that.
- Direct coding sessions do not show usage. OpenCode’s ACP page does send `used`, `size`, and `cost`. Bloom’s OpenCode adapter does not currently put that update into `#usage`.
- There is no context ring and no “100% context left.”

OBSERVED elsewhere:

- Cursor shows a context ring and a category tray, including a summarized-conversation category. It does not show cache read or cache write on the pages opened.
- Codex CLI’s documented terminal example shows “100% context left.”
- OpenCode shows usage in the mini footer when that footer is on, and ACP can report used tokens against context size plus USD cost. Child-session tokens are called out as excluded.
- Claude Code can print a context percentage on a custom status line. The quickstart does not show one by default.
- Copilot’s opened pages point at billing. They do not show a se

7. Gaps and things that could not be verified
- No live app was opened. OpenCode Desktop, Cursor, Claude desktop, Codex, and GitHub were read as documentation. Pane positions that appear only in screenshots were not inspected. The Agents Window page has an image; its pixels were not reviewed.
- OpenCode’s intro names a desktop app and a web app. The opened docs describe the TUI, ACP, agents, permissions, and CLI settings. A desktop layout page was not found.
- Cursor pages opened do not show a pane named Composer. The context-ring categories were read. The subagents page and the models page were not read in full.
- Claude’s permission illustration did not come through as text. The prose names Yes, “Yes, and don’t ask again,” and sometimes “Yes, and switch to auto mode.” The subagents page was only partly read.
- `https://developers.openai.com/codex/app` returned the ChatGPT desktop app article. The overview rendering included “On my computer” and “Do anything.” A Codex computer pane was not documented there. CLI approval-button labels beyond “once” and “for the session” were not listed.
- Copilot approval button labels were not on the two pages opened. Billing pages were not opened, so premium-request counters are unverified as UI.
- The Anthropic article has no product chrome. Its feature-list JSON and progress file are harness behavior, not labels to copy onto Bloom’s panes.
- Bloom’s README and the browser disagree about the first screen. The README does not mention Team,

# Implementability review
> **Owner decision, 2026-11-22.** The adjudication "Shared desktop becomes Files" (section 4) and the `Lead name` / `Role` rows are overruled. The research behind them read an unrelated third-party repository; that evidence is removed. `Head agent`, `Jurisdiction` and `Shared desktop` stay, each with a helper line; see section 0 of [the interface contract](../interface-contract.md). All other verdicts stand.

Reviewed `docs/ui/research/familiar-harness-patterns.md` against the browser surface and the team, store, adapter, harness, and model modules. This file is the interface contract input. It does not change source.

1. Verdict
**approve**

The label set in research section 5 is coherent and specific enough for one contract. Three proposals need code: a second empty-state button, accepting `allow_always` on the existing approval card, and hiding the team workspace path. Two further rows are locks: team turns stay without an approval card, and team notes do not gain a second cache control.

Re-checked claims that hold:

- `src/opencode.mjs` sets `optionKinds` to `allow_once` and `reject_once` only. An option of any other kind is dropped. If none remain, the adapter returns a cancelled outcome.
- `src/teams.mjs` emits `team.usage` with `calls`, `limit`, `actor`, `model`, `usage`, `measuredTotal`, `incomplete`, and `tokenLimit`.

Research claims about this checkout that are false:

- “`src/opencode.mjs` does not emit a usage event.” After `session/prompt`, if `result.usage` is present, the adapter emits `model.usage` with `input`, `output`, `total`, `cacheRead`, and `cacheWrite`.
- “Only `team.usage` fills `#usage`,” “a direct turn does not write `#usage`,” and “Direct: the region stays empty.” `public/app.js` writes `#usage` on `model.usage`. `public/team.js` clears `#usage` on every `turn.started`, including a coding session, and the line appears when `model.usage` arrives.
- The team expanded line uses the word `write`. It does not use the words `cache write`. The coding-session line in `public/app.js` does use `Cache write`.
- “The README still titles the product ViBloom and tells the re

2. How a code agent should read the result
Read section 7 first. It is the include list and the leave-out list. The table is the evidence for that list.

- **copy change** means visible text only. Element ids, option values, stored stage ids, event names, and handlers stay. A row whose proposal already matches the screen is recorded and needs no edit.
- **behavior change** means logic, a new control, or a new event, and only where the note names that work. A note that starts with **Lock** is a sentence the contract includes. It adds no control.
- **reject** means the proposal stays out of the contract and out of the implementation.
- Copy the quoted strings exactly. Do not rename ids. Do not edit the research report, the README, planner prompt text, server fallback names, or tests as part of this contract.
- The browser surface is `public/index.html`, `public/app.js`, and `public/team.js`. Strings not listed in section 7 stay as they are.

3. Recommendation table
Section 5 and section 6. Repeated recommendations are one row.

| Control | Research proposal | Verdict | Evidence | Note |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `#kind` option `team` | Visible label `Team`. Value stays `team`. | copy change | `public/index.html`: `Agent team` | Label only. |
| `#kind` option `direct` | Visible label `Coding session`. Value stays `direct`. | copy change | `public/index.html`: `Direct coding session` | Label only. |
| `#create-session` when team | `Create team` | copy change | `public/team.js`: `Create team` | Already this text. Record it. |
| `#create-session` when direct | `Create coding session` | copy change | `public/team.js`: `Create session` | Label only, when the direct option is selected. |
| Empty heading | `What should we work on?` | copy change | `public/index.html`: `What should your team work on?` | The paragraph under the heading stays: `Give a head agent a brief. Follow the handoffs and open the files your team produces.` |
| `#empty-start` | Keep `Create a team`. Add `Create a coding session`, opening the same form with Coding session selected. | behavior change | `public/index.html` has one button, `Create a team`. `public/app.js` only opens the form. | One form. Primary sets kind `team`. Second button sets kind `direct` and runs the existing configure path. |
| `#head-name` label | `Lead name` | copy change | `public/index.html`: `Head agent name` | Label only. `checks/browser.mjs` also reads the current

4. Three adjudications
### Shared desktop becomes Files

Accept as a copy change. The inspector control is a file catalog: a checkbox list with a limit of six, **Open**, and a dialog for a title, a public link, or pasted text. Files the team writes appear in that list. It is not a live computer, a terminal, or an app preview. The product goal is a first screen a new person can understand, so the visible heading is **Files**.

The contract does not name the on-disk folder, quote a workspace path, or describe this pane as a computer. Hiding `#session-path` on a team is the behavior change that keeps that path off the team screen. Coding sessions still show the project path under the title. The session-list button’s title attribute is unchanged. `#team-inspector` stays hidden on a coding session, so Files is not added there.

The source dialog does not become a local file picker. **Add file** is the button and the source dialog title. **Link** is the URL label. **Or paste text** stays.

### OpenCode `allow_always` and Always allow

Accept as a behavior change. The current card can show an adapter label without a new dialog.

`public/app.js` `renderApproval` builds one card in `#approvals`: the title `Approval needed`, the request title, and one button per option. The button text is `option.label`. `src/opencode.mjs` sets that label from the ACP option name, truncated to 60 characters, or from the kind when the name is absent. The fixture name for `allow_always` is `Always allow`

5. Team turns have no approval card
Confirmed. A team turn does not produce the approval card.

`src/harness.mjs` takes the team path when the session adapter is `team`, calls `teams.run`, and returns before `adapter.run`. The permission callback that emits `permission.requested` is passed only to `adapter.run`. `src/teams.mjs` does not call that callback and does not emit `permission.requested`. The card is rendered only for `permission.requested`.

The contract keeps that absence. It does not add an Allow button on a team turn. A button there would approve nothing in this checkout.

Team HTTP generations are a separate provider path. They are not this card. This contract does not add a team permission control.

6. Plain-language mapping
These are the controls that exist. The contract may say what they already do.

**Notes.** The section is the note list. **Add note** opens the dialog `Save a team note`. Each note has **Forget**. Saved notes are included as data on a specialist call. **Forget** removes that note, advances the team epoch, and stops an active turn. After the recall-line change, a hit reads `{actor} · notes reused · {count} notes` and a miss reads `{actor} · notes loaded · {count} notes`.

**Role.** This is the lead’s charter field, relabeled **Role**, with the placeholder `What should this lead be responsible for?` The roster shows that text under the lead. A specialist row shows that specialist’s charter under the name. The contract does not add a separate Role screen.

**Stage words.** The roster summary shows the stage. Display `head` as `Lead`, `research` as `Research`, `review` as `Review`, `assemble` as `Assemble`, `work` as `Work`, and `verify` as `Check`. # Docs capabilities
This folder holds the hub's local capability ledger (`index.json`) and lead capability specifications (`CAP-NN-<slug>.md`).
Cross-repository milestones, dependencies, and the family ledger live in [the timeline guide](../timeline/README.md).
Same-PR ledger rule: every capability or contract PR updates `index.json`, the owning spec's `Evidence` and `Changes` sections, `docs/CHANGELOG.md`, and touched contract `Changes` sections in the same PR.

Context with its sources attached # Capillary Capillary is an open, local-first **context retrieval system** for agent workspaces. It records sources with their digests, retrieves **bounded, provenance-honest packets** of them, and keeps **typed relations** between the items it holds: the fine-channel work of lifting context up to the team that needs it, without letting prose smuggle in as fact. Agent surfaces like [Bloom](https://github.com/Vidoxlabs/bloom) consume capillary exactly where retrieving (and organizing) their source and context matters: a team brief admits sources, and specialists receive bounded excerpts that say what they are, where they came from, and what was shortened. Harness foundations like [Seed](https://github.com/Vidoxlabs/seed) admit capillary's retrieval tools to their runs and record each retrieval as an intent. **Status: `1.3.0`, retrieval contracts and library modules.** The retrieval seam, source recording, and relation contracts are implemented and covered by `npm test`. The backing stores (index, service) are specified, not shipped. Nothing in this repository opens a network listener or retrieves over the network today.

What is here today (`implemented`)
| Module | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `src/provenance.mjs` | Records source digests, origins, evidence classes and confidence, and records why sources are unknown |
| `src/packet.mjs` | Builds bounded context packets with **declared** truncation, budgeted admission, declared unknown sources, and relevance and recency kept as separate fields |
| `src/epoch-guard.mjs` | Refuses a packet when the deletion epoch at the end of a read differs from the epoch at its start, or cannot be read |
| `src/read.mjs` | Reads caller-supplied text under an estimated token budget and declares truncation in an untrusted envelope |
| `src/search.mjs` | Searches caller-supplied records for literal matches and reports recency and snippet cuts in an untrusted envelope |
| `src/conversation.mjs` | Shapes one conversation's thread, a recent list, a brief of the newest operator intent and verified outcome, and an envelope around the parent walk, all from caller-supplied records |
| `src/relations.mjs` | Typed, append-only relations and bounded walks over supplied parent links |

`npm install && npm test` verifies all of it. No runtime dependencies.

Contracts
- [Bounded retrieval](docs/contracts/retrieval.md): the packet, its budgets, declared shortening, declared omissions
- [Provenance](docs/contracts/retrieval.md): digests and origin classes on every source

How capillary fits the systems (`specified`)
The botanic line, per [docs/systems.md](docs/systems.md): **seed** (the foundation a runtime
grows from) → **capillary** (these channels, lifting context to it) → **myosotis**
(governed memory: consent, keep, and forget) → **aestivation** (the bud's arrangement,
admission and review before assembly) → **drosera** (the sundew's tentacles: tools,
skills, hooks, cookbooks) → **bloom** (the opened team workspace), with the whole line
growing against **trellis** (the testing lattice that keeps every member honest).

Capillary owns retrieval and organization only. Remembering with consent is the memory
fabric's job (forget is a promise there, not a default); deciding what gets admitted into
runs and what assembles is the gate's job. [docs/interop.md](docs/interop.md) draws each
seam.

Documentation
- [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md): start here before editing. Stay in this repository's province.
- [Charter](docs/charter.md): mission, principles, non-goals
- [Architecture](docs/architecture.md): sources, index, packets, relations
- [Contracts](docs/contracts/retrieval.md): bounded retrieval and provenance
- [Relations contract](docs/contracts/relations.md): typed, append-only context relations
- [Interop](docs/interop.md): Bloom, Seed, and the memory seam
- [Systems](docs/systems.md): the botanic naming line

# Architecture decision records
Architecture decision records for `capillary` live in this directory and follow the [Vidoxlabs/docs ADR convention](https://github.com/Vidoxlabs/docs/blob/main/docs/adr/README.md).

- Number ADR files sequentially from `0001` using the filename `NNNN-<slug>.md` (starting at `0001`).
- Valid statuses are `Proposed`, `Accepted`, `Superseded by NNNN`, and `Deferred`.
- Agents propose ADRs as `Proposed`; only an owner decision moves an ADR to `Accepted`.
- Any runtime dependency proposal requires an ADR here before adding a package.

# Capillary architecture
Status: `specified`; modules named below exist (`implemented`) where marked.

The four parts
1. **Sources** (`implemented as records` in `src/provenance.mjs`) — the corpus is an
   append-only set of recorded sources: an id, a title, a 64-hex digest, an origin class
   (`url`, `repository`, `text`, `workspace-file`, `run-artifact`), and an origin
   reference, plus the claim's evidence class and confidence. A source whose digest
   is unavailable is recorded as unknown with a null digest and its reason
   (`not-found`, `read-failed`, `digest-unavailable`). The packet lists it under `unknown`.
2. **The index** (`specified`) — lexical and semantic recall over recorded sources. The
   index is a projection: it is rebuilt from sources, never an authority. A search that
   misses is reported as a miss with its coverage stated; it is never padded.
3. **The packet builder** (`implemented` in `src/packet.mjs`) — retrieval's output
   artifact: a bounded set of excerpt items, each carrying its source id and digest, a
   `shortened` flag with the carried and cut sizes, and a declared budget accounting.
   Admission is ordered and deterministic; what does not fit is listed as omitted, never
   dropped silently.
4. **The relation ledger** (`implemented as records` in `src/relations.mjs`) — typed,
   append-only records linking known sources: the organization half of context work.
   `derived-from`, `references`, `subsumes`, `revised-from`, `relates-to`. The ledger is
   an event history: appended to, never rewritten. `walkParentChain` follows explicit
   parent id

The retrieval seam
```
sources -> index (projection) -> ranked candidate items
        -> packet builder (budgets, truncation, admission)
        -> packet -> the requesting run or workspace
```

Every crossing is stateable to a reviewer:

- *Which sources* were considered and read (ids, digests).
- *Which excerpts* were admitted, in what sizes, with what cut.
- *Which items* the budgets left out.
- *Why* — the budgets and the order are part of the packet.

Neurology of the systems
Capillary decides nothing. It serves retrieval to the layers that decide:

- Runs (a seed objective) admit retrieval tools and record each call as an intent.
- Teams (a bloom turn) attach sources to a task and receive the bounded packets.
- The memory fabric (the myosotis-to-be) is a different organ: it remembers with
  consent and forgets on demand; capillary never copies its role.
- The admission and review loop (the aestivation-to-be) gates assembly; capillary
  hands it exact evidence, never verdicts.

While the public counterparts of those systems are in the works, capillary's contracts
stand alone: `myosotis`, `aestivation`, and capillary are peers with separate
provinces, and the seams are contracts, not assumptions.

What capillary refuses to own
- No verdicts. Retrieval reports; admission decides.
- No remembrance. Provenance and relations, never consent or recall policy.
- No quiet defaults. Budgets, truncation, and misses are declared on the packet.
- No living index. Every projection is rebuildable from sources.

# CAP-05: Codebase-to-context packer
- ID: `CAP-05`
- Title: Codebase-to-context packer
- Lead: `capillary`
- Touches: `drosera`, `bloom`, `trellis`
- Horizon: Now (library slices), Next (composer slices)
- Milestone: M2 (library slices), M3 (composer slices)
- CLI phase: `P3`
- Status: `proposed`
- Claim: `planned`
- Depends on: `CAP-03`, `CAP-04`

Why
Agent coding runs and workspace briefs need a single, reproducible view of a codebase that fits inside context budgets without leaking secrets, truncating silently, or misreporting missing repository state as empty.
By separating pure selection, ordering, budgeting, and rendering inside `capillary` from filesystem traversal and read-only `git` execution in `bloom`, every packed codebase context remains deterministic, inspectable by digest, and safe against untrusted file content.

What it does
1. **Pure selection over caller-supplied path lists**:
   - Accepts caller-supplied relative path lists, file metadata, ignore-file rules, overrides, and file byte buffers without performing disk or network I/O inside `capillary`.
   - Applies include and exclude globs supporting `*`, `**`, `?`, character classes (such as `[a-z]` and `[!0-9]`), and brace lists (such as `{mjs,json}`). Exclude always wins over include, and an empty include list means include all non-excluded paths.
   - Evaluates ignore-file rules scoped per directory with `#` comments, `!` negation (restoring a previously ignored file), trailing `/` for directory-only matches, and leading `/` anchored to the ignore file's directory; ignore evaluation is switchable on or off by the caller.
   - Excludes hidden paths (segments starting with `.`) by default, switchable by the caller.
   - Enforces an always-on secret-file deny list covering environment files (`.env` and variants), private keys and certificates, credential stores, key files, and token caches. Explicit include rules or path overrides for a denied path are refused unless an explicit per-call `CAP-06.1` owner approval permits that path (pending owner decision `D10`), and the refusal is recorded as omission reason `denied`.
   - Supports manual per-path force-include and force-exclude overrides within the deny-list rule above.
   - Performs binary sniffing over caller-supplied bytes (detecting NUL bytes or non-text byte patterns) and omit

Contract touchpoints
- `docs/contracts/retrieval.md`: Extends `capillary`'s bounded retrieval contract additively. Admitted codebase files and diffs map to `recordSource` (`origin: 'workspace-file'` or `'repository'`, `evidenceClass: 'tool-observation'`, `confidence: 'direct-tool'`), failed reads and absent `git` output map to `recordUnknownSource` (`unknown` list), and file payloads inherit the `untrusted: true` envelope rule. Token budgeting (`estimate`) and additive packer omission reasons (`excluded`, `ignored`, `hidden`, `denied`, `binary`) are documented alongside existing `BLOOM_BASELINE` character limits and `OMISSION_REASONS` (`out-of-budget`, `unknown-source`), reusing `out-of-budget` when budget is exhausted without breaking `1.3.0` packet callers.
- `docs/contracts/relations.md`: Packed outputs and derived summaries can link back to admitted source file digests through `derived-from` relation records audited by `isSoundLedger`.

Tool IDs and events
### Tool IDs

| Tool ID | Effect | Owner gate | Purpose |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `workspace.tree.list` | `read` | `false` | Return deterministic directory tree for selected or full workspace paths |
| `context.repo.pack.read` | `read` | `false` | Build bounded codebase context packet and rendered output under token budget |
| `context.budget.verify` | `read` | `false` | Compute per-file largest-first token map and per-extension totals without packing bodies |
| `vcs.repo.diff.read` | `read` | `false` | Read working-tree or ref-to-ref diff as provenance-tagged observation or unknown |
| `vcs.repo.log.read` | `read` | `false` | Read ref-to-ref commit log as provenance-tagged observation or unknown |

### Events

| Event | Emitted by | Payload summary |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `context.packet` | `bloom` | Packet counts, omission and unknown tallies by reason, estimated token budget summary, source SHA-256 digests, and rendered output SHA-256 digest (never raw file or diff contents) |

Acceptance tests
- `exclude-wins-over-include`: When a path matches both include and exclude globs, exclude wins; when include is empty, all non-excluded paths remain eligible.
- `ignore-negation-restores-file`: Ignore-file comments, trailing directory slashes, anchored leading slashes, per-directory scoping, and `!` negation rules evaluate deterministically and restore negated paths when enabled.
- `hidden-off-by-default`: Dot-prefixed files and directories are omitted with reason `hidden` unless hidden inclusion is explicitly enabled.
- `secret-file-denied-even-when-included`: Environment files, private key/certificate files, credential stores, key files, and token caches are refused even under explicit include or manual override unless a per-call `CAP-06.1` owner approval permits them, and are recorded as omitted with `denied`.
- `binary-omitted-with-reason`: Binary byte sequences are detected by sniff and omitted with reason `binary` without entering rendered text.
- `byte-identical-output-for-identical-input`: Repeated runs with identical inputs and options produce byte-identical rendered strings and identical output SHA-256 digests across `markdown`, `tagged`, and `json`.
- `budget-omits-with-reason`: Candidates exceeding the estimated token budget are omitted with reason `out-of-budget` in deterministic order, with total estimated tokens labeled `estimate`.
- `token-map-largest-first`: The returned token map lists admitted files sorted largest estimated tokens first wi

Slices
- `CAP-05.1` (`capillary`, `M2`, `proposed`): Selection engine: globs, ignore rules, deny list, overrides, binary sniff.
- `CAP-05.2` (`capillary`, `M2`, `proposed`): Ordering, tree render, format-aware readers, budget, and token map.
- `CAP-05.3` (`capillary`, `M2`, `proposed`): Render formats, placeholder template, untrusted envelope, and packet output.
- `CAP-05.4` (`drosera`, `M2`, `proposed`): Packer tool faces, map-first exploration skill, and recipe.
- `CAP-05.5` (`bloom`, `M3`, `proposed`): Workspace file walker, read-only git context executor, and bloom pack CLI.
- `CAP-05.6` (`bloom`, `M3`, `proposed`): Coding loop context-step integration and context.packet event.
- `CAP-05.7` (`trellis`, `M3`, `proposed`): Packer behavior and determinism probes.

Non-goals
- Walking the host filesystem, following symlinks, or spawning `git` inside `capillary` (`capillary` stays pure over caller-supplied inputs).
- Vector embeddings, semantic ranking, or network retrieval.
- Exact model-family tokenization requiring runtime dependencies (`capillary` keeps zero runtime dependencies).
- Template scripting languages, conditionals, loops, or helper function execution in custom templates.
- Writing files or altering repository state during pack operations.

Family rules and conflicts
- **Pure library boundary**: `capillary` never imports `drosera`, `myosotis`, `aestivation`, or `bloom`, and performs no disk or subprocess I/O. Filesystem walking and read-only `git` invocation live in `bloom`; tool faces, skills, and recipes live in `drosera`; schema grammar lives in `seed`; behavioral probes live in `trellis`.
- **Zero runtime dependencies**: Globs, ignore matching, binary sniffing, format-aware parsing, token estimation, and template substitution are implemented with Node built-ins only.
- **Unknowns fail closed**: Unreadable files, unfollowed symlinks, and missing `git` stay `unknown` rather than empty results.
- **Public safety**: Secret deny lists block credential artifacts by default; trace events carry digests and counts only; rendered paths never expose host root paths.
- **Contract harmony**: Existing `src/packet.mjs` defines `OMISSION_REASONS = ['out-of-budget', 'unknown-source']` and `BLOOM_BASELINE` character limits (`28000` / `12000`). Packer extensions must remain additive so `1.3.0` retrieval contract callers remain unchanged.

Open owner decisions
- **D5 (pending owner decision)**: Confirm the character-based token estimation rule and `estimate` label convention across packed packets and `context.budget.verify` (exact token counts only from the configured provider at run time, never in tests; e.g., 4 Unicode code points per estimated token matching `readSource`).
- **D6 (pending owner decision)**: Confirm the template model: built-in `markdown`, `tagged`, and `json` formats plus a placeholder-only custom template restricted exclusively to the six placeholder tokens (`{{tree}}`, `{{files}}`, `{{diff}}`, `{{log}}`, `{{budget}}`, `{{omissions}}`) with no template logic or conditionals.
- **D9 (pending owner decision)**: Confirm that `bloom` calls the system `git` binary read-only for working-tree/ref diffs and commit logs (`CAP-05.5`), recording absent or failing `git` as `unknown` and never as an empty diff.
- **D10 (pending owner decision)**: Confirm that the secret-file deny list stays always on, explicit includes of denied paths require a per-call `CAP-06.1` owner approval record, and symlink following stays disabled by default in `bloom`'s walker.
- **D14 (pending owner decision)**: Confirm review conventions made under delegation for `CAP-05`: reusing existing `out-of-budget` from `OMISSION_REASONS` alongside additive packer omission reasons (`excluded`, `ignored`, `hidden`, `denied`, `binary`) and `BLOOM_BASELINE` character caps, plus `M2` (`CAP-05.1` to `CAP-05.4`) and `M3` (`CAP-05.5` to `CAP

Evidence
- `test/codebase-context.test.mjs` exercises scoped selection, denied inputs, format-aware excerpts, deterministic budgets, and untrusted renderers over caller-supplied bytes.

None yet (`status: proposed`, `claim: planned`). Test outputs, probe receipts, and commit SHAs will be recorded here as slices `CAP-05.1` through `CAP-05.7` land.

Changes
- 2026-11-24. Add pure codebase selection, context budgeting, and packet rendering (CAP-05, capillary#3).

- `2026-11-23`: Initial capability specification drafted for `CAP-01` timeline scaffold.
- `2026-11-23`: Reused `out-of-budget` from `OMISSION_REASONS`, aligned canonical `D5`/`D6`/`D9`/`D10`/`D14` decision references and `CAP-06.1` override reference, and added `M2`/`M3` slice milestones (`CAP-01`, review fixes).

# CAP-18: Symbol outline for packed context
- ID: `CAP-18`
- Title: Symbol outline for packed context
- Lead: `capillary`
- Touches: `drosera`, `bloom`
- Horizon: later
- Milestone: M8
- CLI phase: none
- Status: `proposed`
- Claim: `planned`
- Depends on: `CAP-05`

Why
When exploring a large workspace under tight token budgets, reading whole files wastes packet capacity on implementation details when callers only need structural navigation: exported bindings, functions, classes, document headings, or JSON object keys with line ranges.
Adding a zero-dependency symbol outline extractor inside `capillary` keeps packed context compact while obeying retrieval honesty: any file format outside the supported parser set stays explicitly `unknown` instead of emitting an empty symbol list.

What it does
- **Zero-dependency parsers in `capillary`**: Extracts structural outlines from caller-supplied relative path, format hint, and UTF-8 source text without external parser dependencies:
  - **JavaScript** (`.js`, `.mjs`, `.cjs`): extracts `exports` (named, default, re-exports), `functions` (declarations and top-level function bindings), and `classes`, each with symbol name, kind, and 1-based `{ startLine, endLine }` range.
  - **Markdown** (`.md`): extracts headings with level (`1` to `6`), heading text, and 1-based line range.
  - **JSON** (`.json`): validates structure and extracts top-level (and optionally depth-bounded) keys with 1-based line ranges; malformed JSON reports `unknown` (`read-failed` or `parse-failed`), never an empty key list.
- **Packet outline section**: Attaches extracted outlines as a structured section inside `CAP-05` packed context outputs (`markdown`, `tagged`, and `json` renderers), keeping relative paths only, source SHA-256 digests, and the untrusted-content boundary around extracted names and headings.
- **Explicit `unknown` fallback**: For any file language or format outside JavaScript, Markdown, and JSON (or for binary/unparseable content), returns `status: 'unknown'` with an explicit reason instead of an empty outline array.
- **Drosera tool face**: Defines `workspace.file.outline.read` (`effect: 'read'`, `ownerGate: false`) in `drosera` with `CAP-03` input and output schemas.
- **Bloom executor**: Reads workspace file bytes inside

Contract touchpoints
- `docs/contracts/retrieval.md`: Extends `CAP-05` packet output additively with an optional `outlines` section carrying relative `originRef`, 64-hex SHA-256 source digest, `untrusted: true` framing, and explicit `unknown` records whenever a file cannot be parsed or its language is unsupported.

Tool IDs and events
### Tool IDs

| Tool ID | Effect | Owner gate | Purpose |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `workspace.file.outline.read` | `read` | `false` | Extract JS exports, functions, and classes, Markdown headings, or JSON keys with line ranges, or return unknown |

### Events

| Event | Emitted by | Payload summary |
| --- | --- | --- |
| (none added) | `bloom` | Reuses `CAP-05` `context.packet` event digests and counts when outlines are included in a pack |

Acceptance tests
- `js-outline-extracts-exports-functions-classes-with-line-ranges`: Extracts exports, functions, and classes with accurate 1-based line ranges from JavaScript text with zero runtime dependencies.
- `markdown-outline-extracts-headings-with-levels-and-lines`: Extracts Markdown headings with heading levels and 1-based line numbers.
- `json-outline-extracts-keys-with-line-ranges`: Extracts JSON keys with line ranges and reports `unknown` when JSON input is malformed.
- `unsupported-language-reports-unknown-never-empty`: Any non-JS, non-Markdown, non-JSON format or binary payload reports `status: 'unknown'` with reason and never returns an empty symbol outline as success.
- `outline-section-uses-relative-paths-and-untrusted-envelope`: Packed outline sections emit relative paths only, record source digests, and sit inside the untrusted-content envelope.
- `workspace-file-outline-read-validates-and-executes`: `workspace.file.outline.read` validates under `seed` grammar, registers in `drosera`, and executes inside `bloom`'s workspace root guard.

Slices
- `CAP-18.1` (`capillary`, `M8`, `proposed`): Zero-dependency JS, Markdown, and JSON symbol outline parser and unknown fallback.
- `CAP-18.2` (`drosera`, `M8`, `proposed`): Outline reader tool face definition and schema.
- `CAP-18.3` (`bloom`, `M8`, `proposed`): Symbol outline executor and packer wiring.

Non-goals
- Runtime dependencies on AST or tree-sitter parser packages.
- Supporting languages beyond JavaScript, Markdown, and JSON in this capability (unsupported formats stay `unknown`).
- Cross-file type resolution, semantic symbol linking, or code indexing.
- Filesystem traversal inside `capillary`.

Family rules and conflicts
- **Zero runtime dependencies**: Outlines are parsed solely with zero-dependency JavaScript in `capillary`.
- **Unknown stays unknown**: Unsupported file extensions and malformed files never masquerade as empty outlines.
- **Province separation**: `capillary` performs pure parsing and packet assembly; `drosera` owns the `workspace.file.outline.read` face; `bloom` performs workspace reads and invokes the packer; `seed` validates the tool ID and `CAP-03` schemas.

Open owner decisions
None new for `CAP-18`; inherits `CAP-05` packer decisions (`D5`, `D6`, `D9`, `D10`, `D14`) and `CAP-03` schema parity (`D4`).

Evidence
None yet (`status: proposed`, `claim: planned`). Code, test receipts, and commit SHAs will be recorded here as slices `CAP-18.1` through `CAP-18.3` land.

Changes
- `2026-11-23`: Initial capability specification drafted for `CAP-01` timeline scaffold.
- `2026-11-23`: Standardized `Horizon: later`, added `M8` slice milestones, and aligned inherited `CAP-05` decision references (`CAP-01`, review fixes).
