# ADR 0002: Adopt pinned family peers

- Status: Accepted
- Date: 2026-11-24

## Context

Bloom composes the family's contracts and implementations. Drosera owns tool
faces, Capillary owns retrieval and packing, and Aestivation owns plan admission
and review. Each peer ships without runtime dependencies.

## Decision

D15 permits Bloom to adopt these peers as their slices require them. Use full
commit SHAs and record pending upstream merges. Reconcile each pin to the merged
upstream commit on the next touch after merge.

Owner's answer, verbatim: "Assume D15 approval and continue working on CAP-04.2".

## Changes

- 2026-11-24: CAP-04.2 pins Drosera at `033f2907c4cdbcd43598d3087992a1ae1850a531` (drosera#4, pending upstream merge) for workspace and finish faces (CAP-04, bloom#4).

docsPages.body:
# How Bloom works

Bloom runs as one Node.js webserver with an embedded SQLite database, a directory of Markdown artifacts and a browser client. One head owns a team conversation. Every group post names its author. Durable sequence numbers let a disconnected browser replay activity. A model adapter supplies generations. The harness decides which files to read, which specialist owns the next step and when to stop.

## Terminal shell

**Implemented.** The terminal shell shares the team loop, demo adapter, provider selection and SQLite event stream with the browser. Headless JSON ends with an unstored `run.result` record. Missing usage stays unreported. The terminal reads provider addresses from its private data directory configuration. A configured address is masked before events are stored or rendered. Session exports also mask the stored workspace path. File replay reads the exported events without opening a store or starting a runtime.

## The shared computer

Grok Bot’s published design gives a user one persistent cloud computer. The bots share files and browser state, have individual screens, and can hand tasks to another bot in a group. Its primary bot can create specialists. Each responding bot consumes usage. These are product behaviors described by xAI. Its internal prompts and scheduling algorithms are proprietary. [How Grok Bot works](https://docs.x.ai/grok-bot/how-grok-bot-works) · [Shared computer](https://docs.x.ai/grok-bot/computer-and-apps) · [Group messaging](https://docs.x.ai/grok-bot/chat-and-collaboration)

Bloom implements the shared-computer idea locally. Every team can discover ordinary files from the same desktop. Each output gets an immutable ID, a readable filename, a hash and directed input edges. Specialists can change files they were given: a revision, rename or move into a folder writes a new immutable file in the same revision chain, linked to the version it replaces. The desktop lists the newest revision each team may see, and every earlier revision stays readable. A revision derived from team notes is private to that team, so other teams keep the last shareable revision, and Forget withdraws it. Folders are catalog metadata; files on disk stay flat. The shell and browser in the optional graphical desktop belong to the user. Agent-controlled mouse, keyboard, separate screens and browser-login handoff are future integrations. The OS account remains the trust boundary.

## Agent and memory contracts

| Concept | Local implementation |
| --- | --- |
| VI (Virtual Intelligence) | The head holds a name and charter. The planner assigns work by name to saved personas or current team members. Bloom drops unknown names and stops when no assignment matches. Recruiting a persona copies its saved jurisdiction, voice, stage and optional model onto the team. The scripted demo supplies its own example profiles. |
| OAI (Open AI Instance) | A provider-backed generation fulfills a role. The same profile can run on another configured model, and a persona with a preferred model runs on it. Each dispatch owns its input and reports its usage independently. |
| LA (Logical Agent) | The head can assign the verify stage to a named deterministic worker. It re-reads the admitted files and verifies their hashes without spending a model call. |
| Memory recall | Memory keeps the recall distinctions apart. Owner-confirmed notes are either rules, which always apply, or facts, recalled only when they match the task. A note belongs to one team or is shared with every team on the installation. Agent suggestions stay unconfirmed and are never recalled until the owner keeps them. Correct supersedes a note; Correct and Forget both move the epoch of every team that could use the note, so derived files and pending suggestions are withdrawn. Recall ranks notes with a portable floatation reading (`synaptic.score.v1`): lexical relevance in place of vector similarity (0.45), provenance (0.15), confidence (0.08), logarithmic use mass (0.07), a 30-day freshness half-life (0.05) and usefulness (0.05, +0.08 per approved review). A near-duplicate filter applies, with at most eight notes and 2,000 characters per call. Each call records which notes it received. Reading evidence or posting a message creates no durable note. |
| Local roles | Three logical roles run locally. SQLite holds authoritative records and provenance edges. A bounded in-process TTL cache serves the hot note set, and ranking runs per call. File-to-file edges connect inputs with resulting artifacts. There is no external graph or cache daemon to install. |
| Ordered plan and review | The head proposes an ordered plan. A deterministic rule validates the response and the stage order. A reviewer records approve or revise. A revision verdict stops automatic assembly. These are the admission and review behaviors implemented in this edition. |
| Event history | An append-only event history records roles, calls, review decisions and artifact references for inspection. The team receives bounded group posts and selected artifacts. Ambient development telemetry is outside the model’s context. |

These are portable implementations of selected Vidoxlabs behaviors. Full semantic ranking, multi-store replication and the historical seven-stage transport are outside this release. Public background on each behavior is available in the corresponding system's own public documentation.

## Teams talk to each other

A head agent sees the other teams on the installation by name and jurisdiction. It may ask one of them one question per task. Bloom opens a turn in the other team's conversation, so that team shows as busy, cannot start its own task meanwhile, and can stop the answer. The other team's head answers once from shareable material only: its jurisdiction, notes shared with every team, its unscoped group posts and its shareable desktop titles. Private notes never cross a team boundary. The asking head sees no notes, so its question cannot carry them either. The answering head sees no other teams, so a question cannot be passed along. The question and answer are recorded in both conversations' event histories. The answer reaches the asking team's specialists, labelled as coming from another team. The asking team's call and token limits cover the answer.

## Model calls and evidence

The head receives the brief, roster and ordinary desktop file titles. Worker calls receive the jurisdiction, explicit assignment, the ranked notes admitted for that assignment, recent group handoffs (including answers from other teams) and attached evidence. The text budget for all file excerpts in a worker packet is 28,000 characters, with a per-file cap of 12,000 characters. Character caps protect packet size. The usage ledger uses provider-reported token counts. Stable system instructions precede the changing evidence, allowing supporting providers to reuse their prompt prefix.

A team provider implements `generate({system, prompt, model, signal, ...})` and returns `{text, complete, model, usage, costUSD}`. `text` is always a string; a reply with no text body is returned as an empty, incomplete record. `usage` holds token counts only, in five fields: `input`, `output`, `total`, `cacheRead` and `cacheWrite`. A reported monetary cost is `costUSD`, beside usage rather than inside it. Missing metrics use null. Since 0.7.0 Bloom imports seed and runs every team provider behind its provider seam (`src/provider.mjs`): seed's `validateProvider` checks the adapter when Bloom starts, and seed's `normalizeGeneration` checks every reply before the team loop reads it. A reply outside the record stops the turn with `PROVIDER_CONTRACT`. Seed's record has no money field, so Bloom carries a reported `costUSD` beside it. `test/generation-record.test.mjs` holds both halves. A custom provider that still puts `costUSD` inside usage is now refused. Bloom ships one network adapter, for chat completions, with no default service: the private `config.json` in the data directory names the endpoint and the environment variable that holds its key, for the terminal and the web workspace alike. Chat completions commonly includes cached reads in its input count. Bloom keeps the provider’s reported total and never converts absent usage into a monetary saving. Without an endpoint, team turns stop with `PROVIDER_UNCONFIGURED`.

Stopping or losing a server never implicitly repeats a model call. In-progress team outputs appear only after the model returns a complete structured response. A coding session runs on a pluggable runtime: `run(input, hooks)` streams text, plan and tool events, asks for approvals through the harness and returns a stop reason. Bloom offers each option the runtime sends, such as **Allow once**, **Always allow** and **Reject**. The coding loop is the runtime for `--workspace` sessions; the scripted runtime is demo-only.

## Workspace tools

`src/workspace-tools.mjs` binds Drosera's workspace tool pack to the canonical
session directory from `workspacePath`. Its file tools check relative paths
and resolved link targets before content I/O. A recursive text search
visits regular workspace files in path order. Directory output and search
matches use workspace-relative names.

Writes queue by canonical path in the Bloom process and replace the target
atomically. A targeted update needs one exact match, including the check for
overlapping matches. Command execution uses the canonical workspace as its
working directory and takes an executable and arguments without shell
expansion. Bloom forwards `PATH`, `LANG`, and `TERM`. Each command gets a fresh
temporary `HOME`, and `USERPROFILE` on Windows, outside the workspace and the
user's home. Bloom removes it after the run. The command deadline
stops output capture and terminates the launched process. On POSIX it targets
the process group. Commands run under the local OS account and the coding
adapter owns the approval and dispatch flow.
Commands are off by default. The executor runs `workspace.shell.execute` only
when it is created with the `workspaceCommandAccess` symbol, which
`src/workspace-tools.mjs` exports and only `src/coding-loop.mjs` passes (a
guard test checks this). There is no test-only command mode: tests use the
same allowlisted gate.

The executor returns `output`, `truncatedBytes`, and `outputSha256`. It keeps a
UTF-8 prefix ending at a complete code point and hashes the full decoded text
before truncation. For commands, stdout and stderr contribute in observed
order, and a timeout reports the text captured up to the deadline alongside
`timedOut` and a null `exitCode`.

## Coding loop

**Implemented.** `src/coding-loop.mjs` is a coding runtime on the harness seam
`run(input, hooks)`. `bloom chat --workspace PATH` and `bloom run --headless
--workspace PATH` use it when no `--team` is named, and the browser workspace
lists it as a runtime when an endpoint is configured. Every model call runs
behind `src/provider.mjs`, so seed's `normalizeGeneration` checks each record.

Each model reply holds a short note and exactly one fenced json block,
`{ "tool": "<tool id>", "args": { } }`. Parsing is strict. Bloom checks the tool
against the admitted tools and the arguments against the face `inputSchema`
with seed's `validateValue`, and checks a result against an `outputSchema` when
the face declares one. Argument and output checks share one repair turn; a
call that runs resets it. A second failure stops the turn as `malformed`, and
nothing malformed runs. A reply the model did not finish (`complete: false`)
counts as malformed. `run.answer.create` ends the turn with `turn.finished`.

Read tools run without a prompt. `workspace.file.write`, `workspace.file.update`
and `workspace.shell.execute` raise `permission.requested` first, showing the
full content, the edit, or the command with every argument verbatim. A
rejection never executes, and the model is told "denied by owner". "Allow this
exact call for the session" binds the tool ID plus a SHA-256 digest of the
arguments, and is never offered for `workspace.shell.execute`. A headless run
refuses every write and command without asking.

The client streams when it passes a delta callback: `stream: true`, with the
server-sent events read into `assistant.delta` as they arrive. A reply is
complete only on `finish_reason: "stop"`, usage is `null` when the server does
not report it, never `0`, and an abort rejects so no completed record exists.
Streamed text passes the endpoint redactor with a held-back tail, so an address
split across chunks is still masked.

The trace has one `model.call` row per generation (duration and usage, or
"usage unreported") and one `tool.updated` row per tool call: time, tool ID, a
short argument summary (paths, queries and the command, never file contents),
the result status, bytes or the exit code, and the duration in milliseconds.
Command rows carry the tail of the command output.

### Command gate

Before a command runs outside tests, all of these hold:

1. Only `node`, `npm` and `git` run, by exact name, resolved against the search
   path fixed when the tools are created. Relative entries and entries inside the
   workspace are skipped. A command containing `/`, `\`, `..`, a drive letter
   or an absolute path is refused, and so are `sh`, `bash`, `cmd` and `powershell`.
   On Windows a name that resolves to a `.cmd` or `.bat` file is refused, because
   it needs a shell.
2. Arguments that are absolute, start with `~`, contain a `..` segment, have a
   drive or UNC root, or start with `file:` are refused, and the same check
   applies to the value in `--flag=value` and to the remainder of an attached
   short option such as `-O<path>`. An argument is resolved through the nearest
   existing ancestor and through links, so a new file under a linked folder
   outside the workspace is refused.
3. Evaluation and redirection are refused: for `node`, `-e`, `--eval`, `-p`,
   `--print`, `-r`, `--require`, `--import`, `--input-type`, `--loader`,
   `--experimental-loader`, `--run` and any short option cluster holding `e`,
   `p` or `r`; for `npm`, `exec`, `x`, `explore`, `edit`, `--prefix`, `-C`,
   `-g`, `--global`, `--location`, `--script-shell`, `--node-options`,
   `--offline`, `--no-offline`, `--prefer-online`, `--registry`, `--userconfig`,
   `--globalconfig`, `--cache`, `--proxy` and `--https-proxy`; for `git`, `-C`,
   `--git-dir`, `--work-tree`, `-c` and `--exec-path`, with the subcommand limited
   to `status`, `diff`, `log`, `add` and `commit`.
4. The command environment is `PATH`, `LANG` and `TERM` from Bloom's own
   environment; a fresh temporary `HOME`, and `USERPROFILE` on Windows, outside
   the workspace and the user's home; `npm_config_offline=true` with npm's
   update notifier, fund and audit messages off; and `GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM=1`,
   `GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0`, `GIT_PAGER=cat` and `PAGER=cat`. Every git command
   also forces `core.fsmonitor=false`, an empty `core.hooksPath` under the
   temporary home, and `core.pager=cat` through `GIT_CONFIG_COUNT` overrides,
   and adds `--no-ext-diff` on `git diff` and `git log` so a planted
   `diff.external` never runs. If removing the temporary home fails, the
   command result is kept and its trace row says "home cleanup failed".
5. Every command asks for approval and shows the command and every argument.
   There is no session-wide allow for commands. A call runs only on
   `allow-once` or `allow-session`; any other choice is a rejection.
6. File tools refuse any write or update under `.git/` at any depth: a
   case-insensitive string check on path segments before any existence or
   realpath lookup, then a second check on the resolved target that treats
   trailing dots and spaces on a segment as insignificant. On Windows, the
   check also compares native resolved paths to refuse targets inside the
   actual `.git` directory, including targets reached by a short alias.

### Residual risk

Approval of each call is the boundary. `npm test` runs whatever the
`package.json` scripts say, and the model may have written those scripts in an
approved write. Commands can reach the network: npm is set offline (flags that
change registry, cache or online mode are refused, including unambiguous npm
option prefixes) and git is limited to local subcommands with fsmonitor, hooks,
`diff.external` and the pager forced off, but Bloom does not block network
access from the process. The repository's own git config is trusted input and
can still name programs (`textconv`, filters, `core.editor`); only fsmonitor,
hooks, `diff.external` and the pager are forced off. The isolated `HOME` only
changes the environment variable, so a command can still find your real home
folder through the operating system's account lookup, and ssh-based git uses
that account entry too. A detached grandchild process can outlive the call,
because Bloom stops only the process group it launched. Writes under `.git/`
are refused; other repository metadata outside `.git/` can still be written if
approved.

## Cloud providers

A provider with `locality` set to `cloud` is refused in the terminal until
`--allow-cloud` is passed, and only inside a folder created by
`scripts/make-sandbox.mjs` for the coding loop. Team sessions never use a cloud
provider. While cloud is on, Bloom asks before the first message leaves the
machine and before every tool call, including reads, and does not offer
session-wide allow. Model rows say cloud. The web workspace stays local only.
Opt-in live tests run with `BLOOM_LIVE=1 npm run test:live` (and
`BLOOM_LIVE_ALLOW_CLOUD=1` when the provider is cloud) and never from offline
`npm test`.

In cloud mode these leave the machine and go to the provider named in your
config (for AI Studio, Google): each task you approve, Bloom's fixed tool
instructions, short summaries of earlier tasks and answers in the same session,
the model's own replies within the turn, and every tool result you approve,
including file contents and command output. Bloom asks before each task is sent
and before each tool call; the follow-up requests inside a turn carry only
results you already approved and are sent without a further prompt. Your key
travels only in the request's Authorization header. What the provider keeps,
and for how long, is set by its terms, not by Bloom: Google's Gemini API terms
say that on unpaid use, including AI Studio and free quota, Google uses
submitted content and responses to improve its products. Use a throwaway
sandbox and send nothing you would not publish.

## Model profiles

`bloom doctor --probe` asks the configured provider what it supports and saves
the answer as a seed model profile in `profiles.json` in Bloom's data
directory, keyed by the provider's config name and the model alias. The file
holds no address, and the printed checks name the provider only by its config
name and locality.

The probe sends two requests. The models list, with a 5 second limit, shows
whether the server answers, which model IDs it lists, and whether the
configured alias's backend model is among them. A failure is reported as
`refused`, `timeout`, `tls` or `http-<code>`. One fixed one-token streaming
request, with a 30 second limit, shows whether the server streams; it carries
the same short message every time and nothing from the user. Context length,
tool calling and constrained output are `reported` only when the models list
entry publishes them, and `unknown` otherwise. No probe request carries a tools
or schema field, and an unknown check is never a pass. `doctor --probe` exits 1
on any failed check.

The coding loop reads the saved profile for the provider and alias it runs
with. A reported or probed context length sets the prompt budget, and a probed
"no" for streaming makes it ask for whole replies. Anything unknown falls back
to the default budget and to streaming. The action format stays the fenced json
block whatever the profile says, so tool calling and constrained output are
recorded but do not change the requests yet.

## Local note writes

The HTTP handler checks the local host and rejects a mismatched Origin before looking up the team. Add note, Correct, Keep and Forget require `confirmed: true` in the request body after that lookup. The browser sends it on the corresponding user action. An authenticated seat gate would require independently verified browser identity and a seat binding. Bloom's session IDs identify local conversations, and the OS account is the trust boundary.

## ViDesign continuity

Bloom’s original UI uses ViDesign’s emitted Nocturne property names for surfaces, contrast, Geist typography, radii and spacing. The conversation uses solid reading surfaces and a single composer. The application self-hosts its OFL fonts and requires no remote art or font requests. Team identity uses names, charters and voices.

The project includes the numerical and typographic properties it consumes. A maintainer with a ViDesign checkout can verify the public snapshot against its generated CSS:

```sh
npm run design:sync -- ../videsign/dist/tokens.css --check
```

Omit `--check` to update the used properties. A fresh Bloom checkout runs from the included snapshot. The upstream design handbook, source layouts, character artwork and brand marks are separate works.

## Verification

The portable suite exercises the budgets, group handoffs, review hold, restart, deletion fence, file-integrity checks, the chat-completions adapter, the provider seam, the coding-session harness against a scripted runtime, the command gate, the provider probe against a fake server, the coding loop against a scripted provider and a synthetic project with zero network calls, and the smoke eval over the same synthetic project. The hosted checks start a real Bloom listener on Windows, macOS and Linux. A Chromium journey opens a reviewed document and tests a narrow viewport. These checks use synthetic briefs and source files. A hosted, billed generation and a graphical desktop session have distinct verification requirements.

## Changes

- 2026-11-24: Run the deterministic coding smoke dataset with `bloom eval --smoke`, which emits case and report events and makes no network call (CAP-14, bloom#16).
- 2026-11-24: Compare resolved Git metadata paths on Windows and verify the Git command fixture with portable repository configuration (CAP-04, bloom#5).

- 2026-11-24: Harden the command gate and file tools for the coding loop (CAP-04, bloom#5).
- 2026-11-24: Add `bloom doctor --probe` and drive the coding loop's budget and streaming from the saved model profile (CAP-16, bloom#7).
- 2026-11-24: Read the web workspace's endpoint only from the private config and show coding rows and approval detail in the browser (CAP-04, bloom#8).
- 2026-11-24: Add cloud opt-in with `--allow-cloud` in a make-sandbox folder, Gemini OpenAI-compatible probe and error mapping, and opt-in live tests (CAP-16, bloom#9).
- 2026-11-24: Add the coding loop with strict actions, one shared repair turn, per-call approvals, streamed text, a trace row per call, and the allowlisted command gate (CAP-04, bloom#5).
- 2026-11-24: Add workspace executors with contained file paths, a disabled-by-default command executor, and bounded output records behind the internal tool interface (CAP-04, bloom#4).
- 2026-11-24: Use one native path resolver for workspace root and tool path comparisons (CAP-04, bloom#4).

# Bloom agent runtime

> **Withdrawn in part.** This pass planned five fixed starter seats with set names. Vivarium ships no fixed roster: agents are created by each person in setup, from generic templates ([vivarium ADR-0002](https://github.com/Vidoxlabs/vivarium/blob/main/docs/adr/0002-internal-agents-use-the-public-setup.md)). The starter-seat steps below are kept as history with placeholder names and are not to be built.

## 1. What the user does

A normal message to the head gets one head reply and creates no specialists.

Try a sample task sets staff for the next Send. The head may then create and run specialists.

To or @Name talks to one existing seat.

The five starter seats are `Starter 1` to `Starter 5`. The user can edit a seat through the member update route. The form for that edit is not in this pass.

## 2. Create

Inside `Teams.create`, after `nameOf` and before `this.harness.store.transaction`, reject a colliding head name. If `name.toLowerCase()` matches a starter seat name, throw the existing `bad(...)` error (`TEAM_INPUT`, HTTP 400) with a message that names the starter seats. Do not open the transaction. No session row, no `teams` row, and no `members` rows are written.

When the name does not collide, keep the current session and `teams` insert. In that same transaction, after `TeamStore.create`, insert exactly five `members` rows, in this order, so `rowid` order matches:

1. `Starter 1`
2. `Starter 2`
3. `Starter 3`
4. `Starter 4`
5. `Starter 5`

Each row uses the columns that already exist. Every row stores the same profile text:

- `charter`: `Help the user shape the next agent.`
- `voice`: `Clear and specific.`
- `stage`: `work`
- `model`: `null`

Charter and voice are profile text in those columns. They are shown by the existing member row (charter paragraph, voice hint). They are not a second prompt, and `Teams.create` does not gain a prompt column. The five share the turn model because `model` is null and the existing work call already falls back to `selectedModel`. Do not write a model id on these rows. Do not add a persona-library row for these names. The head remains the `teams` row and the session title, not a sixth `members` row.

## 3. Staff

`POST /api/sessions/:id/turns` keeps the body `Harness.start` already accepts. Add a boolean `staff`.

`Teams.input` sets `staff` to true only when `request.staff === true`. Omission, `false`, and any other value are false. `Teams.input` does not read the prompt to decide, and it does not call the provider.

The model must not decide `staff`. No plan call, worker call, or other provider call sets it. The model writes the reply and does not set staff. The sample button is the only way this pass sets staff true.

The browser may set the field. In `public/team.js`, the `Try a sample task` button may set a page flag when it inserts this exact sentence:

`Create a researcher to extract claims from the attached sources, a reviewer to check them, and an assembler to write a guide. Flag any evidence gaps.`

`teamView.target()` includes `staff: true` only while that flag is set. The flag stays set if the user edits the sentence before Send. Typing that sentence, or any other sentence, without using the button does not set the flag. After a successful Send, clear the flag. Clear it on `teamView.reset` as well. Do not add a second button, a checkbox, or a prompt scan in this pass.

`src/harness.mjs` includes `request.staff === true` in the request fingerprint array, after the files entry, so a replay cannot apply a different staff value to the same request id.

In `Teams.run`:

- A direct member (`To` or `@Name:`) ignores `staff`. Keep today’s single assignment, with no planner call and no upsert.
- A head turn with `staff` true keeps today’s planner path: one plan call, `planOf`, the 32-specialist cap, `TeamStore.upsert`, one head `team.message` that carries `assignments`, then the assignments in array order, including the existing `revise` stop.
- A head turn with `staff` not true still speaks as the head. It runs the existing import of the user's own `https` URLs before the reply. It then makes one provider call as the head. That call uses a head-reply instruction that asks for one JSON field, `message`, and forbids a roster. This document does not contain that instruction, and the call does not use the planner instruction or the worker instruction. The model writes the reply text. The model does not set `staff`, does not return a roster, and any `agents` field on that response is ignored. Read `message` only. Validate it with the existing 1600-character group-message limit. If `message` is missing, fail the turn with the existing protocol error. Emit one `team.message` from the head with that text and no `assignments` array. Do not call `planOf`. Do not upsert. Do not run the five seats. Do not run every stored member. The phase of this call is not `plan`. The existing provider path, which runs every call through seed's provider seam in `src/provider.mjs`, still records one `team.call` and one `team.usage` for it. On success the turn returns `{ status: 'finished', reason: 'end_turn' }`.

Omitted `staff` stays false. Do not treat a missing field as true in order to preserve current tests. `test/team.test.mjs` is not part of this pass. Direct cases `@Reviewer:` and `to: 'Researcher'` stay on the direct path.

## 4. Edit

Add `PATCH /api/teams/:id/members` beside the existing `POST` recruit branch. Do not change recruit. The seat name is JSON, not the UUID the path captures.

Body: `{ name, charter, voice, stage, renameTo }`. `renameTo` is optional. Ignore `model`, `prompt`, and any other field.

`name` identifies the current row, compared case-insensitively. Validate it with `nameOf`. If no member row matches, throw `bad('This agent is not on the team.')`. This route does not insert a row.

`charter` uses `string(..., 600, 'a jurisdiction')`. `voice` uses `string(..., 300, 'a voice')`. `stage` must be one of `research`, `review`, `assemble`, `work`, `verify`. Otherwise throw `bad('Choose a stage: research, review, assemble, work or verify.')`. Do not accept `head`.

If `renameTo` is omitted or null, keep the name. If it is present, validate it with `nameOf`. If it matches the current name case-insensitively, keep the name. If it matches the head name case-insensitively, throw `bad('The head agent already uses this name.')`. If another member already has that name, throw `bad('This team already has an agent with this name.')`.

Add `TeamStore.updateMember`. Update the existing row in place so its `rowid` does not change. Set `name` (when renaming), `charter`, `voice`, and `stage`. Do not set `model`.

If `this.harness.active` has this team id, throw the same error recruit uses: `BloomError('TURN_ACTIVE', 'Wait for the current turn to finish before changing the team.', 409)`.

Return HTTP 200 and the object `Teams.detail` already returns.

The route can ship before the form. Do not add roster inputs. Do not relabel the member row. Do not rewrite `docs/ui/interface-contract.md`. The JSON field for the stored charter is `charter`. Do not add a `role` field.

## 5. Timeline

Keep one center log. After `turn.started` clears the previous activity lists, `#plan` is the timeline for the new turn. Append rows in arrival order. Keep the existing `team.call` append. Do not append a second `team.call` row. Keep the existing `#tools` and `#usage` renderers. Do not copy usage into `#plan`. Usage stays in Usage.

Row text, using events the loop already emits:

- `turn.started`: `Turn started`
- `tool.updated`: the title and status label `renderTool` already writes. No new title.
- `team.call`: the existing `${actor} · Planning` when `phase` is `plan`, otherwise `${actor} · Working`
- `team.usage`: no timeline row
- `team.recall`: the existing `${actor} · notes reused · ${count} notes` when `hit` is true, otherwise `${actor} · notes loaded · ${count} notes`
- `team.message`: the author. When `verdict` is present, also `Review approved` for `approve`, and `Changes requested` for any other verdict
- `turn.finished`: `labels[data.status]` from `public/app.js`, or `data.status` when the map has no entry

Do not invent a route event.

Route line, only on a `team.message` whose `assignments` array is present. Under the list `public/app.js` already renders (`name — assignment`), add one text line: the author, then `, `, then each `assignments[].name` in array order, separated by `, `. Example shape: `Lead, Planner, Reviewer`. No arrow. No word “to”. Do not read or write a recipient. Do not put the `persona` boolean on this line.

When a later `team.message` in the same turn has `verdict` `revise`, find that author in the assignments array. On the order line, append ` (not run)` to each assignment name that follows that author. Leave the names visible. If that author is not in the array, append the suffix to nobody.

A direct turn has no `phase: plan` call and one worker `team.message`. Do not add an order line. The route is that author, already shown as the message header.

A verify seat emits `team.message` and no `team.call`. Its timeline row is the message row. Do not invent a `team.call` for it.

## 6. Already present

These already exist. A code agent does not rebuild them.

- `POST /api/teams/:id/members` recruits through `Teams.recruit`.
- `PUT` on the persona path calls `harness.teams.updatePersona`.
- `members.model` is a column. The work call passes `model || selectedModel`. A stored member model replaces the turn model when it is set.
- Specialist rows have a `Save as persona` button.

## 7. Leave out

- A mailbox, a second chat, and a `to` field on `team.message`.
- A per-member model. The five inserts store `model` null. `updateMember` does not change `model`. Do not add a seat model control.
- A prompt column.
- A sixth seeded seat. The head is the `teams` row. Do not insert these five into the persona library.
- Any seeded stage other than `work`. Do not seed `review`, `assemble`, or `verify`. Do not add a stage id. Do not order assignments so a `revise` verdict skips the starter seats. The existing `reviewBlocked` rule stays as it is.
- The untrusted six-step excerpt as `Teams.run`. Do not run one seat twice. Do not add agents or stages for that excerpt.
- A prompt scan, on the server or in the browser, that decides `staff`.
- A loop that runs every stored member on a head turn whose `staff` is not true.
- An insert on `PATCH /api/teams/:id/members`.
- A visible member editor, a roster relabel, and any edit to `docs/ui/interface-contract.md` or any other file under `docs/ui/`.
- Any edit to `docs/backend/research/agent-runtime-patterns.md`.
- A new route event, a usage row inside `#plan`, and an arrow or recipient on the assignment-order line.
- Prompt text copied into charter, voice, docs, or tests.
- Setting omitted `staff` to true.

## Files a code agent may change

- `src/teams.mjs`
- `src/team-store.mjs`
- `src/http.mjs`
- `src/harness.mjs`
- `public/team.js`
- `public/app.js`

# Bloom backend

These docs specify how a Bloom team creates, edits, and shows agent work.

[agent-runtime.md](agent-runtime.md) is the runtime contract. It is the source of truth for the next backend pass.

The two research files are the evidence:

- [research/implementability-review.md](research/implementability-review.md)
- [research/agent-runtime-patterns.md](research/agent-runtime-patterns.md)

Every provider call in this pass, including the head reply, goes through seed's provider seam in `src/provider.mjs`, the same path the planner and worker calls use. The contract does not change that file.

A code agent may change only the files named in the contract: `src/teams.mjs`, `src/team-store.mjs`, `src/http.mjs`, `src/harness.mjs`, `public/team.js`, and `public/app.js`. The code agent must leave `docs/ui/` alone.

# Agent runtime patterns

> **Withdrawn in part.** This pass planned five fixed starter seats with set names. Vivarium ships no fixed roster: agents are created by each person in setup, from generic templates ([vivarium ADR-0002](https://github.com/Vidoxlabs/vivarium/blob/main/docs/adr/0002-internal-agents-use-the-public-setup.md)). The starter-seat steps below are kept as history with placeholder names and are not to be built.

> **Note, 2026-11-22 (Bloom 0.7.0).** Bloom no longer runs OpenCode in any form, and it now imports seed for the provider seam. The OpenCode and swarm-plugin sections below describe other products as they were read that day. They are evidence about those products, not Bloom behavior. The rest of this report is unchanged.

Checkable notes for Bloom's team loop, the installed swarm plugin, and the public harness pages opened on 2026-11-22. OBSERVED claims cite a file or a URL from that day. RECOMMENDED claims are proposals a reviewer can accept or reject. They are not current Bloom behavior.

This file does not paste system prompts. `docs/architecture.md` uses several Vidoxlabs names as labels for local notes, the review stop, and the session event log. The running code is `Teams`, `TeamStore`, and the session event table.

## 1. What Bloom does today

OBSERVED from `src/teams.mjs`, `src/team-store.mjs`, `src/http.mjs`, `src/harness.mjs`, `src/store.mjs`, `src/models.mjs`, `public/index.html`, `public/team.js`, `public/app.js`, `test/team.test.mjs`, and `docs/ui/interface-contract.md`.

### Create

`POST /api/teams` is the only team-create route. `createHandler` returns 201 from `Teams.create`.

`Teams.create` reads a name (`Head agent` when the body omits one), a charter, a call limit (default 6, range 1–20), an optional token limit, and an optional model. Inside one transaction it creates a session with adapter `team` and inserts one `teams` row. It does not insert `members` rows.

The screen copy that submits this call, quoted from `public/index.html` and `docs/ui/interface-contract.md` section 0, is:

- Empty heading: `What should we work on?`
- Primary button: `Create a team`
- Kind: `Team`
- Field: `Head agent name`, initial value `Lead`, hint `Plans the work and creates specialists for it.`
- Field: `Jurisdiction`, placeholder `What should this head agent be responsible for?`, hint `What this agent is responsible for.`
- Submit: `Create team`

The head is the `teams` row and the session title. The roster paints that row with display stage `Head agent`. Stored specialist stages stay `research`, `review`, `assemble`, `work`, and `verify`.

### Delegate

`POST /api/sessions/:id/turns` calls `Harness.start`. For a team session, `Teams.input` chooses the recipient.

- `To`, or a leading `@Name:`, selects one existing member. `Teams.run` then sets a single assignment to that member's stored profile and the user's text. It does not call the planner and does not upsert. `test/team.test.mjs` checks `@Reviewer:` and `to: 'Researcher'`.
- A message to the head (the `To` control's first option, which `teamView.target` omits from the body, or text that does not name a member) calls the planner. `planOf` requires 1 to 5 agents. Each agent has `name`, `charter`, `voice`, `stage`, and `assignment`. Stage must be one of the five stored ids. A review stage after an assemble stage is rejected. Names must be unique and must differ from the head.
- The planner path upserts those specialists, posts one `team.message` from the head with `assignments`, then runs the assignments in array order.
- `TeamStore.upsert` inserts or, on the same team and name, overwrites `charter`, `voice`, and `stage`.
- A specialist cap of 32 is checked before that upsert. The verify stage re-reads supplied files and writes a hash report with no model call. Any other stage makes one provider call.
- A review `verdict` of `revise` finishes that reviewer's post, sets `reviewBlocked`, and does not run later specialists. The turn finishes `revision` / `review_requested_changes`. `test/team.test.mjs` expects authors `Head agent`, `Researcher`, `Reviewer` and no assembler. `approve` lets later specialists run.
- The scripted demo in `src/models.mjs` returns Researcher, Reviewer, and Assembler. That roster is the demo provider, not a seeded product roster.

### Communicate

Group speech is `team.message`. The author, text, epoch, and optional `assignments`, `file`, `scoped`, and `verdict` are stored on the session event. There is no recipient field.

The next specialist sees up to six `team.message` rows for the current epoch, loaded by `Teams.recent`, plus saved notes from `TeamStore.recall`. Those notes are team notes. `Forget` deletes one note, bumps `teams.epoch`, and stops an active turn.

`Harness.event` also records, on this path:

- `user.message` and `turn.started` from `Store.startTurn`
- `team.call` with `phase` `plan` or `work`
- `team.usage`
- `team.recall`
- `tool.updated` for a URL read or a desktop move
- `turn.finished`, and `turn.stopping` if the user presses `Stop`

The transcript in `public/app.js` paints `user.message` and `team.message` in the same log. A head post with `assignments` shows `name — assignment`. A review post shows `Review approved` or `Changes requested`. `team.call` is appended to `#plan` as `Actor · Planning` or `Actor · Working`. `team.recall` is appended to `#tools` as `{actor} · notes reused · {count} notes` or `{actor} · notes loaded · {count} notes`.

### What the user can see or edit afterward

OBSERVED screen, matching the interface contract:

- `To` lists the head first, then members in `rowid` order. `Send` starts a turn. `Stop` aborts it.
- The `Team` list is read-only `<details>`. Summary pattern: `name · Head agent`, `name · Research`, `name · Review`, `name · Assemble`, `name · Work`, `name · Check`.
- Hint lines on those rows: `VI · Team coordinator` for the head, `LA · Deterministic verification` for `verify`, `OAI · Model-backed specialist` otherwise, plus the voice when a specialist has one.
- The user can add a shared-desktop file, check up to six files, open a file, save a note, and `Forget` a note.
- `Shared desktop` heading and hint: `Files every agent on this computer can open and reuse. Check files to include with the next task.`
- `Notes`, `Activity`, and `Usage` are the inspector headings. Waiting copy: `Give the head agent a task. Check the shared desktop when the team needs evidence.`
- The user cannot change a member's name, charter, voice, or stage after create. `createHandler` has no member path. Its team pattern covers the team id plus `sources`, `notes`, and `files` only. A search of `src/http.mjs` finds no `PATCH` or `PUT`.
- A later message to the head can still overwrite an existing member through `TeamStore.upsert`. That is the planner, not an edit form.
- One model id is selected for the turn. Members have no model column.

Coordinator checks re-verified against this code:

| Claim | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `POST /api/teams` creates the head | Observed. `Teams.create` writes the session and the `teams` row. |
| The planner upserts 1 to 5 specialists, posts one group message, then runs them in order | Observed on the head path in `Teams.run`. |
| `To` or `@Name` runs one existing member and does not plan | Observed in `Teams.input` and the direct branch of `Teams.run`. |
| `TeamStore.upsert` exists and no HTTP route edits a member | Observed. |
| Events include `team.message`, `team.call`, `team.usage`, `team.recall`, and `tool.updated` | Observed. The turn also emits `user.message`, `turn.started`, and `turn.finished`. |
| A review verdict of `revise` stops later specialists | Observed. The reviewer still posts. |

## 2. What the installed swarm plugin does

OBSERVED from the installed package `opencode-swarm-plugin` 0.63.2 at the vidoxlabs swarm-tools package path, dependency `swarm-mail` 1.11.2. The plugin `package.json` `repository` is `https://github.com/joelhooks/swarm-tools`. The README badge links `https://github.com/joelhooks/opencode-swarm-plugin`. There is no `swarm-mail.js` in the plugin `dist`. Mail tools are the bundled `src/swarm-mail.ts` section of `dist/index.js`. Cell creation and message append are in `swarm-mail` `dist/index.js`. The state database was not opened.

The README in that install still has a "What's New in v0.33" section. The behavior below is from the 0.63.2 bundle, not from that older section.

### How a cell is created

`hive_create` is described as "Create a new cell in the hive with type-safe validation". Arguments: `title`, optional `type` (`bug`, `feature`, `task`, `epic`, `chore`), optional `priority` 0–3, optional `description`, optional `parent_id`.

`hive.js` `execute` parses those args, takes the hive working directory as the project key, and calls `adapter.createCell`. In `swarm-mail` `src/hive/adapter.ts`, `createCell` builds a `cell_created` event. `generateBeadId` builds the id from a project-name prefix (or `cell` when `package.json` has no usable name), a short hash of the project key, a base-36 timestamp, and three random base-36 characters. `appendCellEventDrizzle` inserts that event and updates projections. The tool then emits another `cell_created` via `safeEmitEvent` and returns the formatted cell. This creates a work record. It does not start an agent process.

`hive_create_epic` creates one epic cell, then one task cell per subtask with `parent_id` set to the epic, and emits `epic_created`, `decomposition_generated`, and `swarm_started`. On failure it deletes the cells it already created.

`hive_update` is declared with `id` plus optional `status`, `description`, and `priority`. `hive_close` is declared with `id` and `reason`.

### How a worker is spawned

`swarm_spawn_subtask` is described as "Prepare a subtask for spawning. Returns prompt with Agent Mail/hive tracking instructions." Its `execute` builds a prompt, selects a model, records a coordinator `worker_spawned` decision, and, when `project_path` is set, appends a `worker_spawned` event whose `worker_agent` is the literal `worker`. The return value is JSON: `prompt`, ids, files, `recommended_model`, and post-completion instructions. The function does not start a process.

`swarm_delegate_planning` is described as "Delegate task decomposition to a swarm/planner subagent. Returns a prompt to spawn the planner." Its `execute` returns that prompt. It does not create the planner process.

`swarm_spawn_researcher` and `swarm_spawn_retry` likewise return prompts.

### How mail is sent

`swarmmail_init` loads session state. If that session already has a state, it returns `already_initialized` and the existing `agent_name`. It does not register the name passed on the second call. On a fresh session, `initSwarmAgent` appends `agent_registered` and stores `projectKey` and `agentName`.

`swarmmail_send` requires that session. `sendSwarmMessage` classifies the subject into `progress`, `blocked`, `question`, `status`, or `general`, appends `message_sent` (recipients, subject, body, thread, importance, ack flag), and appends `thread_created` when the thread id is new. It then reads back a message id. `swarmmail_inbox` returns at most five messages and omits bodies. `swarmmail_read_message` loads one body.

`swarmmail_reserve` grants exclusive path locks through `reserveSwarmFiles`. It does not deliver chat.

On this research run, `swarmmail_init` for `bloom-runtime-researcher` returned `already_initialized` as `bloom-ui-coordinator`. `swarmmail_reserve` for this file still returned a grant. `hivemind_find` returned no matches. `skills_list` returned no skills.

## 3. Public harness observations

Pages opened on 2026-11-22. HTML conversions of the GitHub repo homes did not list source files. Raw files and the GrokBot contents API did.

### GrokBot repository

OBSERVED. These pages disagree with each other. None of them is Bloom.

- `https://github.com/Franzferdinan51/GrokBot` loaded as a repository home without a file list.
- Raw `README.md` on `main` is titled "Grok Build Desktop". It describes one primary agent, optional subagent delegation, and a mixture-of-agents preset of 2–8 reference models plus one acting aggregator. Reference models are plan-only. The aggregator edits and verifies. The install snippet clones `Franzferdinan51/Grok-Build-Desktop-App`. The user can change model, permissions, skills, and workspace files. The page does not show a control named `Head agent`.
- Raw `VISION.md` on `main` describes GrokBot as a terminal-first assistant. It says the project will not merge agent-hierarchy frameworks as a default architecture. It describes plugins, skills, and one active memory plugin. It does not specify a create, delegate, or mailbox API.
- The contents API for `main` lists `docs/cli/agents.md`, `docs/concepts/agent.md`, and `docs/concepts/multi-agent.md`. Those raw pages describe a different surface: `grokbot agents add` creates an isolated agent with a workspace, model, agent directory, and channel bindings. `main` cannot be used as a new id and cannot be deleted. `grokbot agents set-identity` writes `name`, `theme`, `emoji`, and `avatar`. Workspace files `AGENTS.md`, `SOUL.md`, `IDENTITY.md`, and the other bootstrap files are injected on a new session and are user-editable. Inbound channel traffic is routed by bindings. The multi-agent example sets `tools.agentToAgent.enabled` to `false` and comments that agent-to-agent messaging must be enabled and allowlisted. `sessions_send` and `sessions_spawn` appear as names in one tool allow list. Their parameters were not opened. The linked sub-agents page was not opened.

`docs/architecture.md` cites three xAI Grok Bot docs. Those URLs were not opened for this report.

### OpenCode

OBSERVED at `https://opencode.ai/docs/agents/`.

- An agent is a Markdown file or an `agents` entry in JSONC. The Markdown body is the system prompt. Locations: `~/.config/opencode/agents/` and `.opencode/agents/`. Nested project paths become part of the id.
- `mode` is `primary`, `subagent`, or `all`. A subagent runs only through the `subagent` tool, in a child session, in the background. The parent is told when the child goes idle and after later rounds. The parent's `subagent` permission lists which agents it may launch. The child uses its own permissions.
- Built-ins named on the page: `build` and `plan` (primary), `general` and `explore` (subagent). The user asks in text, for example to use a reviewer subagent. `default_agent` does not replace the agent stored on an existing session.
- The user edits the Markdown or JSONC afterward: description, mode, model, permissions, steps, hidden, color, and disabled. A subagent uses its configured model, or the parent session model when none is set.

### Claude Code agent teams

OBSERVED at `https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-teams`. The page says teams are experimental and off until `CLAUDE_CODE_EXPERIMENTAL_AGENT_TEAMS=1`.

- The user asks in a normal prompt. Claude spawns teammates by calling the Agent tool with a `name`. The lead's conversation is not copied. The spawn prompt is. A named subagent definition can supply tools, model, and body text.
- The lead assigns tasks, or a teammate claims the next unblocked task. Claim uses file locking. Tasks are pending, in progress, or completed. Teammates do not spawn teammates. One team per session. The lead stays the lead.
- Teammates message each other with `SendMessage`. Each mailbox is a JSON file under `~/.claude/teams/{team-name}/inboxes/`. A write is reported as sent only when the file write succeeds. Messages are labeled as coming from another session. Idle teammates notify the lead.
- The user sees an agent panel, or split panes with tmux or iTerm2. Enter opens a teammate transcript and sends a message. A teammate's model is fixed at spawn. The page says not to hand-edit the team config. Permission prompts surface on the lead. In-process teammates are not restored by resume.

### Cursor

OBSERVED. `https://cursor.com/docs/agent/chat/subagents` returned 404. The pages that loaded are `https://cursor.com/docs/agent/overview`, `https://cursor.com/docs/subagents`, `https://cursor.com/docs/agent/projects`, and `https://cursor.com/docs/agent/agents-window`. The index `https://cursor.com/llms.txt` supplied those URLs.

- Overview: an agent is instructions, tools, and a selected model. For a larger body of work the user creates a Project. The page says a coordinator plans and delegates. Checkpoints and the chat timeline are how the user reviews file snapshots. Restoring a checkpoint reverts files and leaves messages in place.
- Projects: in the Agents Window the user clicks New Project, sets an icon, name, cloud repository, and coordinator model. The coordinator does not write code. It creates agents and the user can open any of those agents and talk to it. Chats can be added to or removed from the Project. Shared project context is separate from a personal store. A coordinator message to a teammate's coordinator is delivered as a side chat the user can read, stop, or archive, and cannot message.
- Subagents: Markdown files in `.cursor/agents/`, `.claude/agents/`, `.codex/agents/`, or the matching user directories. Frontmatter fields on the page: `name`, `description`, `model` (`inherit` or an id), `readonly`, `is_background`. The parent delegates automatically, by `/name`, or by a sentence. The subagent starts without the parent's history and returns a result. Parallel work is multiple Task calls. The task card shows the model that ran. Background output is written under `~/.cursor/subagents/`. The user resumes with the returned agent id. The user edits the Markdown file. Built-ins named on this page are Explore and Browser.
- Agents Window: command palette `Open Agents Window`. Parallel local and cloud agents, diffs, and `/in-cloud` for a cloud subagent. The editor remains available.

### Plugin repositories

`https://github.com/joelhooks/swarm-tools` and `https://github.com/joelhooks/opencode-swarm-plugin` both loaded as repository homes without a file list or README body. Installed files are the source for section 2. `https://swarmtools.ai/docs`, linked from the installed README, was not opened.

## 4. Creation, delegation, communication, and edit map

OBSERVED comparison. Empty cells mean the opened page did not specify that mechanism.

| System | Create | Delegate | Communicate | User can see or edit afterward |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Bloom | `POST /api/teams` creates the head only. Specialists appear when a head turn's planner passes `planOf` and `TeamStore.upsert` runs. | Head turn: 1–5 specialists, then in order. `To` or `@Name:` runs one stored member. `revise` stops the rest. | One transcript of `team.message`. No recipient field. Recent posts and notes are data on the next call. | Create form edits the head name and `Jurisdiction` before submit. Roster, voice, and stage are display-only. Notes, files, `To`, `Model`, `Send`, and `Stop` stay editable. |
| Swarm plugin 0.63.2 | `hive_create` appends `cell_created` and returns a cell id. | `swarm_spawn_subtask` and `swarm_delegate_planning` return prompts and can append `worker_spawned`. They do not start the worker. | `swarmmail_send` appends `message_sent` to named agents. Inbox omits bodies. | `hive_update` can change status, description, and priority. File locks are reservations, not a transcript. |
| GrokBot raw README | A desktop conversation plus optional subagents and a mixture-of-agents preset. | Primary agent, or reference models feeding one aggregator. | Advisor text is given to the aggregator. Telegram is a separate channel. | Settings, model, skills, and workspace files. |
| GrokBot `VISION.md` | Not specified. | Says a manager hierarchy is not the default it will merge. | Plugins and channels. No mailbox API on this page. | Terminal-first config, with doctor migrations when config changes. |
| GrokBot `grokbot agents` docs | `grokbot agents add` or `agents.list`. | Channel bindings route inbound messages to an agent id. | `agentToAgent` is off unless enabled and allowlisted. `sessions_send` is only an allow-list name here. | Identity fields and bootstrap Markdown in the agent workspace. |
| OpenCode | Markdown or JSONC agent profile. | Parent `subagent` tool, child session. | Child reports to the parent when it goes idle. | Edit the file or config. Existing sessions keep their selected agent. |
| Claude Code teams | Prompt plus Agent tool `name`, or a subagent definition. | Shared task list, lead assignment, or self-claim. | `SendMessage` and per-agent mailbox files. | Agent panel or split panes. Message a teammate. Do not hand-edit team config. Model is fixed at spawn. |
| Cursor subagents | Markdown under `.cursor/agents/` or a user directory. Built-ins exist without a file. | Parent Task call, `/name`, or a sentence. | Result returns to the parent. Background writes local output files. | Edit the Markdown. Task card shows the model. Resume with the agent id. |
| Cursor Projects | New Project in the Agents Window. | Coordinator creates cloud agents and does not write the code itself. | User chats with the coordinator or opens a worker. Coordinators can message another coordinator into a side chat. | Name, model, membership, task board, and shared context. Side chats can be read, stopped, or archived. |

## 5. Recommendations a reviewer can accept or reject

Each item names the Bloom function or the missing route. Accepting one does not accept the others.

### R1. Seed five seats in `Teams.create`

Accept: after the `teams` insert, `Teams.create` inserts five `members` rows with fixed starter names, in a fixed order. They use the columns that already exist: `name`, `charter`, `voice`, `stage`. They share the team turn's model. `Teams.create` does not gain a per-member model or a prompt column.

Reject if the head name, compared case-insensitively, matches one of those five. `planOf` already refuses a specialist with the head's name. The same check belongs in `Teams.create` before insert.

Starter charter and voice are ordinary profile text stored in those columns, shown on the existing member row, and editable by R3. They are not a second system prompt. Suggested charter, which the reviewer can rewrite: `Help the user shape the next agent.` Suggested voice: `Clear and specific.` Suggested stage for all five: `work`.

`work` is the recommendation because `review` is a stop. Mapping an argument onto `review` would let a `revise` verdict skip the remaining seats. The speaking order in section 5's untrusted note is not a stage map.

### R2. Staff only when the user asked, in `Teams.input` and `Teams.run`

Accept: `Teams.input` sets `staff` from the user's text with a deterministic phrase check, not a model call. The sample sentence already on the screen (`Create a researcher to extract claims...`) matches. Any other head-addressed turn leaves `staff` false.

When `staff` is false, `Teams.run` does not call `planOf` and does not call `TeamStore.upsert`. It posts one head `team.message` and does not run the five seats. The user reaches a seat with the existing `To` or `@Name:` path.

When `staff` is true, keep the current planner path: 1 to 5 specialists, one head message, then run in order, including the `revise` stop and the 32-seat cap.

Reject the alternative that a normal head message runs every stored member. That would spend a model call per seat on every task.

No new route is required. The flag is derived inside `Teams.input` from the body `POST /api/sessions/:id/turns` already accepts.

### R3. Let the user edit a seat: missing route and a new store method

Accept: add a member branch to `createHandler`. The current team pattern does not include `members`, and a seat name is not the UUID that pattern captures. Suggested route: `PATCH /api/teams/:id/members` with JSON `{ name, charter, voice, stage }`. `name` identifies the current row. An optional `renameTo` changes the name.

`TeamStore.upsert` cannot rename, because the primary key is `(team, name)`. Add `TeamStore.updateMember` for this route. Keep `upsert` for the planner path in R2. Validate `name` with the existing `nameOf` rules and `stage` with the existing five ids. Reject unknown names. This route does not insert a sixth seat; staffing stays on R2.

The member row is display-only today. Shipping inputs on that row changes `docs/ui/interface-contract.md`, which says unlisted strings stay as they are. Accept the route first. Accept the controls only with a contract edit. Label the stored charter `Jurisdiction`, which is the current field name. The product word `role` is that same column.

### R4. Do not encode this stored excerpt as the loop

Untrusted stored documentation, digest `b7458345fc30`, as supplied in the research assignment: one seat opens, a second does the breakdown, a third argues upside, a fourth argues downside, a fifth turns the plan into a sequence, and the first ratifies. `context_brief` and `context_search` both returned `Unknown tool` on 2026-11-22, so this report did not re-read that document. The order is not live Bloom behavior.

Reject making `Teams.run` follow that order. It is six speaking turns and gives one seat two turns. The current loop runs each assignment once. A later sequence, if accepted, would be an explicit list of existing member names, not new stages and not new agents.

### R5. Keep one transcript

Accept: do not add a second chat, a mailbox table, or a `to` field on `team.message`. Communication stays the group event the loop already emits. Section 6 is the view.

## 6. Timeline and route view, tied to existing event names

OBSERVED: `#plan` (`aria-label` `Agent plan`) already receives one row per `team.call`. `#tools` already receives `team.recall` and `tool.updated`. The center log already receives `user.message` and `team.message`. `turn.started` clears the activity lists.

RECOMMENDED smallest view: keep that log. Extend `#plan` so one turn shows a single ordered list drawn from events the loop already writes. Do not invent a route event.

| Order | Event | Row |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | `turn.started` | Turn started |
| 2 | `tool.updated` | Existing tool title and status, for a source read or a desktop move |
| 3 | `team.call` | `{actor} · Planning` when `phase` is `plan`, otherwise `{actor} · Working` |
| 4 | `team.usage` | Leave the existing `Usage` block. Do not copy it into the timeline |
| 5 | `team.recall` | The existing notes line |
| 6 | `team.message` | `{author}` plus `Review approved` or `Changes requested` when `verdict` is present |
| 7 | `turn.finished` | The turn status already shown by the inspector |

Route, from fields that exist today:

- A `team.message` whose `assignments` array is present is the route. Paint one line under the assignment list `app.js` already renders: the author's name, then each `assignments[].name` in array order.
- The route ends at the first `team.message` with `verdict` `revise`. That matches `reviewBlocked`. Later names in `assignments` can stay visible as not run.
- A direct turn has no `phase: plan` call and one worker `team.message`. The route is that author only.
- A verify seat emits `team.message` and no `team.call`. The timeline row is the message.

There is no recipient on `team.message`. The line is assignment order, not a claim that one specialist addressed the next.

## 7. Gaps

- Digest `b7458345fc30` was not re-opened. `context_brief` and `context_search` returned `Unknown tool`.
- `https://cursor.com/docs/agent/chat/subagents` returned 404. Subagent behavior is from `https://cursor.com/docs/subagents` instead.
- The three xAI URLs cited in `docs/architecture.md` were not opened.
- GrokBot `docs/tools/subagents`, linked from the multi-agent page, was not opened. `sessions_send` and `sessions_spawn` are allow-list names only.
- GitHub HTML for `Franzferdinan51/GrokBot`, `joelhooks/swarm-tools`, and `joelhooks/opencode-swarm-plugin` did not include README or tree text. `https://swarmtools.ai/docs` was not opened.
- The swarm state database was not opened. Live message bodies were not read.
- `swarmmail_init` on this run did not register `bloom-runtime-researcher` because the session was already initialized.
- Bloom has no HTTP member edit, no rename, and no staff flag. Those are R2 and R3, not current routes.
- No browser pass was run for this document. Screen strings were checked in `public/index.html`, `public/app.js`, and `public/team.js`.
