docsPages.body:
# Implementability review

> **Withdrawn in part.** This pass planned five fixed starter seats with set names. Vivarium ships no fixed roster: agents are created by each person in setup, from generic templates ([vivarium ADR-0002](https://github.com/Vidoxlabs/vivarium/blob/main/docs/adr/0002-internal-agents-use-the-public-setup.md)). The starter-seat steps below are kept as history with placeholder names and are not to be built.

Reviewed `docs/backend/research/agent-runtime-patterns.md` against `src/teams.mjs`, `src/team-store.mjs`, `src/http.mjs`, `src/harness.mjs`, `public/index.html`, `public/team.js`, and `public/app.js`. The research file stays as evidence. This review is the instruction for the assembler. Where they disagree, this review wins.

This file does not change source, `docs/ui/`, or the research report. It does not paste prompt text.

## 1. Verdict

**approve**

The report is specific enough to implement once the false checkout claims below are set aside and R1, R2, R3, and the section 6 timeline are followed in the narrowed form in section 2. A mix of accepted, narrowed, and rejected recommendations is still an approval. R4 and R5 stand as written.

Re-checked claims that hold:

- `Teams.create` uses `Head agent` when the body omits a name: `const name = nameOf(body.name ?? 'Head agent');` in `src/teams.mjs`. The create form’s visible value is still `Lead`, on the field labeled `Head agent name` in `public/index.html`.
- `planOf` rejects a review stage after an assemble stage: `const assemble = members.findIndex(a => a.stage === 'assemble');` and `if (assemble !== -1 && members.slice(assemble + 1).some(a => a.stage === 'review')) throw protocol();` in `src/teams.mjs`.
- The create form labels are `Head agent name` and `Jurisdiction` in `public/index.html`. The Jurisdiction hint is `What this agent is responsible for.` The placeholder is `What should this head agent be responsible for?`
- `POST /api/teams` returns 201 from `harness.teams.create`. `Teams.create` writes one session with adapter `team` and one `teams` row. It does not insert `members` rows.
- Stored specialist stage ids are `research`, `review`, `assemble`, `work`, and `verify`.
- A direct `To` or leading `@Name:` runs one stored member, does not call `planOf`, and does not upsert. `teamView.target` omits `to` when the head is the selected option (`selectedIndex > 0` is the members).
- A review `verdict` of `revise` is posted, then `reviewBlocked` stops later assignments. The turn result is `{ status: 'revision', reason: 'review_requested_changes' }`.
- `team.message` stores `author`, `text`, `epoch`, and optional `assignments`, `file`, `scoped`, and `verdict`. It has no recipient field.
- There is no `staff` field and no `TeamStore.updateMember`. There is no `PATCH` in `src/http.mjs`.
- The sample button sets the prompt to `Create a researcher to extract claims from the attached sources, a reviewer to check them, and an assembler to write a guide. Flag any evidence gaps.` It does not set any other flag today.
- `#usage` is where `team.usage` is rendered. `#plan` (`aria-label` `Agent plan`) receives `team.call`. The center log receives `user.message` and `team.message`.

Research claims about this checkout that are false:

- “A search of `src/http.mjs` finds no `PATCH` or `PUT`.” `PATCH` is absent. `PUT` is present: `if (personaPath && method === 'PUT') return json(response, 200, harness.teams.updatePersona(personaPath[1], await readBody(request)));`
- “`createHandler` has no member path. Its team pattern covers the team id plus `sources`, `notes`, and `files` only.” The pattern includes members: `(sources|notes|files|members)`. The member branch is `if (method === 'POST' && kind === 'members' && !item) return json(response, 200, harness.teams.recruit(id, await readBody(request)));`
- “The user cannot change a member's name, charter, voice, or stage after create” and “no HTTP route edits a member.” A name still cannot be renamed. Charter, voice, stage, and model can be overwritten. `TeamStore.upsert` runs `ON CONFLICT(team,name) DO UPDATE SET charter=excluded.charter,voice=excluded.voice,stage=excluded.stage,model=excluded.model`. `Teams.recruit` calls that upsert for a library persona, including when the name already matches a member.
- “The `Team` list is read-only `<details>`.” The rows are still not inputs for name, charter, voice, or stage. `public/team.js` adds a button on specialist rows: `const save = node('button', 'Save as persona', 'text-button');`
- “Members have no model column” and “One model id is selected for the turn. Members have no model column.” `src/team-store.mjs` runs `ALTER TABLE members ADD COLUMN model TEXT` and selects `name,charter,voice,stage,model`. The work call passes the member model through: `model: model || selectedModel` in `src/teams.mjs`. A stored member model replaces the turn model when it is set. The composer still sends one turn model.
- “The next specialist sees up to six `team.message` rows for the current epoch, loaded by `Teams.recent`.” `Teams.recent` loads at most six rows (`LIMIT 6`). `Teams.run` then `recent.push(...)` after each specialist, and the worker prompt sends `group: recent`. A later specialist in the same turn sees those six plus the earlier posts from that turn.
- Section 7, “Bloom has no HTTP member edit.” There is still no member rename and no `PATCH`. `POST /api/teams/:id/members` already writes a member through `Teams.recruit`. “No staff flag” remains true.

Rejected claims stay out of the implementation. They are not repaired by editing the research report.

## 2. Recommendation rows

| id | verdict | evidence | what the assembler may write |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| R1 | narrow | Seed five `members` rows from `Teams.create`. Default head name `Head agent` and form value `Lead` do not collide with those names. | Section 2.1 |
| R2 | narrow | Staff only from an explicit turn-body boolean. The sample button may set it. The model must not. | Section 2.2 |
| R3 | narrow | Add `PATCH /api/teams/:id/members` and `TeamStore.updateMember`. The route ships before any editor. | Section 2.3 |
| R4 | accept | Do not encode the untrusted six-step excerpt as `Teams.run`. | Section 2.4 |
| R5 | accept | One transcript. No mailbox, no second chat, no recipient on `team.message`. | Section 2.5 |
| S6 | narrow | Timeline rows only from events the loop already emits. Usage stays in the Usage block. The route line is assignment order. | Section 2.6 |

The subsections below are the cells of that table.

### 2.1 R1. Seed five seats

**verdict:** narrow

**evidence:** `Teams.create` does not insert members today. `planOf` already refuses a specialist whose name matches the head, using a case-insensitive set seeded with `team.name.toLowerCase()`. The `members` primary key is `(team, name)` with `COLLATE NOCASE`. The table already has a `model` column. It has no prompt column. `call` uses `model || selectedModel`, so a null member model uses the turn model.

**what the assembler may write:**

Inside `Teams.create`, after `nameOf` and before `this.harness.store.transaction`, reject a colliding head name. If `name.toLowerCase()` matches a starter seat name, throw the existing `bad(...)` error (`TEAM_INPUT`, HTTP 400) with a message that names the starter seats. Do not open the transaction. No session row, no `teams` row, and no `members` rows are written.

When the name does not collide, keep the current session and `teams` insert. In that same transaction, after `TeamStore.create`, insert exactly five `members` rows, in this order, so `rowid` order matches:

1. `Starter 1`
2. `Starter 2`
3. `Starter 3`
4. `Starter 4`
5. `Starter 5`

Each row uses the columns that already exist. Every row stores the same profile text:

- `charter`: `Help the user shape the next agent.`
- `voice`: `Clear and specific.`
- `stage`: `work`
- `model`: `null`

Charter and voice are profile text in those columns. They are shown by the existing member row (charter paragraph, voice hint). They are not a second prompt, and `Teams.create` does not gain a prompt column. The five share the turn model because `model` is null and the existing work call already falls back to `selectedModel`. Do not write a model id on these rows. Do not add a persona-library row for these names. The head remains the `teams` row and the session title, not a sixth `members` row.

### 2.2 R2. Staff only when the user asks

**verdict:** narrow

**evidence:** Every head-addressed turn currently calls `call('plan', ...)`, then `planOf`, then `TeamStore.upsert`, then runs the assignments. `Teams.input` does not read a staff flag. `public/team.js` `target()` sends `to` and `files` only. The sample button only assigns the prompt string quoted in section 1. `src/harness.mjs` fingerprints `[text, model ?? null, request.to ?? null, request.files ?? []]`.

The research phrase check is rejected. A hidden scan of the prompt is not the control. `staff` gates creating and running new specialists. It does not mute the head.

**what the assembler may write:**

`POST /api/sessions/:id/turns` keeps the body `Harness.start` already accepts. Add a boolean `staff`.

`Teams.input` sets `staff` to true only when `request.staff === true`. Omission, `false`, and any other value are false. `Teams.input` does not read the prompt to decide, and it does not call the provider.

The model must not decide `staff`. No plan call, worker call, or other provider call sets it.

The browser may set the field. In `public/team.js`, the `Try a sample task` button may set a page flag when it inserts this exact sentence:

`Create a researcher to extract claims from the attached sources, a reviewer to check them, and an assembler to write a guide. Flag any evidence gaps.`

`teamView.target()` includes `staff: true` only while that flag is set. The flag stays set if the user edits the sentence before Send. Typing that sentence, or any other sentence, without using the button does not set the flag. After a successful Send, clear the flag. Clear it on `teamView.reset` as well. Do not add a second button, a checkbox, or a prompt scan in this pass.

`src/harness.mjs` includes `request.staff === true` in the request fingerprint array, after the files entry, so a replay cannot apply a different staff value to the same request id.

In `Teams.run`:

- A direct member (`To` or `@Name:`) ignores `staff`. Keep today’s single assignment, with no planner call and no upsert.
- A head turn with `staff` true keeps today’s planner path: one plan call, `planOf`, the 32-specialist cap, `TeamStore.upsert`, one head `team.message` that carries `assignments`, then the assignments in array order, including the existing `revise` stop.
- A head turn with `staff` not true still speaks as the head. It runs the existing import of the user's own `https` URLs before the reply. It then makes one provider call as the head. That call uses a head-reply instruction that asks for one JSON field, `message`, and forbids a roster. This document does not contain that instruction, and the call does not use the planner instruction or the worker instruction. The model writes the reply text. The model does not set `staff`, does not return a roster, and any `agents` field on that response is ignored. Read `message` only. Validate it with the existing 1600-character group-message limit. If `message` is missing, fail the turn with the existing protocol error. Emit one `team.message` from the head with that text and no `assignments` array. Do not call `planOf`. Do not upsert. Do not run the five seats. Do not run every stored member. The phase of this call is not `plan`. The existing provider path still records one `team.call` and one `team.usage` for it. On success the turn returns `{ status: 'finished', reason: 'end_turn' }`.

Omitted `staff` stays false. Do not treat a missing field as true in order to preserve current tests. `test/team.test.mjs` is not part of this pass. Direct cases `@Reviewer:` and `to: 'Researcher'` stay on the direct path.

### 2.3 R3. Edit a seat by name

**verdict:** narrow

**evidence:** The research premise that the team pattern has no `members` branch is false; see section 1. `POST /api/teams/:id/members` remains `Teams.recruit`. `TeamStore.upsert` cannot rename, because the primary key is `(team, name)`. There is still no `PATCH` and no `updateMember`. The roster has no inputs for name, charter, voice, or stage. `docs/ui/interface-contract.md` says strings it does not list stay as they are. A visible editor would change that contract.

**what the assembler may write:**

Add `PATCH /api/teams/:id/members` beside the existing `POST` recruit branch. Do not change recruit. The seat name is JSON, not the UUID the path captures.

Body: `{ name, charter, voice, stage, renameTo }`. `renameTo` is optional. Ignore `model`, `prompt`, and any other field.

`name` identifies the current row, compared case-insensitively. Validate it with `nameOf`. If no member row matches, throw `bad('This agent is not on the team.')`. This route does not insert a row.

`charter` uses `string(..., 600, 'a jurisdiction')`. `voice` uses `string(..., 300, 'a voice')`. `stage` must be one of `research`, `review`, `assemble`, `work`, `verify`. Otherwise throw `bad('Choose a stage: research, review, assemble, work or verify.')`. Do not accept `head`.

If `renameTo` is omitted or null, keep the name. If it is present, validate it with `nameOf`. If it matches the current name case-insensitively, keep the name. If it matches the head name case-insensitively, throw `bad('The head agent already uses this name.')`. If another member already has that name, throw `bad('This team already has an agent with this name.')`.

Add `TeamStore.updateMember`. Update the existing row in place so its `rowid` does not change. Set `name` (when renaming), `charter`, `voice`, and `stage`. Do not set `model`.

If `this.harness.active` has this team id, throw the same error recruit uses: `BloomError('TURN_ACTIVE', 'Wait for the current turn to finish before changing the team.', 409)`.

Return HTTP 200 and the object `Teams.detail` already returns.

The route can ship before the form. Do not add roster inputs. Do not relabel the member row. Do not rewrite `docs/ui/interface-contract.md`. The JSON field for the stored charter is `charter`. Do not add a `role` field.

### 2.4 R4. Do not encode the stored speaking order

**verdict:** accept

**evidence:** Section 4 of the research quotes an untrusted six-step excerpt that gives one seat two turns. `Teams.run` runs each assignment once. `reviewBlocked` stops later assignments only after a `review` stage returns `revise`.

**what the assembler may write:**

Nothing from that excerpt. `Teams.run` does not gain a fixed speaking order, a second turn for one seat, new stage ids, or new agents. The five seeded seats stay on stage `work`, so a `revise` verdict does not skip them.

### 2.5 R5. One transcript

**verdict:** accept

**evidence:** `public/app.js` paints `user.message` and `team.message` in `#transcript`. `team.message` has no recipient. Section 6 is the view.

**what the assembler may write:**

Keep that log. Do not add a second chat, a mailbox table, or a `to` field on `team.message`.

### 2.6 S6. Timeline and route line

**verdict:** narrow

**evidence:** `turn.started` clears `#plan`, `#tools`, and the usage map. `team.call` already appends `${actor} · Planning` or `${actor} · Working` to `#plan`. `team.recall` and `tool.updated` already render on `#tools`. `team.usage` already renders in `#usage`. A head `team.message` with `assignments` already lists `name — assignment` in `public/app.js`. Assignments may also carry `persona: Boolean(persona)`. That flag is not a recipient. `turn.finished` already drives `#turn-state` through the `labels` map in `public/app.js`.

The research table’s order column is a catalog of row types. It is not a sort that overrides event sequence. `team.usage` does not become a timeline row.

**what the assembler may write:**

Keep one center log. After `turn.started` clears the previous activity lists, `#plan` is the timeline for the new turn. Append rows in arrival order. Keep the existing `team.call` append. Do not append a second `team.call` row. Keep the existing `#tools` and `#usage` renderers. Do not copy usage into `#plan`.

Row text, using events the loop already emits:

- `turn.started`: `Turn started`
- `tool.updated`: the title and status label `renderTool` already writes. No new title.
- `team.call`: the existing `${actor} · Planning` when `phase` is `plan`, otherwise `${actor} · Working`
- `team.usage`: no timeline row
- `team.recall`: the existing `${actor} · notes reused · ${count} notes` when `hit` is true, otherwise `${actor} · notes loaded · ${count} notes`
- `team.message`: the author. When `verdict` is present, also `Review approved` for `approve`, and `Changes requested` for any other verdict
- `turn.finished`: `labels[data.status]` from `public/app.js`, or `data.status` when the map has no entry

Do not invent a route event.

Route line, only on a `team.message` whose `assignments` array is present. Under the list `public/app.js` already renders (`name — assignment`), add one text line: the author, then `, `, then each `assignments[].name` in array order, separated by `, `. Example shape: `Lead, Planner, Reviewer`. No arrow. No word “to”. Do not read or write a recipient. Do not put the `persona` boolean on this line.

When a later `team.message` in the same turn has `verdict` `revise`, find that author in the assignments array. On the order line, append ` (not run)` to each assignment name that follows that author. Leave the names visible. If that author is not in the array, append the suffix to nobody.

A direct turn has no `phase: plan` call and one worker `team.message`. Do not add an order line. The route is that author, already shown as the message header.

A verify seat emits `team.message` and no `team.call`. Its timeline row is the message row. Do not invent a `team.call` for it.

## 3. Include list

The assembler may write only the following behavior.

- The collision check, the five `members` inserts, and the profile values in section 2.1.
- The `staff` boolean, the sample-button flag, the fingerprint entry, and the three `Teams.run` branches in section 2.2.
- `PATCH /api/teams/:id/members` and `TeamStore.updateMember` in section 2.3, with no roster form.
- The timeline rows and the assignment-order line in section 2.6.
- Files that may change: `src/teams.mjs`, `src/team-store.mjs`, `src/http.mjs`, `src/harness.mjs`, `public/team.js`, `public/app.js`.

Accepted strings, copied exactly:

- Collision error: a message that names the starter seats.
- Charter: `Help the user shape the next agent.`
- Voice: `Clear and specific.`
- Stage for all five inserts: `work`
- Sample sentence: `Create a researcher to extract claims from the attached sources, a reviewer to check them, and an assembler to write a guide. Flag any evidence gaps.`
- Unknown member: `This agent is not on the team.`
- Head-name clash on rename: `The head agent already uses this name.`
- Member-name clash on rename: `This team already has an agent with this name.`
- Bad stage: `Choose a stage: research, review, assemble, work or verify.`
- Active turn: `Wait for the current turn to finish before changing the team.`
- Timeline row for start: `Turn started`
- Not-run suffix, including the leading space: ` (not run)`

`staff: true` on a head turn keeps the current planner path. `staff` other than `true`, on a head turn, runs the existing `https` import, makes one provider call as the head, and emits one `team.message` from the head with no `assignments` array. That path does not call `planOf`, does not upsert, and does not run the five seats or every stored member. The model writes the reply text. The model does not set `staff`. The reply JSON is `message` only, checked with the existing 1600-character group-message limit. A missing `message` fails with the existing protocol error. The sample button may set `staff: true` for the next Send.

## 4. Leave-out list

Leave these out of the assembler pass.

- A mailbox, a second chat, and a `to` field on `team.message`.
- A per-member model. The five inserts store `model` null. `updateMember` does not change `model`. Do not add a seat model control.
- A prompt column.
- A sixth seeded seat. The head is the `teams` row. Do not insert these five into the persona library.
- Any seeded stage other than `work`. Do not seed `review`, `assemble`, or `verify`. Do not add a stage id. Do not order assignments so a `revise` verdict skips the starter seats. The existing `reviewBlocked` rule stays as it is.
- The untrusted six-step excerpt as `Teams.run`. Do not run one seat twice. Do not add agents or stages for that excerpt.
- A prompt scan, on the server or in the browser, that decides `staff`.
- A loop that runs every stored member on a head turn whose `staff` is not true.
- An insert on `PATCH /api/teams/:id/members`.
- A visible member editor, a roster relabel, and any edit to `docs/ui/interface-contract.md` or any other file under `docs/ui/`.
- Any edit to `docs/backend/research/agent-runtime-patterns.md`.
- A new route event, a usage row inside `#plan`, and an arrow or recipient on the assignment-order line.
- Prompt text copied into charter, voice, docs, or tests.
- Setting omitted `staff` to true.

# CAP-04: Workspace tool set and coding loop

- ID: `CAP-04`
- Title: Workspace tool set and coding loop
- Lead: `bloom`
- Touches: `drosera`
- Horizon: `now`
- Milestone: `M2`
- CLI phase: `P2`
- Status: `in-progress`
- Claim: `specified`
- Depends on: `CAP-03`

## Why

Bloom's coding sessions (`src/harness.mjs`) currently run only the scripted demonstration adapter (`src/demo.mjs`) and ship no live coding runtime (`docs/architecture.md`). A local coding loop needs deterministic workspace tools bound to the session workspace root so an agent can inspect, search, edit, test, and finish cleanly without escaping the workspace or racing on concurrent writes.

## What it does

- Defines seven neutral tools whose faces and recipe live in `drosera` (`CAP-04.1`) and whose execution runs inside `bloom` (`CAP-04.2`, `CAP-04.3`):
  - Read tools: `workspace.file.read`, `workspace.dir.list`, `workspace.text.search`, and `run.answer.create`.
  - Write tools: `workspace.file.write`, `workspace.file.update`, and `workspace.shell.execute`.
- Read takes `path` and optional one-based inclusive `startLine` and `endLine`. List and literal search use an optional `path` rooted at the workspace. Search requires `query`. Write takes `path` and `content`. Update takes `path`, `oldText`, and `newText`. Command takes `command` and optional string array `args`. Finish takes `text`.
- Contains file tool paths: file tool path parameters resolve relative to the session's canonical workspace root (`realpath` of `session.workspace` in `src/harness.mjs`). File tools check symlink targets and refuse outside paths before content I/O.
- Serializes writes per canonical file path: concurrent `workspace.file.write` and `workspace.file.update` calls targeting the same file wait on a per-path queue so updates never interleave or drop edits.
- Caps tool output deterministically: retain a UTF-8 prefix with no partial code point, report `truncatedBytes`, and include the SHA-256 hex digest of the full decoded output.
- Integrates the coding loop into Bloom's runtime: each model call passes through `src/provider.mjs` (`validateProvider` and `normalizeGeneration`), validates inputs and outputs per `CAP-03`, checks tool admission against `allowedTools`, executes workspace tools locally, and finishes explicitly when `run.answer.create` runs.

## Contract touchpoints

- `docs/architecture.md`: coding runtime seam (`run(input, hooks)`), provider seam (`src/provider.mjs`), and OS-account / workspace trust boundary.
- `drosera/docs/contracts/tools.md` and `drosera/docs/contracts/cookbook.md` (`CAP-04.1`): workspace and finish tool face pack and coding-loop recipe.
- `seed/docs/contracts/tool-id.md` and `seed/docs/contracts/run-model.md`: tool-ID grammar, reading classes, intent-first recording, and `allowedTools` admission.

## Tool IDs and events

### Tool IDs

| Tool ID | Effect | Third-party egress | Owner gate | Summary |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `workspace.file.read` | `read` | `false` | `false` | Read file contents or bounded line ranges inside the workspace root |
| `workspace.dir.list` | `read` | `false` | `false` | List directory entries inside the workspace root |
| `workspace.text.search` | `read` | `false` | `false` | Search text patterns across files inside the workspace root |
| `workspace.file.write` | `write` | `false` | `false` | Create or overwrite a file inside the workspace root |
| `workspace.file.update` | `write` | `false` | `false` | Apply targeted edits to an existing file inside the workspace root |
| `workspace.shell.execute` | `write` | `false` | `false` | Run an allowlisted command with the workspace as the working directory, after per-call approval |
| `run.answer.create` | `read` | `false` | `false` | Emit the structured final response that ends the coding loop |

### Events

| Event | Producer | Payload fields | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `tool.updated` | `bloom` (`src/coding-loop.mjs`) | `id`, `toolId`, `effect`, `summary`, `status`, `durationMs`, `approval`, `bytes`, `truncatedBytes`, `outputSha256`, and for commands `exitCode`, `timedOut`, `output`, `homeCleanupFailed` | One trace row per call; the summary names paths and commands, never file contents |
| `model.call` | `bloom` (`src/coding-loop.mjs`) | `call`, `durationMs`, `model`, `complete`, `usage` | One trace row per generation; `usage` is `null` when unreported |
| `permission.requested` | `bloom` (`src/coding-loop.mjs`) | `id`, `toolId`, `effect`, `summary`, `detail`, `options`, and for commands `command`, `args` | Raised before every write and command |
| `assistant.delta` | `bloom` (`src/coding-loop.mjs`) | `text`, `final` | Streamed reply text; `final: true` marks the answer from `run.answer.create` |
| `turn.finished` | `bloom` (`src/harness.mjs`) | `status`, `reason` | Emitted when the coding loop terminates via finish action, cancel, or error |

## Acceptance tests

- `workspace-root-containment-refuses-escape`: traversal segments and symlinks escaping the workspace root fail closed before any read or write.
- `per-path-write-serialization`: concurrent `workspace.file.write` and `workspace.file.update` calls on one canonical path execute sequentially with no lost edits.
- `capped-output-reports-truncated-bytes-and-sha256`: oversized tool output truncates to budget and includes exact `truncatedBytes` plus SHA-256 of the untruncated output.
- `coding-loop-finishes-via-run-answer-create`: coding loop dispatches provider generations behind `src/provider.mjs`, runs admitted tools, and stops cleanly on `run.answer.create`.
- `unadmitted-tool-rejected-before-execution`: any tool outside the objective's `allowedTools` list is refused before execution.
- `coding-loop-fixes-fixture-offline`: the loop fixes the synthetic project's failing test through approved calls with zero network calls.
- `demo-session-fixture-is-lf`, `demo-session-export-is-byte-stable`: the recorded session stays LF and matches a fresh stable export on every platform.
- `reject-is-never-executed`, `allow-session-binds-args-digest`, `headless-never-writes`, `trace-row-per-call-without-file-contents`, `endpoint-marker-never-in-events-or-export`.
- `shell-refuses-unlisted-command`, `shell-refuses-absolute-and-parent-args`, `shell-refuses-symlinked-outside-arg`, `shell-refuses-eval-flags`, `shell-home-is-isolated`, `shell-home-cleanup-failure-flagged`, `command-access-has-one-production-caller`.
- `stream-usage-null-when-unreported`, `abort-returns-no-completed-record`.
- `make-sandbox-creates-baseline-commit`, `make-sandbox-refuses-non-empty-or-inside-clone`, `web-workspace-runs-coding-loop-from-private-config`, `web-workspace-refuses-cloud-and-has-no-endpoint-option`, `web-coding-view-formats-rows`, `live-test-runbook-commands-exist`, `live-test-runbook-keeps-endpoint-private`.
- `cloud-refused-without-flag-and-config`, `cloud-refused-outside-sandbox`, `cloud-reads-ask-first`, `key-and-endpoint-markers-never-printed`, `npm-test-does-not-load-live-tests`.

## Slices

- `CAP-04.1` (`drosera`, milestone `M2`, status `landed`): Workspace and finish tool faces pack and recipe.
- `CAP-04.2` (`bloom`, milestone `M2`, status `landed`): Workspace root path containment, write serialization, capped digest output.
- `CAP-04.3` (`bloom`, milestone `M2`, status `landed`): Coding loop integration with workspace tools and finish action. Before `workspace.shell.execute` runs outside tests, all of these hold: the exact command allowlist `node`, `npm` and `git`, resolved against a fixed search path; refusal of interpreter eval and redirect flags (`node -e`, `--eval`, `-p`, `--print`, `-r`, `--require`, `--import`, `--input-type`; `npm exec`, `npm x`, `npm --prefix`; `git -C`, `--git-dir`, `--work-tree`, `-c`, `--exec-path`; and `sh`, `bash`, `cmd` and `powershell` as commands); refusal of arguments that are absolute, contain `..`, or resolve outside the workspace, including through links and in `--flag=value`; an isolated per-run `HOME` (and `USERPROFILE` on Windows); per-call approval with no session-wide allow for commands; the owner's network answer, verbatim (2026-11-24): "I accept option A for bloom's coding shell: network not blocked; npm offline; git local-only; risk documented"; and tests for each in `test/shell-gate.test.mjs` and `test/coding-loop.test.mjs`.

## Non-goals

- Importing `drosera` inside `bloom` at runtime before an explicit package adoption task.
- Virtual path remapping or default-off shell scope isolation across custom roots (`CAP-17`).
- The approval modal and resume (`CAP-06.4`) or trace HTML export (`CAP-10`).
- An operating-system sandbox or network block for commands.

## Family rules and conflicts

- Tool faces and recipe definitions belong in `drosera` (`CAP-04.1`); execution and workspace I/O belong in `bloom` (`CAP-04.2`, `CAP-04.3`).
- Every tool ID conforms to `seed` grammar and every provider call runs behind `src/provider.mjs`.
- Zero new runtime dependencies.

## Open owner decisions

# CAP-08: Seat orchestration

- ID: `CAP-08`
- Title: Seat orchestration
- Lead: `bloom`
- Touches: `seed`
- Horizon: `next`
- Milestone: `M3`
- CLI phase: `P3`
- Status: `proposed`
- Claim: `planned`
- Depends on: `CAP-07`

## Why

Bloom's team loop (`src/teams.mjs`) coordinates a head planner and specialist stages sequentially, while `docs/backend/agent-runtime.md` tracks team seats in database `members` rows. Multi-seat runs need declarative seat definitions keyed by role IDs rather than hardcoded character names or per-agent instruction files, pre-run validation so broken team documents fail before any model call, and bounded parallel fan-out that merges results deterministically in plan order.

## What it does

- Preserves deterministic coordinator and verifier roles: the head (`chair`) plans seat assignments, specialists execute in plan order, a `revise` verdict stops downstream assembly, and the deterministic verifier checks file integrity and invariants without calling any model.
- Stores seats strictly as structured data in `src/seats.mjs` alongside persisted `members` rows in `src/team-store.mjs`: stored rows, events, tool IDs, and model prompts carry closed role IDs only (`chair`, `framing`, `risk`, `coherence`, `sequencing`), never per-agent instruction files and never display names; display labels come from the design canon and are read **only by renderers** (pending owner ruling `D12`).
- Validates the declarative team document before a run starts (`CAP-08.1` in `seed`, wired in `CAP-08.2`): passes parsed `agents` and `tools` documents through `seed`'s `checkRegistryDocuments` plus tool-ID grammar checks (`parseToolId` / `checkRegistry`) and stops before any model call if any reference or ID is invalid.
- Adds bounded parallel fan-out (`CAP-08.3`): independent steps marked for parallel execution run under a strict concurrency cap, a per-step timeout, and a per-seat tool subset strictly contained within the objective's `allowedTools`, merging outputs deterministically in plan order.

## Contract touchpoints

- `docs/architecture.md`: coordinator, specialist, and deterministic verifier roles, admission checks, and review hold behavior.
- `docs/backend/agent-runtime.md`: `members` table persistence, direct vs planned execution paths, and deterministic verifier step semantics.
- `seed/docs/contracts/tool-id.md` (`CAP-08.1`): `checkRegistryDocuments`, tool-ID grammar checks, and `allowedTools` constraints.
- `seed/docs/contracts/run-model.md`: objective `allowedTools` and deterministic ordering rules.

## Tool IDs and events

### Tool IDs

| Tool ID | Effect | Third-party egress | Owner gate | Summary |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |

None. This capability introduces no tool IDs.

### Events

| Event | Producer | Payload fields | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `team.call` | `bloom` (`src/teams.mjs`) | `actor`, `roleId`, `calls`, `limit`, `phase`, `stepIndex` | Records seat role ID and step order for planned and fan-out calls |
| `team.message` | `bloom` (`src/teams.mjs`) | `author`, `roleId`, `text`, `epoch`, `assignments`, `verdict` | Carries ordered assignments, review verdicts, and deterministic verifier output |
| `team.usage` | `bloom` (`src/teams.mjs`) | `actor`, `roleId`, `calls`, `limit`, `model`, `usage`, `costUSD` | Records per-seat usage independently through `src/provider.mjs` |

## Acceptance tests

- `invalid-team-document-stops-before-model-call`: malformed `agents` or `tools` document, unknown tool in `allowedTools`, or invalid tool ID stops via `checkRegistryDocuments` before invoking the provider.
- `revise-verdict-blocks-assembly`: a specialist review returning `revise` halts assembly and downstream assignments.
- `deterministic-verifier-makes-zero-model-calls`: verifier seat validates hashes and invariants deterministically with zero calls to `provider.generate`.
- `seats-data-uses-role-ids-only-no-instruction-files`: `src/seats.mjs`, `members` rows, emitted events, tool IDs, and model prompts carry only `chair`, `framing`, `risk`, `coherence`, and `sequencing` role IDs with no display names or instruction markdown files, while display labels come from the design canon and are read only by renderers (pending `D12`).
- `bounded-fanout-respects-concurrency-timeout-and-tool-subset`: parallel fan-out enforces max concurrency, cancels/times out slow steps at per-step limit, and rejects tools outside the seat's subset of objective `allowedTools`.
- `fanout-merges-results-in-plan-order`: regardless of completion arrival order, merged messages and artifacts match original plan step order.

## Slices

- `CAP-08.1` (`seed`, milestone `M3`, status `proposed`): Declarative team document validation checks.
- `CAP-08.2` (`bloom`, milestone `M3`, status `proposed`): Declarative seats data, role IDs, and deterministic verifier handoff.
- `CAP-08.3` (`bloom`, milestone `M3`, status `proposed`): Bounded parallel fan-out with timeout, tool subset, and plan-order merge.

## Non-goals

- Storing per-seat prompt or instruction markdown files in the repository (`AGENTS.md` prohibits agent instruction directories).
- Allowing any seat to expand `allowedTools` beyond the objective's admitted set.
- Defining the plan review state machine or owner plan-gate records (`CAP-07` in `aestivation`).

## Family rules and conflicts

- Stored seat rows (`src/seats.mjs` and `members` rows), events, tool IDs, and model prompts carry only the five closed role IDs (`chair`, `framing`, `risk`, `coherence`, `sequencing`); display labels come from the design canon and are read **only by renderers** (pending `D12`).
- Pre-run validation delegates to `seed`'s `checkRegistryDocuments` and `parseToolId` rather than duplicating registry validation in Bloom.
- Sequencing note: `CAP-08` (`M3`) depends on `CAP-07` (`M3`), which depends on `CAP-06.1` (owner-gate decision record at `M3`, with `CAP-07.3` plan-digest binding folded into `CAP-06.1` under `D14`), keeping all of `CAP-08` inside `M3`.

## Open owner decisions

- `D12` (pending owner ruling): seats ruling confirming that `src/seats.mjs` and `members` rows store closed role IDs (`chair`, `framing`, `risk`, `coherence`, `sequencing`) while display labels live in the design canon and are read only by renderers, how `src/seats.mjs` aligns with or supersedes starter `members` rows in `docs/backend/agent-runtime.md`, plus default concurrency cap and step timeout values.
- `D14` (pending owner confirmation unless overridden): `CAP-06.1` ships at `M3` with `CAP-07.3` folded in so `CAP-07` depends on `CAP-06.1` at `M3`.

## Evidence

- None yet (`claim: planned`).

## Changes

- `2026-11-23`: Clarified role-ID storage vs renderer-only design-canon display labels (`D12`), updated `CAP-07` sequencing note to `CAP-06.1` at `M3` (`D14`), and added `M3` slice milestones.
- `2026-11-23`: Initial capability specification created in Phase 0 timeline scaffold.

# CAP-10: Trace and observability

- ID: `CAP-10`
- Title: Trace and observability
- Lead: `bloom`
- Touches: `seed`
- Horizon: `next`
- Milestone: `M4`
- CLI phase: `P4`
- Status: `proposed`
- Claim: `planned`
- Depends on: `CAP-04`

## Why

`Store` (`src/store.mjs`) and SSE streaming (`src/http.mjs`) already persist and stream numbered events, but team and coding turns emit different payloads without uniform correlation IDs, there is no `bloom trace` replay or static HTML export command, and private content plus endpoint privacy rules require explicit digest redaction across stored events and exports.

## What it does

- Unifies team and coding runs onto one append-only typed event stream with monotonic sequence numbers (`seq`) and correlation IDs (`run`, `attempt`, `step`, `seat`) specified in `CAP-10.1` (`seed`) and emitted by `bloom` (`CAP-10.2`).
- Supports four read-only renderer views driven strictly from the persisted event stream (renderers never mutate run state or call providers):
  1. Full state post-step view
  2. Deltas-only view
  3. Debug view (correlation IDs, digests, counts, refusal codes)
  4. Token deltas view (streamed model text chunks)
- Implements `bloom trace <run>` (`CAP-10.3`) to replay a stored run step-by-step in the terminal or export a self-contained static HTML trace report with zero external network links or third-party assets.
- Enforces digest redaction and endpoint privacy: private content (private notes, redacted tool or memory payloads) is logged using SHA-256 digests and byte/character counts rather than raw private text, and configured provider endpoint addresses and credentials are never recorded in events or exports.
- Aggregates per-seat and per-step usage across `seed`'s five-field token record (`input`, `output`, `total`, `cacheRead`, `cacheWrite`) and optional reported `costUSD`, keeping unreported metrics `null`.

## Contract touchpoints

- `docs/architecture.md`: durable event sequence numbers, SSE replay, provider usage ledger (`costUSD` beside usage), and private-note scoping.
- `seed/docs/contracts/run-model.md` (`CAP-10.1`): correlation IDs (`run`, `attempt`, `step`, `seat`) on run trace records.
- `seed/docs/contracts/provider.md`: normalized five-field `usage` record.

## Tool IDs and events

### Tool IDs

| Tool ID | Effect | Third-party egress | Owner gate | Summary |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |

None. This capability introduces no tool IDs.

### Events

| Event | Producer | Payload fields | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `turn.started` | `bloom` (`src/store.mjs`) | `seq`, `run`, `attempt`, `model`, `title` | Starts correlated trace span for a run attempt |
| `assistant.delta` | `bloom` (`src/harness.mjs`) | `seq`, `run`, `attempt`, `step`, `seat`, `text` | Streamed text delta consumed by the token-delta view |
| `tool.updated` | `bloom` (`src/harness.mjs`) | `seq`, `run`, `attempt`, `step`, `seat`, `toolId`, `status`, `outputSha256`, `truncatedBytes` | Typed tool lifecycle record with digest metadata |
| `team.call` | `bloom` (`src/teams.mjs`) | `seq`, `run`, `attempt`, `step`, `seat`, `actor`, `phase` | Correlated model dispatch marker |
| `team.usage` | `bloom` (`src/teams.mjs`) | `seq`, `run`, `attempt`, `step`, `seat`, `model`, `usage`, `costUSD` | Per-seat and per-step token usage and reported cost |
| `team.recall` | `bloom` (`src/teams.mjs`) | `seq`, `run`, `attempt`, `step`, `seat`, `hit`, `count`, `digests` | Records memory participation using digests/counts under strict redaction |
| `turn.finished` | `bloom` (`src/store.mjs`) | `seq`, `run`, `attempt`, `status`, `reason` | Closes correlated trace span |

## Acceptance tests

- `stream-preserves-monotonic-seq-and-correlation-ids`: every emitted event carries strictly increasing `seq` and valid `run`, `attempt`, `step`, and `seat` correlation IDs.
- `four-renderer-views-read-only-over-same-stream`: full-state, deltas-only, debug, and token-deltas views render deterministically from the persisted event stream without mutating state.
- `bloom-trace-replays-steps-and-exports-self-contained-html`: `bloom trace <run>` replays events step-by-step and emits a single self-contained HTML file with zero external requests.
- `private-content-stored-as-digests-and-endpoint-address-never-recorded`: private memory text and endpoint addresses/credentials never appear in stored events or exported HTML.
- `per-seat-and-per-step-usage-preserves-null-for-missing-metrics`: usage summaries break down token fields and `costUSD` by `seat` and `step` while keeping missing counts as `null`.

## Slices

- `CAP-10.1` (`seed`, milestone `M4`, status `proposed`): Correlation IDs on run trace records.
- `CAP-10.2` (`bloom`, milestone `M4`, status `proposed`): Unified append-only typed event stream and four renderer views.
- `CAP-10.3` (`bloom`, milestone `M4`, status `proposed`): Trace replay command, HTML export, digest redaction, and per-seat usage.

## Non-goals

- Adding a third-party terminal UI library (zero runtime dependencies remain law).
- Streaming traces to a remote observability backend or loading external scripts/styles in HTML exports.
- Estimating missing token counts or fabricating monetary cost savings.

## Family rules and conflicts

- Zero new runtime dependencies: terminal renderer and HTML export use Node.js built-ins and Bloom's self-hosted Nocturne CSS snapshot.
- Renderers are strictly read-only consumers of the event stream.
- Endpoint URLs, credentials, and raw private notes must never reach stored traces or exports.

## Open owner decisions

- `D12` (pending owner ruling): renderer ruling without a third-party TUI library, governing terminal view formatting and planned for `docs/adr/0001-terminal-renderer.md`.

## Evidence

- None yet (`claim: planned`).

## Changes

- `2026-11-23`: Added `M4` slice milestones across `CAP-10.1`..`CAP-10.3` and aligned `D12` ADR status reference.
- `2026-11-23`: Initial capability specification created in Phase 0 timeline scaffold.

# CAP-14: Eval harness

- ID: `CAP-14`
- Title: Eval harness
- Lead: `bloom`
- Touches: `seed`, `trellis`
- Horizon: `next` (`CAP-14.1`, `CAP-14.2` in `M5`; `CAP-14.3`, `CAP-14.4` in `later` `M8`)
- Milestone: `M5` (`CAP-14.1`, `CAP-14.2` at `M5`; `CAP-14.3`, `CAP-14.4` at `M8`)
- CLI phase: `P5`
- Status: `in-progress`
- Claim: `specified`
- Depends on: `CAP-10`

## Why

Bloom needs repeatable, deterministic evaluation over coding and team workflows so changes to prompts, tool schemas, context packing, or orchestration can be measured locally against known cases and saved baselines without manual testing or opaque scores.

## What it does

- Defines a structured dataset format of evaluation cases, each carrying `id`, `input` (prompt, workspace fixture, admitted tools), `expected` assertions, and `metadata` (tags, suite tier, baseline reference).
- Runs deterministic evaluators first on every case:
  - `exact`: exact normalized text equality.
  - `contains`: required substring or pattern presence.
  - `schema-valid`: output conformance via `CAP-03` schema validation.
  - `tool-trajectory`: invoked tool IDs checked in exact order or as an unordered set.
  - `files-changed`: expected modified file paths and content digests inside the isolated fixture workspace.
  - `tests-pass`: deterministic command exit check inside the fixture workspace.
- Supports an optional model-based evaluator only when explicitly enabled, always labeled `judge` in outputs and reports, and never allowed as the sole pass criterion (any deterministic evaluator failure fails the case).
- Executes offline cases against scripted response queues and pure function model test doubles behind `seed`'s provider seam (`CAP-14.1` in `seed`, `src/provider.mjs`).
- Generates an experiment report recording per-case verdict, deterministic evaluator outcomes, optional `judge` score, five-field token usage, reported `costUSD`, duration in milliseconds, and delta against a saved baseline report (`CAP-14.3`).
- Adds `bloom eval --smoke` (`CAP-14.2`) to execute the fast offline smoke dataset deterministically, and exposes `eval.suite.execute` as the neutral tool face.

## Contract touchpoints

- `docs/architecture.md`: provider seam (`src/provider.mjs`), scripted verification boundaries.
- `seed/docs/contracts/provider.md` (`CAP-14.1`): scripted and function model test doubles conforming to `validateProvider` and `normalizeGeneration`.
- `trellis/docs/contracts/probes.md` (`CAP-14.4`): consistency and determinism probes from outside the call path.

## Tool IDs and events

### Tool IDs

| Tool ID | Effect | Third-party egress | Owner gate | Summary |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `eval.suite.execute` | `read` | `false` | `false` | Execute an evaluation suite over a dataset of cases and return a structured report |

### Events

| Event | Producer | Payload fields | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `eval.case.started` | `bloom` | `run`, `caseId`, `dataset`, `smoke` | Marks start of an isolated case run |
| `eval.case.finished` | `bloom` | `run`, `caseId`, `passed`, `evaluators`, `judge`, `usage`, `costUSD`, `durationMs` | Records deterministic results, labeled `judge` if run, usage, and duration |
| `eval.report.written` | `bloom` | `run`, `dataset`, `passedCount`, `failedCount`, `baselineDiff` | Summarizes suite outcome and baseline comparison |

## Acceptance tests

- `smoke-dataset-runs-offline-with-deterministic-evaluators`: `bloom eval --smoke` runs the smoke dataset with zero network calls and produces a deterministic pass/fail report.
- `deterministic-evaluators-cover-exact-contains-schema-trajectory-files-tests`: all six deterministic evaluator kinds (`exact`, `contains`, `schema-valid`, `tool-trajectory`, `files-changed`, `tests-pass`) pass on matching fixtures and fail on mismatches.
- `judge-output-always-labeled-and-never-sole-pass-criterion`: enabling a model judge labels its output `judge` and keeps overall `passed: false` whenever any deterministic check fails.
- `scripted-and-function-doubles-conform-to-seed-provider-seam`: scripted and function model doubles pass `validateProvider` and `normalizeGeneration`.
- `experiment-report-captures-usage-duration-and-baseline-diff`: report emits per-case result, token usage, duration, and baseline diff cleanly.

## Slices

- `CAP-14.1` (`seed`, milestone `M5`, status `proposed`): Scripted and function model test doubles.
- `CAP-14.2` (`bloom`, milestone `M5`, status `proposed`): Smoke eval dataset, deterministic evaluators, and smoke command (`next`, `M5`, `P5`).
- `CAP-14.3` (`bloom`, milestone `M8`, status `proposed`): Full eval suite, labeled judge option, and baseline diff reports (`later`, `M8`).
- `CAP-14.4` (`trellis`, milestone `M8`, status `proposed`): Eval harness consistency and determinism probes (`later`, `M8`).

## Non-goals

- Calling hosted or live network models during `npm test` or `bloom eval --smoke`.
- Allowing an ungrounded model judge to override failing deterministic assertions.
- Mutating the user's real workspace during evaluation (cases run in isolated temporary copies).

## Family rules and conflicts

- Model test doubles belong in `seed` (`CAP-14.1`); eval execution belongs in `bloom` (`CAP-14.2`, `CAP-14.3`); consistency probes belong in `trellis` (`CAP-14.4`) without importing `bloom`.
- Smoke evaluation (`M5`, `P5`) stays decoupled from the full suite (`M8`, `Later`) so `P5` ships early and reliably.

## Open owner decisions

- Decided 2026-11-24 in bloom#16: Should the scripted and pure-function model doubles move to Seed in a later draft PR? I recommend proving them in Bloom first, then upstreaming them. Owner's answer, relayed (owner typed in code-agent chat, not seen by reviewers): "Upstream them later".
- Baseline report storage path and full-suite dataset curation criteria for `M8` (`CAP-14.3`) remain open for owner guidance; `CAP-14.1` and `CAP-14.2` require no blocking decision.

## Evidence

- `test/smoke-eval.test.mjs` runs the smoke command twice with a denied transport, checks deterministic assertions, and exercises both fixture provider doubles through Seed.

## Changes

- 2026-11-24. Add the offline smoke command, six deterministic assertions and case/report events (CAP-14, bloom#16).
- `2026-11-23`: Added explicit `M5` (`CAP-14.1`, `CAP-14.2`) and `M8` (`CAP-14.3`, `CAP-14.4`) slice milestones.
- `2026-11-23`: Initial capability specification created in Phase 0 timeline scaffold.

- Depends on: `CAP-05`, `CAP-07`, `CAP-08`

## Why

Today `src/sources.mjs` (`importURL`) only retrieves literal HTTPS URLs pasted into a brief by the user (`src/teams.mjs`). Complex investigations need coordinator routing between a direct answer and a structured research workflow, optional local context scanning, an owner-approved research plan before external egress, owner-gated source searches, and a reporter that ties every factual claim to recorded sources or labels gaps explicitly.

## What it does

- **Coordinator routing (`CAP-15.4`)**: The coordinator (`chair`) evaluates whether the prompt can be answered directly from admitted local context or requires a multi-step research workflow.
- **Optional background scan**: When local context is needed first, a bounded workspace scan gathers project context via `capillary`'s context packer (`CAP-05`) before planning external research.
- **Owner-approved typed research plan (`CAP-15.2` in `aestivation`)**: Proposes a plan with typed steps (`research`, `analysis`, `processing`) routed through `CAP-07` (`aestivation` validation plus owner approval or edit) before any search or processing step executes.
- **Owner-gated search and read (`CAP-15.1` in `drosera`, `CAP-15.4` in `bloom`)**: External search runs through `research.source.search` (`effect: read`, `thirdPartyEgress: true`), passing through the `CAP-06` owner gate before leaving the owner's system. Retrieved public documents are stored as recorded `capillary` sources with SHA-256 digests (`CAP-15.3`).
- **Cited reporter (`CAP-15.3` in `capillary`, `CAP-15.4` in `bloom`)**: Final research output cites recorded `capillary` source IDs and digests for claims; any claim lacking a supporting recorded source is explicitly flagged as uncited rather than presented as verified.
- **Plan revision and step caps**: Research plans enforce strict per-run step limits and plan revision limits; reaching either limit stops further exploration and reports the limit reason cleanly.

## Contract touchpoints

- `docs/architecture.md`: public source retrieval rules (`src/sources.mjs`), coordinator planning, evidence packet bounds.
- `drosera/docs/contracts/tools.md` (`CAP-15.1`): `research.source.search` tool face with `thirdPartyEgress: true`.
- `aestivation/docs/contracts/plan.md` (`CAP-15.2`): typed research steps (`research`, `analysis`, `processing`) and step/revision caps.
- `capillary/docs/contracts/retrieval.md` (`CAP-15.3`): cited source attachment and uncited-claim flagging.

## Tool IDs and events

### Tool IDs

| Tool ID | Effect | Third-party egress | Owner gate | Summary |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `research.source.search` | `read` | `true` | `true` | Search public sources through an owner-gated external connector |

### Events

| Event | Producer | Payload fields | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `plan.proposed` | `bloom` / `aestivation` | `run`, `planDigest`, `steps`, `stepTypes` | Emitted when coordinator proposes a typed research plan |
| `plan.decision` | `bloom` | `run`, `planDigest`, `decision` | Records owner approval, edit, or rejection via `CAP-07` before research egress |
| `permission.requested` | `bloom` (`src/harness.mjs`) | `id`, `toolId`, `argsDigest`, `thirdPartyEgress` | Owner gate prompt for `research.source.search` per `CAP-06` |
| `context.packet` | `bloom` / `capillary` | `run`, `sourceIds`, `digests`, `omissions` | Records scan and fetched source attachments without raw private leaks |

## Acceptance tests

- `coordinator-routes-direct-answer-vs-research-plan`: simple local requests answer directly while multi-source investigations enter the research flow.
- `research-plan-requires-owner-approval-before-egress`: typed research steps (`research`, `analysis`, `processing`) pause for `CAP-07` owner approval before calling search or processing.
- `research-source-search-triggers-third-party-egress-gate`: invoking `research.source.search` enforces `thirdPartyEgress: true` and `ownerGate: true` via `CAP-06`.
- `reporter-cites-recorded-sources-and-labels-uncited-claims`: factual claims link to recorded `capillary` source IDs and any unsupported claim carries an explicit uncited label.
- `step-and-revision-caps-halt-run-with-reason`: exceeding research step cap or plan revision cap terminates further research deterministically with a stated reason.

## Slices

- `CAP-15.1` (`drosera`, milestone `M8`, status `proposed`): Research source search face with third-party egress metadata.
- `CAP-15.2` (`aestivation`, milestone `M8`, status `proposed`): Typed research plan steps and step/revision caps.
- `CAP-15.3` (`capillary`, milestone `M8`, status `proposed`): Cited source attachment and uncited-claim flagging.
- `CAP-15.4` (`bloom`, milestone `M8`, status `proposed`): Coordinator research routing, scan, gated search, and cited reporter.

## Non-goals

- Allowing a model to initiate unapproved outbound web searches or crawl private networks (`src/sources.mjs` keeps public IPv4/HTTPS restrictions).
- Fabricating citations or concealing unverified claims as source-backed findings.
- Adopting `capillary`, `aestivation`, or `drosera` inside `bloom` before their `M2`/`M3` integration slices land.

## Family rules and conflicts

- Model output never initiates unapproved network egress; `research.source.search` carries `thirdPartyEgress: true` and `ownerGate: true` per `seed/docs/contracts/tool-id.md`.
- Unknown or missing source support stays explicitly labeled uncited per the family engineering law.

## Open owner decisions

- Default step cap, plan revision cap, and permitted public search connector bindings remain open for owner decision ahead of `M8`.

## Evidence

- None yet (`claim: planned`).

## Changes

- `2026-11-23`: Added `M8` slice milestones across `CAP-15.1`..`CAP-15.4`.
- `2026-11-23`: Initial capability specification created in Phase 0 timeline scaffold.

# Changelog

Earlier history lives in git history and [docs/architecture.md](architecture.md).

## Unreleased

### Added

- Run the deterministic coding smoke dataset with `bloom eval --smoke` and emit case and report events (CAP-14, bloom#16).
- Terminal shell with private endpoint configuration (M1, bloom#1).
- Phase 0 capability ledger scaffold and Bloom lead specifications (`CAP-04`, `CAP-08`, `CAP-10`, `CAP-14`, `CAP-15`) (CAP-01, bloom#2).
- Standalone capability ledger checks and scaffold squash evidence (CAP-02, bloom#3).
- Workspace file tools contained to the workspace root, serialized writes, bounded output, and a command executor that stays disabled until argument containment lands (CAP-04, bloom#4).
- Coding loop for `bloom chat --workspace` and `bloom run --workspace` with strict actions, per-call approvals, streamed text, trace rows, and an allowlisted command gate (CAP-04, bloom#5).
- Pre-dispatch argument checks and output checks sharing one repair turn (CAP-03, bloom#5).
- `bloom doctor --probe` model profile capture, with the coding loop's budget and streaming taken from the saved profile (CAP-16, bloom#7).
- Live-test kit: a sandbox maker, the web workspace's coding view with model rows, tool rows and approval detail, and the `docs/live-test.md` runbook (CAP-04, bloom#8).
- Cloud provider opt-in with `--allow-cloud` in a make-sandbox folder, Gemini OpenAI-compatible probe and error mapping, and opt-in `npm run test:live` (CAP-16, bloom#9).
- Name videsign roles in the terminal trace, and show model and tool budgets with a diff-aware output viewer in the page (CAP-10, bloom#15).

### Changed

- Harden the command gate: distinct refusal reasons, linked-folder argument containment, `.git` write refusal, git config overrides, npm network-flag refusal, attached short-option paths, `node --run` refusal, and allow-only approvals (CAP-04, bloom#5).
- Terminal cloud providers need `--allow-cloud` inside a make-sandbox folder; while cloud is on, reads ask first, session allow is off, team sessions are refused, and model rows say cloud (CAP-16, bloom#9).
- Pin seed and drosera to the commits their main carries, move the lock file and the recorded seed pin with them, and state both imports in the province note (CAP-04, bloom#14).

### Fixed

- Check Windows metadata paths against the resolved `.git` directory and use Git to configure the command gate test repository (CAP-04, bloom#5).
- Close the coding-loop test store before deleting its temp tree, and keep fixtures as LF, so Windows CI no longer fails on EBUSY unlinks or CRLF session exports (CAP-04, bloom#5).
- Close the web coding-loop store before deleting its temp tree, and accept CRLF in live-test runbook fences (CAP-04, bloom#8).

### Removed

- The `npm start -- --api-base` option. The web workspace reads its endpoint only from the private `config.json` (CAP-04, bloom#8).

# Live test runbook

This runbook takes the coding loop from an offline rehearsal to a first live run against your own local model, in a throwaway sandbox. Every write and every command asks first. Run the commands from the folder that holds your checkouts. `<sandbox folder>` is a new or empty folder outside any git clone, and `<your-endpoint>` is your model server's chat-completions base URL.

The endpoint lives only in the private config file described below. Never put it on a command line, in an environment variable, in a chat message or in a shared log. Bloom prints the provider by its config name and locality, never by its address.

## Offline rehearsal

These steps call no model and need no config file.

Run the test suite:

```bash
cd bloom && npm install && npm test
```

Step through the recorded coding session, pressing Enter to advance:

```bash
cd bloom && node bin/bloom.mjs replay test/fixtures/demo-session.jsonl --step
```

Run the scripted model against a fresh sandbox. It asks before each write and command and ends with the sandbox's git diff:

```bash
cd bloom && node scripts/scripted-run.mjs <sandbox folder>
```

The shell rows show the demo test failing (`pass 0 fail 1`) and then passing (`pass 1 fail 0`). The diff adds `NOTES.md` and changes `value < end` to `value <= end` in `src/range.mjs`.

## Config

Bloom reads `config.json` from its data directory, `~/.bloom` unless you pass `--data-dir`. Create the file yourself in a text editor, readable only by your account, and keep it out of every repository:

```json
{
  "version": 1,
  "providers": {
    "lab": { "kind": "chat-completions", "baseURL": "<your-endpoint>", "locality": "local" }
  },
  "models": {
    "aliases": [{ "alias": "coder", "backendModel": "<your model ID>", "workload": "code" }],
    "default": "coder"
  }
}
```

The provider name, here `lab`, is how Bloom refers to the provider in its output. A server on your private network needs `"locality": "local"`, and a plain HTTP server also needs `"allowInsecureHttp": true`. If your server requires a key, the README's Terminal commands section names the provider field that holds the name of the environment variable your shell keeps the key in. Put the key only in that variable, never in the file, a flag or the chat.

Check the file without sending anything to the server:

```bash
cd bloom && node bin/bloom.mjs doctor
```

The Endpoint rule row should read `pass` and name the provider and its locality.

## Probe

Ask the server what it supports and save its model profile:

```bash
cd bloom && node bin/bloom.mjs doctor --probe
```

The probe sends two requests: the models list, and one fixed one-token streaming request that carries nothing of yours. Each row reads `pass`, `fail` or `unknown`. Reachability, Model IDs and Model should pass. Context length, Tool calling and Constrained output stay `unknown` unless the server publishes them, and that is fine. The command exits 1 if any row fails. The saved profile sets the coding loop's prompt budget and whether it streams. The offline version of the probe runs in `npm test` against a fake server.

## Live run

Make a fresh sandbox, then start the coding loop in it:

```bash
cd bloom && node scripts/make-sandbox.mjs <sandbox folder>
```

```bash
cd bloom && node bin/bloom.mjs chat --workspace <sandbox folder>
```

At the prompt, type the same task the rehearsal uses:

```text
Create NOTES.md with one line describing this project. Run the tests, fix the failing test, run the tests again, and finish with a short summary.
```

Read each approval before you answer it. Approve writes and test commands in the sandbox, and reject anything else. When the loop finishes, look at what changed:

```bash
cd <sandbox folder> && env -u GEMINI_API_KEY git -c core.fsmonitor=false --no-pager status && env -u GEMINI_API_KEY git -c core.fsmonitor=false --no-pager diff --no-ext-diff
```

The run passes when all of these hold:

- Text streams as the model writes it, and a model row follows each call.
- Every tool call shows one trace row with its tool, summary, status and timing, and no file contents.
- Bloom asked before every write and every command, and nothing you rejected ran.
- The sandbox tests fail first, and pass after the fix.
- The loop ends with an answer, and the diff holds only the note and the fix.
- No output shows the endpoint.

## Web view

The same run in the browser, against a second fresh sandbox:

```bash
cd bloom && node scripts/make-sandbox.mjs <sandbox folder>
```

```bash
cd bloom && npm start -- --workspace <sandbox folder>
```

Open the local page the command prints, choose a coding session with the sandbox folder, and send the task. The conversation streams the replies and ends with an Answer message. The activity panel shows a row for each model call and each tool call, with command output under shell rows, and an approval card with the exact change or command before each write and command. Answer approvals in the page. Stop the server with Ctrl-C, then check the diff as in the live run. To see the same view with no model at all, start Bloom with `npm run demo` and create a coding session: the scripted demo runtime drives it.

## Troubleshooting

- **Reachability fails with `refused`:** the server is not running, or the address in the config is wrong. Fix the config file and probe again.
- **`timeout`:** the server answered too slowly. The models list gets 5 seconds and the streaming check 30.
- **`tls`:** the server's certificate is not trusted. Use a trusted certificate, or for a plain HTTP server on your own network set `"allowInsecureHttp": true`.
- **`http-401` or `http-403`:** the server wants a key. Set the key field described in the README and keep the key in your shell's environment.
- **`http-404`:** the base URL usually needs its API path, such as one ending in `/v1`.
- **Model fails:** the alias's backend model is not among the listed IDs. Copy the exact ID from the Model IDs row into `backendModel`.
- **The run stops as `malformed`:** the model did not reply with exactly one fenced json action, even after one repair turn. Try a model that follows instructions more closely.
- **A command is refused:** only `node`, `npm` and `git` run, with arguments inside the workspace. The refusal message names the rule.
- **Replies arrive all at once:** the probe saw that the server does not stream, so the loop asks for whole replies.

## Google AI Studio

Use your provider's OpenAI-compatible base URL as `<cloud-endpoint>` (the provider's own documentation names it) with a cloud provider and the model id `gemini-4-hydrogen` (or the id your AI Studio list shows). Example provider entry:

```json
"aistudio": {
  "kind": "chat-completions",
  "baseURL": "<cloud-endpoint>",
  "locality": "cloud",
  "apiKeyEnv": "GEMINI_API_KEY"
}
```

Put the key only in the shell (type this yourself; do not paste the value into chat or a file): `read -rs GEMINI_API_KEY && export GEMINI_API_KEY`.

Probe and chat need `--allow-cloud`, and chat only inside a sandbox from `scripts/make-sandbox.mjs`:

```bash
cd bloom && node bin/bloom.mjs doctor --probe --allow-cloud
```

```bash
cd bloom && node scripts/make-sandbox.mjs <sandbox folder>
```

```bash
cd bloom && node bin/bloom.mjs chat --workspace <sandbox folder> --allow-cloud
```

While cloud is on, Bloom asks before the first message leaves the machine and before every tool call, including reads. Model rows say cloud. The web workspace stays local only.
Team sessions never use a cloud provider.
The sandbox marker guards against mistakes; it is not a security boundary.

## Opt-in live tests

Offline `npm test` never loads these. Against your configured provider:

```bash
cd bloom && BLOOM_LIVE=1 npm run test:live
```

At most 20 model calls per run of the whole suite. The suite reads the provider only from bloom's data directory (or `BLOOM_LIVE_DATA_DIR`), never from an endpoint environment variable. When the configured provider is cloud, set `BLOOM_LIVE_ALLOW_CLOUD=1` as well; without that second flag the cloud live tests fail on an assert before any request. `live-loop-fixes-sandbox` is local-only and does not use the cloud flag. Local providers need only `BLOOM_LIVE=1`.

## Residual risk

Approval of each call is the boundary. `npm test` runs whatever the sandbox's `package.json` scripts say, and the model may have written those scripts in a write you approved. Commands can reach the network: npm is set offline (flags that change registry, cache or online mode are refused) and git is limited to local subcommands with fsmonitor, hooks and `diff.external` forced off, but Bloom does not block network access from the process. The isolated `HOME` only changes an environment variable, so a command can still find your real home folder through the operating system. A detached grandchild process can outlive the call. Writes under `.git/` are refused. Use a throwaway sandbox, read every approval, and keep the sandbox away from folders you care about. [architecture.md](architecture.md) has the full command gate.

In cloud mode these leave the machine and go to the provider named in your config (for AI Studio, Google): each task you approve, Bloom's fixed tool instructions, short summaries of earlier tasks and answers in the same session, the model's own replies within the turn, and every tool result you approve, including file contents and command output. Bloom asks before each task is sent and before each tool call; the follow-up requests inside a turn carry only results you already approved and are sent without a further prompt. Your key travels only in the request's Authorization header. What the provider keeps, and for how long, is set by its terms, not by Bloom: Google's Gemini API terms say that on unpaid use, including AI Studio and free quota, Google uses submitted content and responses to improve its products. Use a throwaway sandbox and send nothing you would not publish.
docsPages.head: 064e18b2d868648c48bde32c65f7d07c59968ccd
docsPages.title: Live test runbook
