docsPages.body:
# Implementability review

> **Owner decision, 2026-11-22.** The adjudication "Shared desktop becomes Files" (section 4) and the `Lead name` / `Role` rows are overruled. The research behind them read an unrelated third-party repository; that evidence is removed. `Head agent`, `Jurisdiction` and `Shared desktop` stay, each with a helper line; see section 0 of [the interface contract](../interface-contract.md). All other verdicts stand.

Reviewed `docs/ui/research/familiar-harness-patterns.md` against the browser surface and the team, store, adapter, harness, and model modules. This file is the interface contract input. It does not change source.

## 1. Verdict

**approve**

The label set in research section 5 is coherent and specific enough for one contract. Three proposals need code: a second empty-state button, accepting `allow_always` on the existing approval card, and hiding the team workspace path. Two further rows are locks: team turns stay without an approval card, and team notes do not gain a second cache control.

Re-checked claims that hold:

- `src/opencode.mjs` sets `optionKinds` to `allow_once` and `reject_once` only. An option of any other kind is dropped. If none remain, the adapter returns a cancelled outcome.
- `src/teams.mjs` emits `team.usage` with `calls`, `limit`, `actor`, `model`, `usage`, `measuredTotal`, `incomplete`, and `tokenLimit`.

Research claims about this checkout that are false:

- “`src/opencode.mjs` does not emit a usage event.” After `session/prompt`, if `result.usage` is present, the adapter emits `model.usage` with `input`, `output`, `total`, `cacheRead`, and `cacheWrite`.
- “Only `team.usage` fills `#usage`,” “a direct turn does not write `#usage`,” and “Direct: the region stays empty.” `public/app.js` writes `#usage` on `model.usage`. `public/team.js` clears `#usage` on every `turn.started`, including a coding session, and the line appears when `model.usage` arrives.
- The team expanded line uses the word `write`. It does not use the words `cache write`. The coding-session line in `public/app.js` does use `Cache write`.
- “The README still titles the product ViBloom and tells the reader to create a session and enter a project path.” The README title is `Bloom`. Its try-it steps say to create a team. The document `<title>` is `Bloom`. The header brand is `bloom`. Neither mismatch is a contract edit.

The false usage rows are rejected below. The accepted rows still tell an assembler what to write.

## 2. How a code agent should read the result

Read section 7 first. It is the include list and the leave-out list. The table is the evidence for that list.

- **copy change** means visible text only. Element ids, option values, stored stage ids, event names, and handlers stay. A row whose proposal already matches the screen is recorded and needs no edit.
- **behavior change** means logic, a new control, or a new event, and only where the note names that work. A note that starts with **Lock** is a sentence the contract includes. It adds no control.
- **reject** means the proposal stays out of the contract and out of the implementation.
- Copy the quoted strings exactly. Do not rename ids. Do not edit the research report, the README, planner prompt text, server fallback names, or tests as part of this contract.
- The browser surface is `public/index.html`, `public/app.js`, and `public/team.js`. Strings not listed in section 7 stay as they are.

## 3. Recommendation table

Section 5 and section 6. Repeated recommendations are one row.

| Control | Research proposal | Verdict | Evidence | Note |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `#kind` option `team` | Visible label `Team`. Value stays `team`. | copy change | `public/index.html`: `Agent team` | Label only. |
| `#kind` option `direct` | Visible label `Coding session`. Value stays `direct`. | copy change | `public/index.html`: `Direct coding session` | Label only. |
| `#create-session` when team | `Create team` | copy change | `public/team.js`: `Create team` | Already this text. Record it. |
| `#create-session` when direct | `Create coding session` | copy change | `public/team.js`: `Create session` | Label only, when the direct option is selected. |
| Empty heading | `What should we work on?` | copy change | `public/index.html`: `What should your team work on?` | The paragraph under the heading stays: `Give a head agent a brief. Follow the handoffs and open the files your team produces.` |
| `#empty-start` | Keep `Create a team`. Add `Create a coding session`, opening the same form with Coding session selected. | behavior change | `public/index.html` has one button, `Create a team`. `public/app.js` only opens the form. | One form. Primary sets kind `team`. Second button sets kind `direct` and runs the existing configure path. |
| `#head-name` label | `Lead name` | copy change | `public/index.html`: `Head agent name` | Label only. `checks/browser.mjs` also reads the current label. This contract does not edit that check. |
| `#head-name` value | `Lead` | copy change | `public/index.html`: `value="Lead"` | Already this text. The server fallback `Head agent` is not a visible default and is not part of this contract. |
| `#charter` label | `Role` | copy change | `public/index.html`: `Jurisdiction` | Visible label only. The stored field remains the charter. |
| `#charter` placeholder | `What should this lead be responsible for?` | copy change | `public/index.html`: `What should this head own?` | Placeholder only. |
| Member summary in `#members` | `name · Lead`, `Research`, `Review`, `Assemble`, `Work`, `Check` | copy change | `public/team.js`: `a.name + ' · ' + a.stage`, with the lead stage set to `head` | Display words only. Stored stages stay `research`, `review`, `assemble`, `work`, `verify`. Summary pattern stays `name · Word`. Hint, charter, and voice lines stay. |
| `#prompt` placeholder for a team | `Give your team a task` | copy change | `public/index.html` and `public/team.js` | Already this text. The coding-session placeholder stays `Tell the agent what to work on`. |
| Waiting copy in the transcript | `Give the lead a task. Check files on the right when the team needs evidence.` | copy change | `public/app.js`: `Give the head agent a brief. Attach sources from the shared desktop when the team needs evidence.` | Team sessions only. Coding sessions stay `Start a turn in this workspace.` |
| `#sample-brief` | `Try a sample task` | copy change | `public/index.html`: `Use research brief` | Button label only. The inserted sentence stays the current sample. |
| Disclosure summary | `Model and limits` | copy change | `public/index.html`: `Model and budget` | Summary text only. |
| `#team-model` placeholder | `Default` | copy change | `public/index.html`: `Provider default` | Placeholder only. A filled model value still replaces it. |
| `#model` placeholder | `Default` | copy change | `public/index.html`: `Runtime default` | Placeholder only. `agent.connected` may still fill the field from the runtime. |
| `#call-limit` label | `Model calls` | copy change | `public/index.html`: `Model calls per run` | Label only. Default `6`, minimum `1`, maximum `20` stay. |
| `#token-limit` label | `Token limit` | copy change | `public/index.html`: `Token stop threshold` | Label only. Placeholder `Optional` stays. |
| `#token-limit` helper | `Stop after this many measured tokens. Leave blank to keep going.` | copy change | `public/index.html` has no helper on this field. | New helper text only. The between-calls stop in `src/teams.mjs` stays. |
| `h2` in `#team-inspector` | `Files` | copy change | `public/index.html`: `Shared desktop` | Heading only. The pane stays a file catalog inside `#team-inspector`, hidden on a coding session. |
| `#new-source` | `Add file` | copy change | `public/index.html`: `Add source` | Button label only. The dialog stays title, link, or pasted text. |
| `#editor-title` for a source | `Add a file` | copy change | `public/team.js`: `Add a shared source` | Source mode only. Note mode stays `Save a team note`. |
| `#source-address` label | `Link` | copy change | `public/index.html`: `Public source URL` | Label only. Placeholder `Website or GitHub repository` stays. |
| `#body-label` for a source | `Or paste text` | copy change | `public/index.html` and `public/team.js` | Already this text in source mode. Note mode stays `What should this team remember?` |
| Hint under Files | `Check files to include with the next task.` | copy change | `public/index.html`: `Select files to attach to the next message.` | Hint only. The six-file checkbox limit and the error `Attach up to six files at a time.` stay. |
| `h2` Team memory | `Notes` | copy change | `public/index.html`: `Team memory` | Heading only. |
| `#new-note` | `Add note` | copy change | `public/index.html`: `Add note` | Already this text. |
| Note button | `Forget` | copy change | `public/team.js`: `Forget` | Already this text. |
| `h2` Run activity | `Activity` | copy change | `public/index.html`: `Run activity` | Heading only. |
| `#usage` heading | Add the heading `Usage` above the details element. | copy change | `public/index.html` has `#usage` and no usage heading. | Put the heading immediately before `#usage`, outside that element. `public/team.js` replaces the children of `#usage`, and `public/app.js` sets its text. A heading inside `#usage` would be removed. |
| Recall line in `public/team.js` | `notes reused` or `notes loaded` | copy change | `public/team.js`: `actor · memory cache hit · count notes` or `actor · memory read · count notes` | Keep actor and count. Hit becomes `notes reused`. Miss becomes `notes loaded`. |
| Approval card title | `Approval needed` | copy change | `public/app.js`: `Approval needed` | Already this text while the choice is open. |
| `src/opencode.mjs` `optionKinds` | Also accept `allow_always`, and show the name OpenCode sends, `Always allow`, on the same card. | behavior change | `src/opencode.mjs`: `new Set(['allow_once', 'reject_once'])`. `public/app.js` already makes one button per option from `option.label`. | Same card. No new dialog. See section 4. |
| Team turns | Leave team turns without a tool-approval card. Do not invent an Allow button that approves nothing. | behavior change | `src/harness.mjs` runs `teams.run` and returns before the adapter permission hook. `src/teams.mjs` never emits `permission.requested`. | **Lock.** No new control. See section 5. |
| `#session-path` for a team | Hide the raw path on a team. Coding sessions keep the project path. | behavior change | `public/app.js` sets `#session-path` from `session.workspace` for every session. `src/teams.mjs` stores the catalog directory as that workspace. | Hide and clear the element on a team. Coding sessions still show `session.workspace`. The contract does not name the on-disk folder. |
| Team usage summary (§6) | Keep `calls/limit model calls · measured tokens`, and call the expanded field `cache write`. | reject | `public/team.js`: the summary matches the pattern; the expanded line says `write`, not `cache write`. | Leave this wording out. Section 7 records the actual line. |
| `(partial)` sentence (§6) | When `incomplete` is set, add “A model call did not report tokens, so the token limit stopped the run.” | reject | `src/teams.mjs` sets `incomplete` whenever a call omits a total. The next call is skipped for that reason only when a token limit is set. | `(partial)` is not itself proof that the limit stopped the run. Do not add the sentence. |
| Coding-session usage block (§6) | On ACP `usage_update` or prompt usage, write the team Usage block with used tokens, context size, and USD, and say `this session` unless a child total is present. | reject | `src/opencode.mjs` emits `model.usage` from prompt `result.usage` and has no `usage_update` branch. `public/app.js` already writes a different line. | The “no usage event” premise is false. Do not replace the existing line or promise fields the event does not carry. |
| Second cache for notes (§6) | Do not add a second cache concept for team notes. | behavior change | `public/team.js` recall row uses the word cache. `src/team-store.mjs` keeps notes for 60 seconds. Usage lines use cache for prompt tokens. | **Lock.** The recall wording change is the whole edit. No new cache control. |

## 4. Three adjudications

### Shared desktop becomes Files

Accept as a copy change. The inspector control is a file catalog: a checkbox list with a limit of six, **Open**, and a dialog for a title, a public link, or pasted text. Files the team writes appear in that list. It is not a live computer, a terminal, or an app preview. The product goal is a first screen a new person can understand, so the visible heading is **Files**.

The contract does not name the on-disk folder, quote a workspace path, or describe this pane as a computer. Hiding `#session-path` on a team is the behavior change that keeps that path off the team screen. Coding sessions still show the project path under the title. The session-list button’s title attribute is unchanged. `#team-inspector` stays hidden on a coding session, so Files is not added there.

The source dialog does not become a local file picker. **Add file** is the button and the source dialog title. **Link** is the URL label. **Or paste text** stays.

### OpenCode `allow_always` and Always allow

Accept as a behavior change. The current card can show an adapter label without a new dialog.

`public/app.js` `renderApproval` builds one card in `#approvals`: the title `Approval needed`, the request title, and one button per option. The button text is `option.label`. `src/opencode.mjs` sets that label from the ACP option name, truncated to 60 characters, or from the kind when the name is absent. The fixture name for `allow_always` is `Always allow`. Forwarding that option is enough for the pending card to show it. `allow_once` stays the primary button. Every other kind, including `allow_always` and `reject_once`, stays a quiet button.

The resolved-title map is only `allow_once` → `Allowed once`, `reject_once` → `Declined`, and `cancelled` → `Request closed`. The contract adds `allow_always` → `Allowed always` on that same card. Bloom forwards the selected option id. The contract does not add a rules screen or say that Bloom stores an allow rule.

The demo adapter’s buttons remain `Allow once` and `Reject`. Accepting the kind does not add `Always allow` to the demo.

### Usage on a direct coding session

The event missing today is the ACP session update `usage_update`. `projectUpdate` in `src/opencode.mjs` handles `agent_message_chunk`, `plan`, `tool_call`, and `tool_call_update`. Any other `sessionUpdate`, including `usage_update`, returns null and is not emitted. The contract must not promise `used`, `size`, `cost`, a context ring, a child-session total, or the words `this session`.

The event that exists is `model.usage`, emitted from `session/prompt` `result.usage` when that object is present. Its fields are `input`, `output`, `total`, `cacheRead`, and `cacheWrite`. Each is a non-negative safe integer or null. There is no USD field on this event.

The contract may promise this and only this for a coding session: `#usage` is cleared when the turn starts; when `model.usage` arrives, `#usage` shows `Tokens: {total or unreported} · Input: {input or unreported} · Output: {output or unreported} · Cache read: {cacheRead or unreported} · Cache write: {cacheWrite or unreported}`. When the prompt has no usage object, the region stays empty for that turn. The line stays under the new `Usage` heading. It does not become the team details block.

## 5. Team turns have no approval card

Confirmed. A team turn does not produce the approval card.

`src/harness.mjs` takes the team path when the session adapter is `team`, calls `teams.run`, and returns before `adapter.run`. The permission callback that emits `permission.requested` is passed only to `adapter.run`. `src/teams.mjs` does not call that callback and does not emit `permission.requested`. The card is rendered only for `permission.requested`.

The contract keeps that absence. It does not add an Allow button on a team turn. A button there would approve nothing in this checkout.

Team HTTP generations are a separate provider path. They are not this card. This contract does not add a team permission control.

## 6. Plain-language mapping

These are the controls that exist. The contract may say what they already do.

**Notes.** The section is the note list. **Add note** opens the dialog `Save a team note`. Each note has **Forget**. Saved notes are included as data on a specialist call. **Forget** removes that note, advances the team epoch, and stops an active turn. After the recall-line change, a hit reads `{actor} · notes reused · {count} notes` and a miss reads `{actor} · notes loaded · {count} notes`.

**Role.** This is the lead’s charter field, relabeled **Role**, with the placeholder `What should this lead be responsible for?` The roster shows that text under the lead. A specialist row shows that specialist’s charter under the name. The contract does not add a separate Role screen.

**Stage words.** The roster summary shows the stage. Display `head` as `Lead`, `research` as `Research`, `review` as `Review`, `assemble` as `Assemble`, `work` as `Work`, and `verify` as `Check`. Stored specialist stages stay the five ids. `verify` still writes a hash report and does not call a model. A review post still shows `Review approved` or `Changes requested`.

**The lead.** The lead is the name in **Lead name**, default `Lead`, and that name becomes the session title. **To** lists the lead first, and the lead is the default recipient. A message to the lead can plan one to five specialists. A message addressed with **To**, or with `@Name:`, runs that one member and does not plan a new roster.

The roster also shows one hint line that already exists: `VI · Team coordinator` for the lead, `LA · Deterministic verification` for `verify`, and `OAI · Model-backed specialist` for the other stages, plus the voice when a specialist has one. Those are labels on the same roster row. They are not screens.

Separate memory engines, intent engines, and persona engines are not present in this checkout. The contract must not describe them as screens. Notes, Role, and the roster are the whole of those ideas on this surface.

## 7. What the assembler copies, and what it leaves out

### Copy into the contract

Visible text:

- Kind labels: `Team` and `Coding session`. Values remain `team` and `direct`.
- Submit: `Create team` and `Create coding session`.
- Empty heading: `What should we work on?` Paragraph under it unchanged.
- `Lead name`, value `Lead`.
- `Role`, placeholder `What should this lead be responsible for?`
- Roster summaries: `name · Lead`, `name · Research`, `name · Review`, `name · Assemble`, `name · Work`, `name · Check`. Hint, charter, and voice lines unchanged.
- Team composer placeholder: `Give your team a task`.
- Team waiting copy: `Give the lead a task. Check files on the right when the team needs evidence.`
- Sample button: `Try a sample task`. The inserted sentence unchanged.
- `Model and limits`, both model placeholders `Default`, `Model calls`, `Token limit`.
- Helper: `Stop after this many measured tokens. Leave blank to keep going.`
- `Files`, `Add file`, source dialog title `Add a file`, `Link`, hint `Check files to include with the next task.`
- `Notes`, `Add note`, `Forget`, `Activity`, heading `Usage` immediately before `#usage`.
- Recall: `{actor} · notes reused · {count} notes` or `{actor} · notes loaded · {count} notes`.
- Pending card title `Approval needed`.

Behavior the contract specifies:

- `#empty-start` remains `Create a team` and opens the one form with kind `team`. A second button, `Create a coding session`, opens that form with kind `direct`.
- `optionKinds` includes `allow_always`. The existing card shows the adapter name on a quiet button. The resolved title for that kind is `Allowed always`.
- On a team, `#session-path` is hidden and empty. A coding session still shows the project path. The contract does not name the on-disk folder.

Locks the contract states:

- Team turns have no approval card and gain no Allow button.
- Notes do not gain another cache control. The word cache remains on the usage lines.

Usage text the contract records from the checkout, not from the rejected section 6 wording:

- Team summary: `{calls}/{limit} model calls · {measured total} measured tokens`, plus ` (partial)` when `incomplete` is true.
- Team line: `{actor} · {model or Default model} · input {n} · output {n} · cache read {n} · write {n} · USD {n or unreported}`.
- Coding-session line, only when `model.usage` arrives: `Tokens: {total or unreported} · Input: {input or unreported} · Output: {output or unreported} · Cache read: {cacheRead or unreported} · Cache write: {cacheWrite or unreported}`.

Mapping the contract may say: Notes, Forget, Role, the stage words, and the lead, as written in section 6. It may say the roster hint lines are labels on the member row.

Words and controls the contract keeps without rewriting: `Workspaces`, inspector heading `Team`, `To`, `Send`, `Stop`, `Model`, `Open`, `Allow once`, `Reject`, `Cancel`, `Save`, `Close`, `Download Markdown`, `Review approved`, `Changes requested`, `Blank starts in Scratch`, `Tell the agent what to work on`, `Start a turn in this workspace.`, and `Approval needed`.

### Leave out

- The section 6 request to name the team expanded field `cache write`. The word on that line is `write`.
- The sentence `A model call did not report tokens, so the token limit stopped the run.`
- A coding-session promise of ACP `usage_update`, `used`, `size`, USD, `this session`, or a child-session total.
- Replacing the coding-session usage line with the team details block.
- An Allow button, or any approval card, on a team turn.
- A second cache control for notes.
- A new approval dialog. `Always allow` is a button on the current card.
- A local file picker, a live computer, a terminal, or an app preview in the Files pane.
- The on-disk folder name and any absolute workspace path.
- A memory-engine screen, an intent-engine screen, or a persona-engine screen.
- Planner-prompt edits, README edits, server fallback renames, and test edits.
- Any string this review does not list. In particular, the empty-state paragraph, the note dialog, the source URL placeholder, and the six-file error stay.

# CAP-01: Development timeline and capability ledger

- ID: `CAP-01`
- Title: Development timeline and capability ledger
- Lead: `docs`
- Touches: `seed`, `capillary`, `myosotis`, `aestivation`, `drosera`, `trellis`, `bloom`
- Horizon: `now`
- Milestone: `M0`
- CLI phase: `none`
- Status: `in-progress`
- Claim: `planned`
- Depends on: `none`

## Why

The family spans eight public repositories (`docs`, `seed`, `capillary`, `myosotis`, `aestivation`, `drosera`, `trellis`, `bloom`), each with its own contracts, tests, and release cadence. Without a shared capability catalog and per-repository ledger convention, milestones, cross-repository dependencies, owner rulings, and implementation claims drift apart across checkouts.

## What it does

- Establishes the canonical hub timeline under `docs/timeline/`:
  - `docs/timeline/README.md`: usage guide, agent read order, and continual integration workflow.
  - `docs/timeline/roadmap.md`: milestones `M0` to `M9` across `Now`, `Next`, and `Later`, mapped onto Bloom CLI phases `P1` to `P6`.
  - `docs/timeline/capabilities.json`: machine-readable catalog of all 19 capabilities (`CAP-01` to `CAP-19`) with `id`, `title`, `lead`, `touches`, `horizon`, `milestone`, `cliPhase`, `dependsOn` (allowing `CAP-NN` and `CAP-NN.k`), and `spec`.
  - `docs/timeline/ledger.md`: human-readable capability status table (`# Capability ledger`, hand-maintained until `CAP-02` lands, generated afterward as a pure function of `capabilities.json` and lead entries).
  - `docs/timeline/decisions.md`: owner decision log format (`D-YYYYMMDD-NN`) and reference table of pending owner rulings (`D1` to `D14`).
  - `docs/timeline/agent-guide.md`: nine-step per-slice working loop, per-repository index rules (`milestone` on every slice, `lead` vs `touches` slice/spec scope, `prs` as `"<repo>#<n>"`, full 40-character squash SHAs in `commits`), status/claim fixed pairing rules, and hard governance constraints.
  - `docs/timeline/spec-template.md`: standardized 12-section capability specification layout.
- Establishes hub governance and terminology conventions:
  - `docs/proposals/`: proposal intake rules and template (`P-YYYYMMDD-<slug>.md`).
  - `docs/adr/`: cross-family ADR numbering (`NNNN-<slug>.md`) and owner ratification rule.
  - `docs/conventions/changelog.md`: standardized `docs/CHANGELOG.md` layout across all eight repositories (earlier-history pointer above `## Unreleased`, non-empty subsections only, `(CAP-NN, <repo>#<n>)` entry format).
  - `docs/glossary.md`: generalized family terminology linked to `seed`'s `docs/lexicon.md` plus definitions for 20 timeline and harness terms and closed role IDs (`chair`, `framing`, `risk`, `coherence`, `sequencing`).
- Establishes `docs/capabilities/` in every family repository (`README.md`, `index.json`, and lead capability specifications `CAP-NN-<slug>.md`), plus `docs/adr/README.md`, `docs/CHANGELOG.md`, and `AGENTS.md` read-order and same-PR ledger rule updates.

## Contract touchpoints

- `docs/sync.md`: `sources.json` already syncs `docs/` (`.md` and `.json`) from every peer repository into `sources/<repo>/docs/`, carrying per-repo `docs/capabilities/` and `docs/CHANGELOG.md` updates to the hub automatically after merge.
- `docs/engineering-law.md`: preserves zero runtime dependencies, strict claim honesty (`implemented`, `specified`, `planned`, `observed`), public safety, and zero em-dashes.

## Tool IDs and events

### Tool IDs

| Tool ID | Effect | Owner gate | Third-party egress | Summary |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| none | n/a | n/a | n/a | This capability defines no runtime tool IDs. |

### Events

| Event | Emitted by | Payload summary |
| --- | --- | --- |
| none | n/a | This capability emits no runtime events. |

## Acceptance tests

- `timeline-catalog-valid`: `docs/timeline/capabilities.json` parses cleanly, declares `version: 1`, holds 19 unique capabilities `CAP-01`..`CAP-19` with valid horizons (`now`, `next`, `later`), and forms an acyclic dependency graph where every dependency's milestone is less than or equal to the dependent's milestone.
- `cross-repo-ledger-consistent`: all eight `docs/capabilities/index.json` files parse cleanly, match `capabilities.json` lead/touches assignments 1-to-1, carry `milestone` on every slice, follow `lead` vs `touches` slice/spec rules, use valid status/claim pairs, and resolve every `spec` and `contracts[]` file on disk.
- `spec-template-conformance`: all 19 capability specs contain the exact 12 sections in order, separate `### Tool IDs` and `### Events` tables, and valid tool IDs under `seed` grammar and `drosera` face rules.
- `public-hygiene-clean`: zero YAML frontmatter, zero em-dashes, zero `@`-prefixed strings, zero private addresses/paths/credentials, and zero internal story or persona names appear in any committed timeline artifact.

## Slices

1. `CAP-01.1` (`docs`, `M0`, `in-progress`): Hub timeline scaffold (`docs/timeline/*`, `docs/proposals/*`, `docs/adr/*`, `docs/conventions/changelog.md`, `docs/glossary.md`, `docs/capabilities/*`, `docs/CHANGELOG.md`, `docs/index.md`, `AGENTS.md`).
2. `CAP-01.2` (`seed`, `M0`, `in-progress`): Seed capability docs and roadmap mapping (`CAP-03`, `CAP-06`, `CAP-12`, `CAP-13`, `CAP-16`, `CAP-17` specs, `index.json`, roadmap mapping, ADR pointer, changelog, `AGENTS.md`).
3. `CAP-01.3` (`capillary`, `M0`, `in-progress`): Capillary capability docs and packer spec (`CAP-05`, `CAP-18` specs, `index.json`, ADR pointer, changelog, `AGENTS.md`).
4. `CAP-01.4` (`myosotis`, `M0`, `in-progress`): Myosotis capability docs and memory integration spec (`CAP-11` spec, `index.json`, ADR pointer, changelog, `AGENTS.md`).
5. `CAP-01.5` (`aestivation`, `M0`, `in-progress`): Aestivation capability docs and plan loop spec (`CAP-07` spec, `index.json`, ADR pointer, changelog, `AGENTS.md`).
6. `CAP-01.6` (`drosera`, `M0`, `in-progress`): Drosera capability docs and run guard / scan specs (`CAP-09`, `CAP-19` specs, `index.json`, ADR pointer, changelog, `AGENTS.md`).
7. `CAP-01.7` (`trellis`, `M0`, `in-progress`): Trellis capability docs and ledger entries (`index.json`, ADR pointer, changelog, `AGENTS.md`).
8. `CAP-01.8` (`bloom`, `M0`, `in-progress`): Bloom capability docs and workspace/orchestration specs (`CAP-04`, `CAP-08`, `CAP-10`, `CAP-14`, `CAP-15` specs, `index.json`, ADR pointer, changelog, `AGENTS.md`).

## Non-goals

- Implementing `test/timeline.test.mjs`, `test/capabilities.test.mjs`, or automated `ledger.md` generation (deferred to `CAP-02`).
- Modifying any source code, runtime test suite, `package.json`, `sources/`, `manifest.json`, or existing `docs/contracts/` documents during Phase 0.
- Ratifying proposals, ADRs, or pending owner decisions (`D1` to `D14`).

## Family rules and conflicts

- Honors `docs` hub neutrality: the hub edits only its own pages and never patches peer repositories from `docs` automation (`sources/` remains a verbatim read-only mirror).
- Preserves existing contract invariants across peers (for example `seed`'s Stage 2 roadmap table row assertion and `bloom`'s separate open PR #1 branch ancestry).
- Avoids all internal story names and persona names in public hub pages and glossary definitions.

## Open owner decisions

- `D1` (unratified / pending owner ruling): Spec placement: plan of record in the hub; specs and progress in owner repos.
- `D2` (unratified / pending owner ruling): Two-field status (`status` lifecycle plus `claim` truth label) with fixed pairings.
- `D7` (unratified / pending owner ruling): Proposal intake via files under the hub's `docs/proposals/`; anything needing private detail goes directly to the owner, never to the hub.
- `D8` (unratified / pending owner ruling): Changelog location in `docs/CHANGELOG.md` per repository, so sync carries it without a `sources.json` change.
- `D13` (unratified / pending owner ruling): Accept the timeline structure, milestones `M0` to `M9`, and the capability catalog (review recommendation: accept the structure now, move `CAP-01` to `CAP-05` to `accepted` now, and leave `CAP-06` to `CAP-19` `proposed` until their milestone opens).
- `D14` (unratified / pending owner ruling): Review conventions made under delegation: changelog shape; slice milestones and slice IDs in `dependsOn`; `lead` lists all slices and `touches` list their own; `prs` as `"<repo>#<n>"` and full squash SHAs in `commits`; `CAP-06.1` at `M3` with `CAP-07.3` folded in; the `CAP-02` nine-slice split; reuse of `out-of-budget`.

## Evidence

None yet (`CAP-01.1` scaffold PR in progress across the eight repositories; `npm test` and Phase 0 cross-repo verification cover docs consistency and hygiene).

## Changes

- `2026-11-23`: Initial `CAP-01` specification drafted and Phase 0 scaffold prepared across `docs` and the seven peer repositories (`CAP-01.1`).
- `2026-11-23`: Review updates: align canonical `D1` to `D14` decision references, record full `CAP-01.1` to `CAP-01.8` slice entries with milestones and `prs: ["docs#1"]`, and document updated changelog, `spec`/`slices`, and `dependsOn` conventions (`CAP-01.1`).

# CAP-02: Docs freshness check

- ID: `CAP-02`
- Title: Docs freshness check
- Lead: `docs`
- Touches: `seed`, `capillary`, `myosotis`, `aestivation`, `drosera`, `trellis`, `bloom`
- Horizon: `now`
- Milestone: `M2`
- CLI phase: `none`
- Status: `proposed`
- Claim: `planned`
- Depends on: `CAP-01`

## Why

Hand-maintained ledgers and cross-repository capability specs inevitably drift as slice PRs land across eight repositories. Without automated freshness tests in both the hub (`docs`) and each standalone repository, broken spec paths, invalid status/claim pairs, cyclic or milestone-inverted dependencies, malformed tool IDs, or stale `ledger.md` tables can merge silently.

## What it does

Enforces four deterministic freshness rules offline, without network access:

1. **Hub cross-repo check (`CAP-02.1`, `test/timeline.test.mjs` in `docs`)**:
   - Reads the `docs` repository's `docs/timeline/capabilities.json`, `docs/timeline/ledger.md`, `docs/capabilities/index.json`, and lead specs alongside synced peer artifacts under `sources/<repo>/docs/capabilities/` (`index.json` and spec Markdown files).
   - Verifies JSON schema validity, exact 1-to-1 `lead` and symmetric `touches` alignment between `capabilities.json` and synced `index.json` files, slice `"milestone"` fields matching the capability's earliest slice milestone (`D14`), full slice coverage on `lead` entries vs per-repo slices on `touches` entries (`D14`), acyclic `dependsOn` graph resolving both `CAP-NN` and `CAP-NN.k` slice IDs against the `lead` entry with every dependency milestone less than or equal to the dependent's milestone (`D14`), valid two-field `status`/`claim` pairs (`D2`), and resolution of every `lead` repo-relative `spec`, `touches` `<repo>/<path>` `spec`, and `contracts[]` target (`D14`).
   - Compares deterministic `ledger.md` generation (from `capabilities.json` and `lead` entries, preserving `# Capability ledger` on line 1 and existing columns) byte-for-byte against committed `docs/timeline/ledger.md` and fails on drift.
   - Fails closed if a synced source carries an unknown status/claim pair, invalid spec heading sequence, or malformed tool ID.
2. **Standalone repository self-tests (`CAP-02.2` to `CAP-02.8`, `test/capabilities.test.mjs` in each peer repo)**:
   - Runs as part of `npm test` inside each repository (`seed`, `capillary`, `myosotis`, `aestivation`, `drosera`, `trellis`, `bloom`) without requiring any peer checkout on disk.
   - Verifies local files on disk: `docs/capabilities/index.json` schema and entry keys (including `"milestone"` on every slice), valid `status`/`claim` pairs, existence of every `lead` `spec` file and every listed `contracts[]` file inside the repository, existence and shape of `docs/CHANGELOG.md` (earlier-history line above `## Unreleased`, non-empty subsections only, `(CAP-NN, <repo>#<n>)` lines), `docs/adr/README.md`, and the 12-section order in local lead specs.
   - Checks only `lead` `spec` paths on disk; validates cross-repository `touches` `spec` paths syntactically (`<repo>/docs/capabilities/CAP-NN-<slug>.md` naming a known family repository) without reading outside the repository tree (`D14`).
3. **Sync-time `ledger.md` regeneration (`CAP-02.9`, `docs` sync + `docs/sync.md` + sync tests in one commit)**:
   - Extends `scripts/sync-sources.mjs` alongside `docs/sync.md` and sync tests in a single commit so sync runs regenerate `docs/timeline/ledger.md` deterministically (preserving `# Capability ledger` on line 1, `Hand-maintained until CAP-02 lands; generated afterward.`, and the pure function of `capabilities.json` + `lead` entries) whenever synced `sources/` updates.
4. **Grammar source (`D3`) and build order (`D14`)**:
   - Enforces `seed` tool-ID grammar (`domain . [resource . [sub .]] verb`, closed verb set, no forbidden vendor/infrastructure/persona segments) across all `toolIds[]` arrays and spec `### Tool IDs` tables.
   - Pending owner ruling `D3`, `CAP-02.1` sources the grammar from `seed` as a commit-pinned `devDependency` of `docs` (one grammar, zero runtime dependencies), while peer self-tests run standalone without peer checkouts.
   - Build order (`D14`): land `CAP-02.2` to `CAP-02.8` self-tests first, then `CAP-02.1` (`test/timeline.test.mjs` in `docs`), then `CAP-02.9` (sync regeneration with `docs/sync.md` and sync tests in one commit).

## Contract touchpoints

- `docs/sync.md`: synced `sources/<repo>/docs/capabilities/` files and `manifest.json` digests feed `test/timeline.test.mjs` (`CAP-02.1`), and `CAP-02.9` updates `docs/sync.md` alongside sync code and tests in one commit for `ledger.md` regeneration.
- `docs/engineering-law.md`: zero runtime dependencies, offline deterministic `npm test`, and fail-closed unknown handling.

## Tool IDs and events

### Tool IDs

| Tool ID | Effect | Owner gate | Third-party egress | Summary |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| none | n/a | n/a | n/a | This capability defines no runtime tool IDs. |

### Events

| Event | Emitted by | Payload summary |
| --- | --- | --- |
| none | n/a | This capability emits no runtime events. |

## Acceptance tests

- `hub-timeline-validates-repo-and-synced-sources` (`CAP-02.1`): `test/timeline.test.mjs` validates `capabilities.json`, `docs/capabilities/index.json`, and synced `sources/*/docs/capabilities/` records together, resolving `<repo>/<path>` on `touches` entries and `lead` repo-relative paths.
- `hub-ledger-drift-fails-closed` (`CAP-02.1`): modifying `capabilities.json` or synced `index.json` status without regenerating `docs/timeline/ledger.md` causes `test/timeline.test.mjs` to fail.
- `slice-depends-on-resolves-against-lead` (`CAP-02.1`): slice IDs in `dependsOn` (`CAP-NN.k`) resolve against the capability's `lead` entry and fail if missing, cyclic, or milestone-inverted.
- `repo-self-test-runs-without-siblings` (`CAP-02.2` to `CAP-02.8`): `test/capabilities.test.mjs` passes in every peer repository with zero peer directories mounted, checking only `lead` `spec` paths on disk and syntactic `<repo>/<path>` on `touches`.
- `invalid-status-claim-or-tool-id-rejected` (`CAP-02.1` to `CAP-02.8`): an unpermitted `status`/`claim` pair, cyclic `dependsOn`, missing `contracts[]` file, missing spec section, or invalid tool ID fails the test deterministically.
- `sync-regenerates-ledger-in-same-run` (`CAP-02.9`): sync updates `docs/timeline/ledger.md` deterministically alongside `manifest.json` and `docs/sources-index.md`, verified with `docs/sync.md` and sync tests in one commit.

## Slices

Build order: `CAP-02.2`..`CAP-02.8` -> `CAP-02.1` -> `CAP-02.9`.

1. `CAP-02.1` (`docs`, `M2`, `proposed`): Hub timeline test `test/timeline.test.mjs`.
2. `CAP-02.2` (`seed`, `M2`, `proposed`): Self-test `test/capabilities.test.mjs` in `seed`.
3. `CAP-02.3` (`capillary`, `M2`, `proposed`): Self-test `test/capabilities.test.mjs` in `capillary`.
4. `CAP-02.4` (`myosotis`, `M2`, `proposed`): Self-test `test/capabilities.test.mjs` in `myosotis`.
5. `CAP-02.5` (`aestivation`, `M2`, `proposed`): Self-test `test/capabilities.test.mjs` in `aestivation`.
6. `CAP-02.6` (`drosera`, `M2`, `proposed`): Self-test `test/capabilities.test.mjs` in `drosera`.
7. `CAP-02.7` (`trellis`, `M2`, `proposed`): Self-test `test/capabilities.test.mjs` in `trellis`.
8. `CAP-02.8` (`bloom`, `M2`, `proposed`): Self-test `test/capabilities.test.mjs` in `bloom`.
9. `CAP-02.9` (`docs`, `M2`, `proposed`): Sync regenerates `docs/timeline/ledger.md` with `docs/sync.md` and sync tests in the same commit.

## Non-goals

- Reading peer repositories directly from disk during `npm test` (cross-repo checks run in `docs` against `sources/`, while each peer runs standalone).
- Auto-committing changes across peer repositories or bypassing PR review.
- Adding runtime dependencies to any repository (`CAP-02.1` grammar sourcing via `devDependency` is governed by `D3`).

## Family rules and conflicts

- Must respect zero runtime dependencies (`docs/engineering-law.md`) and standalone repository CI isolation (`test/capabilities.test.mjs` never reaches `../seed` or other peers on disk).
- Must keep `docs/sources/` strictly read-only during tests and ledger generation, and change sync code, `docs/sync.md`, and sync tests together in `CAP-02.9`.

## Open owner decisions

- `D2` (unratified / pending owner ruling): Two-field status (`status` lifecycle plus `claim` truth label) with fixed pairings enforced by `CAP-02`.
- `D3` (unratified / pending owner ruling): Grammar source for the hub's `CAP-02.1` test (review recommendation: `seed` as a commit-pinned `devDependency` of `docs`, keeping one grammar and zero runtime dependencies).
- `D14` (unratified / pending owner ruling): Review conventions made under delegation: `CAP-02` nine-slice split (`CAP-02.1` hub test only, `CAP-02.2` to `CAP-02.8` self-tests, `CAP-02.9` sync ledger regeneration, build order `CAP-02.2`..`CAP-02.8` -> `CAP-02.1` -> `CAP-02.9`), slice milestones, slice IDs in `dependsOn`, and `lead` vs `touches` slice and spec rules.

## Evidence

None yet (`proposed`, `planned`).

## Changes

- `2026-11-23`: Initial `CAP-02` specification drafted (`CAP-01.1`).
- `2026-11-23`: Review updates: split `CAP-02.1` and `CAP-02.9` with build order, apply slice milestone, slice dependency, and `lead` vs `touches` spec resolution rules, and align `D2`, `D3`, and `D14` (`CAP-01.1`).

docsPages.body: Context with its sources attached # Capillary Capillary is an open, local-first **context retrieval system** for agent workspaces. It records sources with their digests, retrieves **bounded, provenance-honest packets** of them, and keeps **typed relations** between the items it holds: the fine-channel work of lifting context up to the team that needs it, without letting prose smuggle in as fact. Agent surfaces like [Bloom](https://github.com/Vidoxlabs/bloom) consume capillary exactly where retrieving (and organizing) their source and context matters: a team brief admits sources, and specialists receive bounded excerpts that say what they are, where they came from, and what was shortened. Harness foundations like [Seed](https://github.com/Vidoxlabs/seed) admit capillary's retrieval tools to their runs and record each retrieval as an intent. **Status: `1.3.0`, retrieval contracts and library modules.** The retrieval seam, source recording, and relation contracts are implemented and covered by `npm test`. The backing stores (index, service) are specified, not shipped. Nothing in this repository opens a network listener or retrieves over the network today. ## What is here today (`implemented`) | Module | What it does | | --- | --- | | `src/provenance.mjs` | Records source digests, origins, evidence classes and confidence, and records why sources are unknown | | `src/packet.mjs` | Builds bounded context packets with **declared** truncation, budgeted admission, declared unknown sources, and relevance and recency kept as separate fields | | `src/epoch-guard.mjs` | Refuses a packet when the deletion epoch at the end of a read differs from the epoch at its start, or cannot be read | | `src/read.mjs` | Reads caller-supplied text under an estimated token budget and declares truncation in an untrusted envelope | | `src/search.mjs` | Searches caller-supplied records for literal matches and reports recency and snippet cuts in an untrusted envelope | | `src/conversation.mjs` | Shapes one conversation's thread, a recent list, a brief of the newest operator intent and verified outcome, and an envelope around the parent walk, all from caller-supplied records | | `src/relations.mjs` | Typed, append-only relations and bounded walks over supplied parent links | `npm install && npm test` verifies all of it. No runtime dependencies. ## Contracts - [Bounded retrieval](docs/contracts/retrieval.md): the packet, its budgets, declared shortening, declared omissions - [Provenance](docs/contracts/retrieval.md): digests and origin classes on every source ## How capillary fits the systems (`specified`) The botanic line, per [docs/systems.md](docs/systems.md): **seed** (the foundation a runtime grows from) → **capillary** (these channels, lifting context to it) → **myosotis** (governed memory: consent, keep, and forget) → **aestivation** (the bud's arrangement, admission and review before assembly) → **drosera** (the sundew's tentacles: tools, skills, hooks, cookbooks) → **bloom** (the opened team workspace), with the whole line growing against **trellis** (the testing lattice that keeps every member honest). Capillary owns retrieval and organization only. Remembering with consent is the memory fabric's job (forget is a promise there, not a default); deciding what gets admitted into runs and what assembles is the gate's job. [docs/interop.md](docs/interop.md) draws each seam. ## Documentation - [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md): start here before editing. Stay in this repository's province. - [Charter](docs/charter.md): mission, principles, non-goals - [Architecture](docs/architecture.md): sources, index, packets, relations - [Contracts](docs/contracts/retrieval.md): bounded retrieval and provenance - [Relations contract](docs/contracts/relations.md): typed, append-only context relations - [Interop](docs/interop.md): Bloom, Seed, and the memory seam - [Systems](docs/systems.md): the botanic naming line ## License [MIT](LICENSE) The Vidoxlabs name and mark are trademarks of Vidoxlabs LLC. They are not covered by this repository's MIT license.

# Capillary architecture

Status: `specified`; modules named below exist (`implemented`) where marked.

## The four parts

1. **Sources** (`implemented as records` in `src/provenance.mjs`) — the corpus is an
   append-only set of recorded sources: an id, a title, a 64-hex digest, an origin class
   (`url`, `repository`, `text`, `workspace-file`, `run-artifact`), and an origin
   reference, plus the claim's evidence class and confidence. A source whose digest
   is unavailable is recorded as unknown with a null digest and its reason
   (`not-found`, `read-failed`, `digest-unavailable`). The packet lists it under `unknown`.
2. **The index** (`specified`) — lexical and semantic recall over recorded sources. The
   index is a projection: it is rebuilt from sources, never an authority. A search that
   misses is reported as a miss with its coverage stated; it is never padded.
3. **The packet builder** (`implemented` in `src/packet.mjs`) — retrieval's output
   artifact: a bounded set of excerpt items, each carrying its source id and digest, a
   `shortened` flag with the carried and cut sizes, and a declared budget accounting.
   Admission is ordered and deterministic; what does not fit is listed as omitted, never
   dropped silently.
4. **The relation ledger** (`implemented as records` in `src/relations.mjs`) — typed,
   append-only records linking known sources: the organization half of context work.
   `derived-from`, `references`, `subsumes`, `revised-from`, `relates-to`. The ledger is
   an event history: appended to, never rewritten. `walkParentChain` follows explicit
   parent ids in a caller-supplied map with a declared stopping reason.

## The retrieval seam

```
sources -> index (projection) -> ranked candidate items
        -> packet builder (budgets, truncation, admission)
        -> packet -> the requesting run or workspace
```

Every crossing is stateable to a reviewer:

- *Which sources* were considered and read (ids, digests).
- *Which excerpts* were admitted, in what sizes, with what cut.
- *Which items* the budgets left out.
- *Why* — the budgets and the order are part of the packet.

## Neurology of the systems

Capillary decides nothing. It serves retrieval to the layers that decide:

- Runs (a seed objective) admit retrieval tools and record each call as an intent.
- Teams (a bloom turn) attach sources to a task and receive the bounded packets.
- The memory fabric (the myosotis-to-be) is a different organ: it remembers with
  consent and forgets on demand; capillary never copies its role.
- The admission and review loop (the aestivation-to-be) gates assembly; capillary
  hands it exact evidence, never verdicts.

While the public counterparts of those systems are in the works, capillary's contracts
stand alone: `myosotis`, `aestivation`, and capillary are peers with separate
provinces, and the seams are contracts, not assumptions.

## What capillary refuses to own

- No verdicts. Retrieval reports; admission decides.
- No remembrance. Provenance and relations, never consent or recall policy.
- No quiet defaults. Budgets, truncation, and misses are declared on the packet.
- No living index. Every projection is rebuildable from sources.

# CAP-05: Codebase-to-context packer

- ID: `CAP-05`
- Title: Codebase-to-context packer
- Lead: `capillary`
- Touches: `drosera`, `bloom`, `trellis`
- Horizon: Now (library slices), Next (composer slices)
- Milestone: M2 (library slices), M3 (composer slices)
- CLI phase: `P3`
- Status: `proposed`
- Claim: `planned`
- Depends on: `CAP-03`, `CAP-04`

## Why

Agent coding runs and workspace briefs need a single, reproducible view of a codebase that fits inside context budgets without leaking secrets, truncating silently, or misreporting missing repository state as empty.
By separating pure selection, ordering, budgeting, and rendering inside `capillary` from filesystem traversal and read-only `git` execution in `bloom`, every packed codebase context remains deterministic, inspectable by digest, and safe against untrusted file content.

## What it does

1. **Pure selection over caller-supplied path lists**:
   - Accepts caller-supplied relative path lists, file metadata, ignore-file rules, overrides, and file byte buffers without performing disk or network I/O inside `capillary`.
   - Applies include and exclude globs supporting `*`, `**`, `?`, character classes (such as `[a-z]` and `[!0-9]`), and brace lists (such as `{mjs,json}`). Exclude always wins over include, and an empty include list means include all non-excluded paths.
   - Evaluates ignore-file rules scoped per directory with `#` comments, `!` negation (restoring a previously ignored file), trailing `/` for directory-only matches, and leading `/` anchored to the ignore file's directory; ignore evaluation is switchable on or off by the caller.
   - Excludes hidden paths (segments starting with `.`) by default, switchable by the caller.
   - Enforces an always-on secret-file deny list covering environment files (`.env` and variants), private keys and certificates, credential stores, key files, and token caches. Explicit include rules or path overrides for a denied path are refused unless an explicit per-call `CAP-06.1` owner approval permits that path (pending owner decision `D10`), and the refusal is recorded as omission reason `denied`.
   - Supports manual per-path force-include and force-exclude overrides within the deny-list rule above.
   - Performs binary sniffing over caller-supplied bytes (detecting NUL bytes or non-text byte patterns) and omits binary files with omission reason `binary`.
2. **Deterministic ordering**:
   - Sorts selected paths by relative path Unicode code-point order by default.
   - Supports optional ordering by modification time (`mtime`, newest first or oldest first) with relative path Unicode code-point order as a deterministic tiebreak.
   - Produces byte-identical rendered output and packet structures for identical inputs.
3. **Directory tree**:
   - Renders a deterministic directory tree covering either the selected paths only or the full considered path list, using normalized relative paths only.
4. **Optional change context**:
   - Accepts working-tree diffs, ref-to-ref diffs, and ref-to-ref commit logs as caller-supplied text records carrying provenance (`origin: 'repository'`, `evidenceClass: 'tool-observation'`).
   - In `bloom`, optional change context is collected via read-only system `git` (pending owner decision `D9`); when `git` is absent, fails, or returns an unreadable state, the change context is recorded as `unknown` with its reason and is never emitted as an empty diff.
5. **Format-aware readers**:
   - Reads content through format-aware readers: plain text, tabular files (header row plus first N data rows), JSON lines (first N records), and notebooks (extracted cell sources without binary attachment payloads).
   - Declares every shortening performed by a format-aware reader with carried and cut measures.
6. **Token budget and token map**:
   - Applies a caller-specified token budget using a character-based estimate explicitly labeled `estimate` (pending owner decision `D5`).
   - Fills admitted files strictly in deterministic order and omits remaining candidates with omission reason `out-of-budget` once the budget is exhausted (reusing existing `out-of-budget` from `OMISSION_REASONS`, pending owner decision `D14`).
   - Returns a per-file token map sorted by estimated tokens descending (largest first, deterministic path tiebreak) and per-extension token totals.
7. **Render formats, custom templates, and safety framing**:
   - Renders packed context in `markdown`, `tagged`, and `json` formats, with optional line numbers.
   - Renders relative paths only; absolute paths or parent-traversal paths are rejected or normalized safely and never appear in rendered output.
   - Sizes Markdown code fences to be strictly longer than any fence run present inside the embedded file text so file contents cannot break out of a code block.
   - Supports a placeholder-only custom template using `{{tree}}`, `{{files}}`, `{{diff}}`, `{{log}}`, `{{budget}}`, and `{{omissions}}`, with zero template conditionals, loops, or evaluation logic (pending owner decision `D6`).
   - Wraps file contents and repository diffs in an explicit untrusted-content envelope (`untrusted: true` and boundary framing) so downstream callers treat repository text as data, never instructions.
8. **Packet honesty**:
   - Declares every excerpt truncation (`shortened`, carried, cut) and every format-aware shortening.
   - Records every omitted path in deterministic order with one closed omission reason: `excluded`, `ignored`, `hidden`, `denied`, `binary`, or `out-of-budget` (plus `unknown-source` when underlying source verification fails; `D14`).
   - Lists every failed, missing, unreadable, unfollowed-symlink, or absent-`git` entry under `unknown` with its reason (`not-found`, `read-failed`, `digest-unavailable`).
   - Records 64-hex SHA-256 content digests for every admitted file and for the final rendered packet output.
9. **Drosera tool faces**:
   - Defines five `read`-effect tool faces in `drosera`: `workspace.tree.list`, `context.repo.pack.read`, `context.budget.verify`, `vcs.repo.diff.read`, and `vcs.repo.log.read`, with `CAP-03` input and output schemas.
10. **Drosera skill and recipe**:
    - Ships a map-first exploration skill in `drosera` (inspect tree and token budget map before requesting full file contents) and a cookbook recipe tying the packer faces together. Skills stay instructional and grant no permissions.
11. **Bloom executor and CLI**:
    - Walks the workspace root in `bloom` without following symlinks by default (`D10`), reads raw bytes and computes SHA-256 digests, gathers optional read-only `git` diffs and logs (`D9`), and invokes `capillary`'s packer.
    - Emits the `context.packet` trace event carrying counts, omission/unknown tallies, budget totals, and SHA-256 digests, never raw file contents or diffs.
    - Integrates packing into the coding loop context step and exposes `bloom pack` on the CLI.
12. **Trellis behavior probe**:
    - `trellis` runs behavior and determinism probes against `capillary`'s packer library covering selection precedence, secret denial, budget honesty, and byte-identical rendering without patching `capillary`.

## Contract touchpoints

- `docs/contracts/retrieval.md`: Extends `capillary`'s bounded retrieval contract additively. Admitted codebase files and diffs map to `recordSource` (`origin: 'workspace-file'` or `'repository'`, `evidenceClass: 'tool-observation'`, `confidence: 'direct-tool'`), failed reads and absent `git` output map to `recordUnknownSource` (`unknown` list), and file payloads inherit the `untrusted: true` envelope rule. Token budgeting (`estimate`) and additive packer omission reasons (`excluded`, `ignored`, `hidden`, `denied`, `binary`) are documented alongside existing `BLOOM_BASELINE` character limits and `OMISSION_REASONS` (`out-of-budget`, `unknown-source`), reusing `out-of-budget` when budget is exhausted without breaking `1.3.0` packet callers.
- `docs/contracts/relations.md`: Packed outputs and derived summaries can link back to admitted source file digests through `derived-from` relation records audited by `isSoundLedger`.

## Tool IDs and events

### Tool IDs

| Tool ID | Effect | Owner gate | Purpose |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `workspace.tree.list` | `read` | `false` | Return deterministic directory tree for selected or full workspace paths |
| `context.repo.pack.read` | `read` | `false` | Build bounded codebase context packet and rendered output under token budget |
| `context.budget.verify` | `read` | `false` | Compute per-file largest-first token map and per-extension totals without packing bodies |
| `vcs.repo.diff.read` | `read` | `false` | Read working-tree or ref-to-ref diff as provenance-tagged observation or unknown |
| `vcs.repo.log.read` | `read` | `false` | Read ref-to-ref commit log as provenance-tagged observation or unknown |

### Events

| Event | Emitted by | Payload summary |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `context.packet` | `bloom` | Packet counts, omission and unknown tallies by reason, estimated token budget summary, source SHA-256 digests, and rendered output SHA-256 digest (never raw file or diff contents) |

## Acceptance tests

- `exclude-wins-over-include`: When a path matches both include and exclude globs, exclude wins; when include is empty, all non-excluded paths remain eligible.
- `ignore-negation-restores-file`: Ignore-file comments, trailing directory slashes, anchored leading slashes, per-directory scoping, and `!` negation rules evaluate deterministically and restore negated paths when enabled.
- `hidden-off-by-default`: Dot-prefixed files and directories are omitted with reason `hidden` unless hidden inclusion is explicitly enabled.
- `secret-file-denied-even-when-included`: Environment files, private key/certificate files, credential stores, key files, and token caches are refused even under explicit include or manual override unless a per-call `CAP-06.1` owner approval permits them, and are recorded as omitted with `denied`.
- `binary-omitted-with-reason`: Binary byte sequences are detected by sniff and omitted with reason `binary` without entering rendered text.
- `byte-identical-output-for-identical-input`: Repeated runs with identical inputs and options produce byte-identical rendered strings and identical output SHA-256 digests across `markdown`, `tagged`, and `json`.
- `budget-omits-with-reason`: Candidates exceeding the estimated token budget are omitted with reason `out-of-budget` in deterministic order, with total estimated tokens labeled `estimate`.
- `token-map-largest-first`: The returned token map lists admitted files sorted largest estimated tokens first with deterministic path tiebreaks alongside per-extension totals.
- `diff-unknown-when-git-absent`: When `git` is absent or returns an error during change-context collection, the diff or log is recorded under `unknown` and never emitted as an empty diff.
- `absolute-paths-never-rendered`: Rendered output and trees contain relative paths only; absolute paths or parent-traversal inputs are rejected or normalized before rendering.
- `fence-longer-than-inner-fence`: Markdown rendering emits code fences strictly longer than the longest backtick or tilde run in any admitted file's text.
- `custom-template-has-no-logic`: Custom templates expand only `{{tree}}`, `{{files}}`, `{{diff}}`, `{{log}}`, `{{budget}}`, and `{{omissions}}`, treating control syntax literally or rejecting non-placeholder expressions without executing logic.
- `untrusted-envelope-wraps-file-text`: File contents and repository diffs appear inside an explicit untrusted-content boundary (`untrusted: true`) separate from caller prompt text.
- `packet-event-carries-digests-not-content`: `bloom`'s emitted `context.packet` trace event contains counts, budget summaries, and SHA-256 digests with zero file text or diff lines.

## Slices

- `CAP-05.1` (`capillary`, `M2`, `proposed`): Selection engine: globs, ignore rules, deny list, overrides, binary sniff.
- `CAP-05.2` (`capillary`, `M2`, `proposed`): Ordering, tree render, format-aware readers, budget, and token map.
- `CAP-05.3` (`capillary`, `M2`, `proposed`): Render formats, placeholder template, untrusted envelope, and packet output.
- `CAP-05.4` (`drosera`, `M2`, `proposed`): Packer tool faces, map-first exploration skill, and recipe.
- `CAP-05.5` (`bloom`, `M3`, `proposed`): Workspace file walker, read-only git context executor, and bloom pack CLI.
- `CAP-05.6` (`bloom`, `M3`, `proposed`): Coding loop context-step integration and context.packet event.
- `CAP-05.7` (`trellis`, `M3`, `proposed`): Packer behavior and determinism probes.

## Non-goals

- Walking the host filesystem, following symlinks, or spawning `git` inside `capillary` (`capillary` stays pure over caller-supplied inputs).
- Vector embeddings, semantic ranking, or network retrieval.
- Exact model-family tokenization requiring runtime dependencies (`capillary` keeps zero runtime dependencies).
- Template scripting languages, conditionals, loops, or helper function execution in custom templates.
- Writing files or altering repository state during pack operations.

## Family rules and conflicts

- **Pure library boundary**: `capillary` never imports `drosera`, `myosotis`, `aestivation`, or `bloom`, and performs no disk or subprocess I/O. Filesystem walking and read-only `git` invocation live in `bloom`; tool faces, skills, and recipes live in `drosera`; schema grammar lives in `seed`; behavioral probes live in `trellis`.
- **Zero runtime dependencies**: Globs, ignore matching, binary sniffing, format-aware parsing, token estimation, and template substitution are implemented with Node built-ins only.
- **Unknowns fail closed**: Unreadable files, unfollowed symlinks, and missing `git` stay `unknown` rather than empty results.
- **Public safety**: Secret deny lists block credential artifacts by default; trace events carry digests and counts only; rendered paths never expose host root paths.
- **Contract harmony**: Existing `src/packet.mjs` defines `OMISSION_REASONS = ['out-of-budget', 'unknown-source']` and `BLOOM_BASELINE` character limits (`28000` / `12000`). Packer extensions must remain additive so `1.3.0` retrieval contract callers remain unchanged.

## Open owner decisions

- **D5 (pending owner decision)**: Confirm the character-based token estimation rule and `estimate` label convention across packed packets and `context.budget.verify` (exact token counts only from the configured provider at run time, never in tests; e.g., 4 Unicode code points per estimated token matching `readSource`).
- **D6 (pending owner decision)**: Confirm the template model: built-in `markdown`, `tagged`, and `json` formats plus a placeholder-only custom template restricted exclusively to the six placeholder tokens (`{{tree}}`, `{{files}}`, `{{diff}}`, `{{log}}`, `{{budget}}`, `{{omissions}}`) with no template logic or conditionals.
- **D9 (pending owner decision)**: Confirm that `bloom` calls the system `git` binary read-only for working-tree/ref diffs and commit logs (`CAP-05.5`), recording absent or failing `git` as `unknown` and never as an empty diff.
- **D10 (pending owner decision)**: Confirm that the secret-file deny list stays always on, explicit includes of denied paths require a per-call `CAP-06.1` owner approval record, and symlink following stays disabled by default in `bloom`'s walker.
- **D14 (pending owner decision)**: Confirm review conventions made under delegation for `CAP-05`: reusing existing `out-of-budget` from `OMISSION_REASONS` alongside additive packer omission reasons (`excluded`, `ignored`, `hidden`, `denied`, `binary`) and `BLOOM_BASELINE` character caps, plus `M2` (`CAP-05.1` to `CAP-05.4`) and `M3` (`CAP-05.5` to `CAP-05.7`) slice milestones.

## Evidence

- `test/codebase-context.test.mjs` exercises scoped selection, denied inputs, format-aware excerpts, deterministic budgets, and untrusted renderers over caller-supplied bytes.

None yet (`status: proposed`, `claim: planned`). Test outputs, probe receipts, and commit SHAs will be recorded here as slices `CAP-05.1` through `CAP-05.7` land.

## Changes

- 2026-11-24. Add pure codebase selection, context budgeting, and packet rendering (CAP-05, capillary#3).

- `2026-11-23`: Initial capability specification drafted for `CAP-01` timeline scaffold.
- `2026-11-23`: Reused `out-of-budget` from `OMISSION_REASONS`, aligned canonical `D5`/`D6`/`D9`/`D10`/`D14` decision references and `CAP-06.1` override reference, and added `M2`/`M3` slice milestones (`CAP-01`, review fixes).

# CAP-18: Symbol outline for packed context

- ID: `CAP-18`
- Title: Symbol outline for packed context
- Lead: `capillary`
- Touches: `drosera`, `bloom`
- Horizon: later
- Milestone: M8
- CLI phase: none
- Status: `proposed`
- Claim: `planned`
- Depends on: `CAP-05`

## Why

When exploring a large workspace under tight token budgets, reading whole files wastes packet capacity on implementation details when callers only need structural navigation: exported bindings, functions, classes, document headings, or JSON object keys with line ranges.
Adding a zero-dependency symbol outline extractor inside `capillary` keeps packed context compact while obeying retrieval honesty: any file format outside the supported parser set stays explicitly `unknown` instead of emitting an empty symbol list.

## What it does

- **Zero-dependency parsers in `capillary`**: Extracts structural outlines from caller-supplied relative path, format hint, and UTF-8 source text without external parser dependencies:
  - **JavaScript** (`.js`, `.mjs`, `.cjs`): extracts `exports` (named, default, re-exports), `functions` (declarations and top-level function bindings), and `classes`, each with symbol name, kind, and 1-based `{ startLine, endLine }` range.
  - **Markdown** (`.md`): extracts headings with level (`1` to `6`), heading text, and 1-based line range.
  - **JSON** (`.json`): validates structure and extracts top-level (and optionally depth-bounded) keys with 1-based line ranges; malformed JSON reports `unknown` (`read-failed` or `parse-failed`), never an empty key list.
- **Packet outline section**: Attaches extracted outlines as a structured section inside `CAP-05` packed context outputs (`markdown`, `tagged`, and `json` renderers), keeping relative paths only, source SHA-256 digests, and the untrusted-content boundary around extracted names and headings.
- **Explicit `unknown` fallback**: For any file language or format outside JavaScript, Markdown, and JSON (or for binary/unparseable content), returns `status: 'unknown'` with an explicit reason instead of an empty outline array.
- **Drosera tool face**: Defines `workspace.file.outline.read` (`effect: 'read'`, `ownerGate: false`) in `drosera` with `CAP-03` input and output schemas.
- **Bloom executor**: Reads workspace file bytes inside the workspace root (no symlink follow by default) and passes content to `capillary`'s outline extractor for direct tool calls and outline-mode context packing.

## Contract touchpoints

- `docs/contracts/retrieval.md`: Extends `CAP-05` packet output additively with an optional `outlines` section carrying relative `originRef`, 64-hex SHA-256 source digest, `untrusted: true` framing, and explicit `unknown` records whenever a file cannot be parsed or its language is unsupported.

## Tool IDs and events

### Tool IDs

| Tool ID | Effect | Owner gate | Purpose |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `workspace.file.outline.read` | `read` | `false` | Extract JS exports, functions, and classes, Markdown headings, or JSON keys with line ranges, or return unknown |

### Events

| Event | Emitted by | Payload summary |
| --- | --- | --- |
| (none added) | `bloom` | Reuses `CAP-05` `context.packet` event digests and counts when outlines are included in a pack |

## Acceptance tests

- `js-outline-extracts-exports-functions-classes-with-line-ranges`: Extracts exports, functions, and classes with accurate 1-based line ranges from JavaScript text with zero runtime dependencies.
- `markdown-outline-extracts-headings-with-levels-and-lines`: Extracts Markdown headings with heading levels and 1-based line numbers.
- `json-outline-extracts-keys-with-line-ranges`: Extracts JSON keys with line ranges and reports `unknown` when JSON input is malformed.
- `unsupported-language-reports-unknown-never-empty`: Any non-JS, non-Markdown, non-JSON format or binary payload reports `status: 'unknown'` with reason and never returns an empty symbol outline as success.
- `outline-section-uses-relative-paths-and-untrusted-envelope`: Packed outline sections emit relative paths only, record source digests, and sit inside the untrusted-content envelope.
- `workspace-file-outline-read-validates-and-executes`: `workspace.file.outline.read` validates under `seed` grammar, registers in `drosera`, and executes inside `bloom`'s workspace root guard.

## Slices

- `CAP-18.1` (`capillary`, `M8`, `proposed`): Zero-dependency JS, Markdown, and JSON symbol outline parser and unknown fallback.
- `CAP-18.2` (`drosera`, `M8`, `proposed`): Outline reader tool face definition and schema.
- `CAP-18.3` (`bloom`, `M8`, `proposed`): Symbol outline executor and packer wiring.

## Non-goals

- Runtime dependencies on AST or tree-sitter parser packages.
- Supporting languages beyond JavaScript, Markdown, and JSON in this capability (unsupported formats stay `unknown`).
- Cross-file type resolution, semantic symbol linking, or code indexing.
- Filesystem traversal inside `capillary`.

## Family rules and conflicts

- **Zero runtime dependencies**: Outlines are parsed solely with zero-dependency JavaScript in `capillary`.
- **Unknown stays unknown**: Unsupported file extensions and malformed files never masquerade as empty outlines.
- **Province separation**: `capillary` performs pure parsing and packet assembly; `drosera` owns the `workspace.file.outline.read` face; `bloom` performs workspace reads and invokes the packer; `seed` validates the tool ID and `CAP-03` schemas.

## Open owner decisions

None new for `CAP-18`; inherits `CAP-05` packer decisions (`D5`, `D6`, `D9`, `D10`, `D14`) and `CAP-03` schema parity (`D4`).

## Evidence

None yet (`status: proposed`, `claim: planned`). Code, test receipts, and commit SHAs will be recorded here as slices `CAP-18.1` through `CAP-18.3` land.

## Changes

- `2026-11-23`: Initial capability specification drafted for `CAP-01` timeline scaffold.
- `2026-11-23`: Standardized `Horizon: later`, added `M8` slice milestones, and aligned inherited `CAP-05` decision references (`CAP-01`, review fixes).

# Capillary charter

## Mission

Give agent workspaces retrieval they can quote: sources recorded with their digests,
excerpts bounded by stated budgets, and relations between context items that stay typed
and inspectable — so a conversation, a run, or a reviewer can always ask *where did this
context come from, what was it, and what was cut*.

Capillary is the context-retrieval member of the botanic family: the fine-channel system
that lifts context to the workspace that needs it. Where bloom is the opened team
workspace and seed is the growth layer beneath it, capillary decides nothing — it
retrieves, bounds, and organizes.

## Principles

1. **Provenance or it is not context.** Every item capillary admits to a packet carries a
   source reference and a digest. Untethered prose does not enter.
2. **Declared truncation.** A shortened excerpt is marked shortened, with the size
   carried and the size cut. A omitted-for-budget item is recorded as omitted, not
   silently dropped.
3. **Bounded recall.** Every packet carries its budgets. What arrives matches them or
   the packet says why not.
4. **Unknown stays unknown.** A source that could not be read or verified stays unknown;
   it is never reported as "no results" and never substituted with plausible content.
5. **Retrieval is not remembering.** Capillary holds sources and relations, not consent.
   Remembering with consent and forget belongs to the memory fabric. Retrieving into a
   run is an admitted, recorded intent — never an ambient memory grab.
6. **Relations are typed and append-only.** Context organization is an event history:
   records are added, never rewritten in place.

## Non-goals

- Not a chat log, not a transcript store, not a memory of conversations.
- Not a black-box similarity dump: relevance signals are stated, not implied.
- Not a network crawler: anything that reaches outside the local process ships as an
  adapter behind a contract, never an assumption.
- No silent coupling to any single store format. The contracts are the interface.

## Standing constraint

The first consumers already proved the operating shape: a team's evidence budget lands
whole, bounded excerpts per file with an honest "shortened" marker on the ones that were
cut. Those numbers (28,000 characters across a packet, 12,000 per item) are capillary's
family baseline defaults; a caller's budgets, where stated, always win.

# Contract: context relations

Status: `specified`; record validation, ledger soundness and parent walking are `implemented` in
`src/relations.mjs`.

## Why relations

Retrieval answers "what is here"; organization answers "how does it connect". Capillary
keeps the second answer as an append-only ledger of typed records between known sources,
so a reviewer can ask how a derived artifact traces back to the records it grew from, or
which items were revised into which.

## Relation types

| Type | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `derived-from` | the item was produced from the referenced source (assembly, summary, extraction) |
| `references` | the item cites or points at the referenced source |
| `subsumes` | the item contains the referenced source whole |
| `revised-from` | the item is a revision of the referenced source |
| `relates-to` | a general, weaker connection; used only when no stronger type fits |

## Records

```js
{ type, from, to }   // both endpoints are known source ids; self-relations are invalid
```

## Ledger soundness

A ledger is sound when every record's endpoints resolve to known sources, every type is
one of the five, no record links a source to itself, and no duplicate
`(type, from, to)` exists. The ledger is an event history:

1. **Append-only.** Records are added; existing records are never rewritten or deleted.
   Corrections arrive as new records.
2. **Small and closed.** The type set is closed; a new type is a contract decision, not
   a caller's improvisation.
3. **Ledger checks are cheap and public.** `isSoundLedger` returns every violation, so
   any consumer can audit organization without trusting the writer.

## Parent walk

`walkParentChain({ startId, parentsById, limit = 50 })` reads a supplied `Map`
from known source ids to their explicit parent ids. A known root maps to `null`.
The function returns a frozen `{ parentIds, stop, at }`. `parentIds` is frozen and
lists only resolved parents, from nearest to farthest, excluding the starting id.
The walk leaves the input map untouched.

| `stop` | `at` |
| --- | --- |
| `root` | The root id. |
| `missing` | The first missing start or parent id. |
| `cycle` | The id that would repeat. |
| `limit` | The next parent id, whose existence was left unchecked. |

`limit` can be any integer from 0 through 50. Invalid limits and malformed parent
links encountered during the walk throw `RelationError`. The walk uses only explicit
links in the map. A missing id remains missing even if other relations are available.
